title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄序
隆慶改元歲在丁卯當天下
大比士于鄉
聖天子體元正始思得奇杰之士
與天下維新海內懷忠待用
者首應
期觀光
上國誠千載一時也河南巡按
監察御史成守節受
命監臨虔弗寧處執憲矢公剔蠧
振靡視往昔加慎焉乃以前
巡按御史李文續聘至教授
子臣教諭錙䃔為考試官教
授劉一惇唐應鯨教諭梅友
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄序

隆慶改元，歲在丁卯，當天下大比士于鄉。聖天子體元正始，思得奇杰之士，與天下維新。海內懷忠待用者，首應期觀光上國，誠千載一時也。河南巡按監察御史成守節受命監臨，虔弗寧處，執憲矢公，剔蠧振靡，視往昔加慎焉。乃以前巡按御史李文續聘至教授子臣、教諭錙䃔為考試官，教授劉一惇、唐應鯨，教諭梅友
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the first year of the Longqing reign, the dingmao year [1567], the time came for the great triennial examination of scholars in the provinces throughout the realm. The sagely Son of Heaven embodied the primal principle and set the beginning aright, seeking men of exceptional talent to join in renewing all under Heaven. Throughout the empire, those who cherished loyalty and awaited employment promptly answered the appointed summons to behold the glory of the realm. Truly, this was an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years.

Cheng Shoujie, Regional Inspector for Henan and Investigating Censor, received the command to serve as Supervising Official. Reverently attentive, he allowed himself no ease. Upholding the law and pledging impartiality, he rooted out abuses and roused the dispirited, exercising even greater care than in previous examinations. He then appointed as Examiners the Confucian School Instructor Zichen [?] and the County School Instructor Zi Hong [?], who had been invited by the preceding Regional Inspector, Censor Li Wenxu [?]. The Confucian School Instructors Liu Yidun and Tang Yingjing, and the County School Instructor Mei You…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
守陸通霄陳應徵張敷潜宋
崇獻張學詩爲同考試官分
經而校簾以內罔不敬以慎
也提調則左布政使萬衣右
布政使陳典監試則按察使
李敏德僉事邵夢麟暨諸執
事咸慎選以充靖共以承簾
===
以外罔不祗以肅也合提學
副使達其道所簡士二千有
奇鎖院三試之遵
制額拔其雋八十人幷錄其文以
獻予臣猥以典役得敘諸首簡
乃進多士而告之曰夫聖主
待賢臣以弘功業而賢士亦
punctuated: 守、陸通霄、陳應徵、張敷潜、宋崇獻、張學詩爲同考試官，分經而校，簾以內罔不敬以慎也。提調則左布政使萬衣、右布政使陳典，監試則按察使李敏德、僉事邵夢麟，暨諸執事，咸慎選以充，靖共以承，簾以外罔不祗以肅也。合提學副使達其道所簡士二千有奇，鎖院三試之，遵制額拔其雋八十人，幷錄其文以獻。予臣猥以典役，得敘諸首簡，乃進多士而告之曰：「夫聖主待賢臣以弘功業，而賢士亦
translation_en:
…Mei Youshou, Lu Tongxiao, Chen Yingzheng, Zhang Fuqian, Song Chongxian, and Zhang Xueshi served as Associate Examiners, dividing the Classics among themselves for marking. Within the examination screen, all acted with respect and care. The Proctors were the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Wan Yi and the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Dian; those overseeing the examination were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Li Minde and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Shao Menglin. They and all the other functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts and discharged their duties with quiet reverence. Outside the screen, all acted with deference and solemnity.

More than two thousand candidates selected by Da Qidao, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant, were assembled. The examination compound was locked, and they were examined in three sessions. In accordance with the imperially prescribed quota, eighty of the most outstanding were selected, and their writings were also transcribed for presentation to the throne.

I, your servant, unworthily entrusted with overseeing this undertaking, have had the privilege of writing a preface for the opening pages. I therefore summoned the assembled scholars and addressed them: “An enlightened sovereign awaits worthy ministers to extend his achievements, while worthy scholars likewise…”

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
俟明主以顯其德其所脩于
家乘時而奮興者豈直爲爾
身榮侈耶孟軻氏曰有王者
興其間必有名世者信斯言
也而豈徒哉夫河洛當天地
之中會陰陽之粹賢哲代興
所從來遠矣阿衡耕莘野以
===
天民自任而堯舜之道親見
其行仲山甫于宣于蕃爲周
良翰而正己格君陳善閉邪
至今倡明道學者以程氏爲
宗前哲高風炳炳可睹也我
聖祖以
神武開基略定中原首敷文教
punctuated:
俟明主以顯其德。其所脩于家，乘時而奮興者，豈直爲爾身榮侈耶？孟軻氏曰：「有王者興，其間必有名世者。」信斯言也，而豈徒哉！夫河洛當天地之中，會陰陽之粹，賢哲代興，所從來遠矣。阿衡耕莘野，以天民自任，而堯舜之道親見其行；仲山甫于宣于蕃，爲周良翰；而正己格君，陳善閉邪，至今倡明道學者以程氏爲宗。前哲高風，炳炳可睹也。
我聖祖以神武開基，略定中原，首敷文教。
translation_en:
…await an enlightened ruler under whom to manifest their virtue. Having cultivated themselves at home, they seize the opportunity to rise to service: can this be merely for your own glory and splendor? Meng Ke said, “Should a true king arise, there would surely be someone renowned in his age.” These words are indeed true—how could they be empty talk! The region of the He and Luo rivers lies at the center of Heaven and Earth, gathering the purest energies of yin and yang. Worthies and sages have arisen here generation after generation, a tradition extending far into the past. Aheng, Yi Yin, plowed the fields of Shen, taking upon himself the responsibilities of a man of Heaven, and personally saw the Way of Yao and Shun put into practice. Zhong Shanfu served King Xuan as a bulwark [?], becoming a worthy pillar of Zhou. As for rectifying oneself to correct the ruler, setting forth what is good and shutting out what is wrong, even today those who promote and elucidate the Learning of the Way take the Cheng masters as their guiding authorities. The lofty example of these earlier sages shines clearly before our eyes.
Our sagely founding emperor established the dynasty through his divine martial prowess, subdued and pacified the Central Plain, and made the extension of literary and moral instruction his first undertaking…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承興賢育德中州人士彬
彬輩出載在名臣者可少耶
迨于
先皇壽考作人道久成化菁莪棫
樸涵濡醞釀者四十五年于
玆薄海内外家絃誦而户詩
書超越古今于斯爲盛語曰
===
人君之計惟在樹人人者一
樹而百穫者也於戲此其所
甄陶長養期望而需待之者
信非一朝夕之積矣今
皇上以天縱之聖
握符崇治
聖作物覩之時也思皇多士生此
punctuated: 列聖相承，興賢育德，中州人士彬彬輩出，載在名臣者可少耶？迨于先皇壽考，作人道久成化，菁莪棫樸，涵濡醞釀者四十五年于玆。薄海内外，家絃誦而户詩書，超越古今，于斯爲盛。語曰：「人君之計，惟在樹人。人者，一樹而百穫者也。」於戲！此其所甄陶長養、期望而需待之者，信非一朝夕之積矣！今皇上以天縱之聖，握符崇治，聖作物覩之時也。思皇多士，生此
translation_en:
…Successive sage sovereigns carried on this legacy, promoting the worthy and nurturing virtue. Cultivated men of the Central Plain emerged generation after generation: could those numbered among the celebrated ministers have been few? Then, during the late emperor’s long life, his enduring work of nurturing men brought their transformation to fruition. Like the luxuriant wormwood of “Jing E” and the flourishing trees of “Yu Pu,” they were steeped in instruction and gradually cultivated for forty-five years. Throughout the realm and beyond, to the seas, every family recited to stringed accompaniment, and every household studied the Odes and Documents. Surpassing past and present, this was an age of supreme flourishing. As the saying goes: “A ruler’s planning lies solely in cultivating men. Men are a planting that yields a hundred harvests.” Ah! The molding and nurturing bestowed upon them, the hopes placed in them, and the waiting for their service were assuredly the accumulation of far more than a single morning or evening!
Now His Majesty, with his Heaven-endowed sagacity, holds the token of sovereignty and advances good government. This is a time when “the sage arises, and all things behold him.” These admirable, numerous scholars, born in this …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
南國密邇
熈化乘奮彙征以應
龍飛景運濟濟蹌蹌挾策攄猷者
孰非
先帝之所遺哉乃縱觀士藝率多
憲經勦史搉古揚今體軌而
識洽詞茂而能裁經濟謨謀
===
如示諸掌斯爲竒杰名世章
章矣夫文以發志文華也本
實之枝葉也今於多士得見
者文耳吾懼文勝而枝葉繁
也邇者
皇上勅司文之臣崇雅黜浮刋華
斂實用忠救文藹然從先進
punctuated:
南國，密邇熈化，乘奮彙征，以應龍飛景運。濟濟蹌蹌，挾策攄猷者，孰非先帝之所遺哉？乃縱觀士藝，率多憲經勦史，搉古揚今，體軌而識洽，詞茂而能裁，經濟謨謀，如示諸掌，斯爲竒杰名世，章章矣。
夫文以發志。文，華也，本實之枝葉也。今於多士得見者，文耳。吾懼文勝而枝葉繁也。邇者，皇上勅司文之臣，崇雅黜浮，刋華斂實，用忠救文，藹然從先進
translation_en:
…in this southern land, close to the radiant influence of imperial transformation, they rise with vigor and advance together to answer the auspicious fortune of the dragon’s ascent to the throne. These numerous, dignified men, bearing their essays and unfolding their plans—who among them is not a legacy of the late emperor? Surveying the candidates’ compositions, I find that most take the Classics as their standard and draw together material from the histories, assess antiquity and elucidate the present. Their forms follow established rules, their knowledge is comprehensive, and their language is rich yet restrained. Their plans for ordering the realm and aiding the people are as clearly displayed as something held in the palm. That these are exceptional talents who will win renown in their age is manifest indeed.
Writing gives expression to aspiration. Writing is the blossom, the branches and leaves of what is rooted in substance. What I can see of these many scholars today, however, is only their writing. I fear that literary embellishment may prevail and the branches and leaves grow too luxuriant. Recently, His Majesty instructed the officials responsible for literary matters to exalt refinement and reject superficiality, prune ornament and gather substance, and use sincerity to remedy excessive embellishment, abundantly displaying a disposition to follow the men of earlier times…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
之意也爾多士對揚伊邇必
有浚明亮采之責其尚飭躬
根實仰止前脩能自任天民
之重宣力內外啓沃忠懇追
古賢哲者流耶矧
先皇所樹藝士將以貽之百穫也
則又何以辭焉允若茲豈惟
===
乃言底績將必曰隆慶改元
惟中州取士得人之盛而襃
然爲一代稱首主司者不與
有榮藉巳乎乃若言與行相
背而馳或希世獵名曲學阿
世奸利不顧其義先身圖而
後
punctuated: 之意也。爾多士對揚伊邇，必有浚明亮采之責，其尚飭躬根實，仰止前脩，能自任天民之重，宣力內外，啓沃忠懇，追古賢哲者流耶？矧先皇所樹藝士，將以貽之百穫也，則又何以辭焉？允若茲，豈惟乃言底績，將必曰：「隆慶改元，惟中州取士得人之盛，而襃然爲一代稱首。」主司者不與有榮藉巳乎？乃若言與行相背而馳，或希世獵名，曲學阿世，奸利不顧其義，先身圖而後
translation_en:
…such is his intention. You assembled scholars will soon have occasion to respond to and carry forward the imperial favor, and you will surely bear responsibility for discerning clearly and faithfully discharging your duties. May you discipline yourselves, take root in substance, and look up to worthy predecessors. Can you shoulder the weighty responsibility of being Heaven’s people, exert yourselves in service within and beyond the capital, enlighten the sovereign with loyal and earnest counsel, and follow in the footsteps of the wise and worthy of antiquity? Moreover, you are scholars whom the late emperor planted and nurtured, intending thereby to bequeath a hundredfold harvest. How, then, could you decline this responsibility? If you truly act thus, not only will your words bear fruit in achievement; people will surely say: “In the first year of Longqing, Zhongzhou’s success in selecting worthy men through the examination was so outstanding that it ranked foremost in the dynasty.” Would not those presiding over the examination also share in that honor [?]?

But if your words and deeds run contrary to one another—if you cater to prevailing tastes and hunt for fame, distort learning to flatter the age, pursue illicit gain without regard for righteousness, and put plans for yourselves first while placing afterward…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
國家之急則今日之文功利之
媒聲華之餌矣吾懼之未釋
也爾諸士載贄伊俶可不為
永終哉斯役也巡撫河南都
御史劉應節暨前任都御史
孟養性綏敎右文功弘康濟
總理河道太子少保工部尚
===
書朱衡拯世亨屯勞光底績
撫治鄖陽都御史劉秉仁威
遠寧邇乂阜民甿巡鹽御史
劉翺趙睿印馬御史顧廷對
清查御史趙岩經國裕民詰
戎勅法布政司左參政王紹
元右參政沈寅左參議朱卿
punctuated:
國家之急，則今日之文，功利之媒、聲華之餌矣。吾懼之未釋也。爾諸士載贄伊俶，可不為永終哉？
斯役也，巡撫河南都御史劉應節暨前任都御史孟養性，綏敎右文，功弘康濟；總理河道太子少保工部尚書朱衡，拯世亨屯，勞光底績；撫治鄖陽都御史劉秉仁，威遠寧邇，乂阜民甿；巡鹽御史劉翺、趙睿，印馬御史顧廷對，清查御史趙岩，經國裕民，詰戎勅法；布政司左參政王紹元、右參政沈寅、左參議朱卿、
translation_en:
…the urgent needs of the state, then the compositions written today will be mere instruments of personal gain and bait for fame. My fear of this has not yet subsided. You scholars are only now beginning to present your offerings; can you fail to strive to carry this through to the end?
In this undertaking, Liu Yingjie, Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Henan, together with Meng Yangxing, the former Censor-in-Chief, fostered education and honored literary learning, making great contributions to public well-being. Zhu Heng, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Works, charged with overall administration of the waterways, aided the realm and relieved its difficulties; his labors shone in their accomplishments. Liu Bingren, Censor-in-Chief charged with pacifying and governing Yunyang, extended his authority afar, brought peace nearby, and kept the common people orderly and prosperous. Liu Ao and Zhao Rui, Censors Inspecting the Salt Administration; Gu Tingdui, Censor Supervising Horse Branding; and Zhao Yan, Censor Conducting Investigations, administered affairs of state, enriched the people, put military affairs in order, and enforced the laws. Wang Shaoyuan, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left; Shen Yin, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right; and Zhu Qing, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left, of the Provincial Administration Commission…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
李淑按察司副使鄭伯興鮑
承蔭僉事湯彬姜國華董文
寀梁綱劉得寛都司署都指
揮僉事聶大經馬承勳于夢
孫敷政飭戎崇禮興讓而泰
寧侯陳良弼右通政王正國
都督周于德刑部郎中黃國
===
華户部主事王宇行人司行
人周以敬陳文燧各以使事
先後戾止樂觀厥成若右叅
政莫如忠先以督賦行副使
李廷龍適以履任至法得並
書云
直隸揚州府儒學教授熊子
punctuated:
李淑，按察司副使鄭伯興、鮑承蔭，僉事湯彬、姜國華、董文寀、梁綱、劉得寛，都司署都指揮僉事聶大經、馬承勳、于夢孫，敷政飭戎，崇禮興讓。而泰寧侯陳良弼、右通政王正國、都督周于德、刑部郎中黃國華、户部主事王宇、行人司行人周以敬、陳文燧，各以使事先後戾止，樂觀厥成。若右叅政莫如忠，先以督賦行；副使李廷龍，適以履任至，法得並書云。
直隸揚州府儒學教授熊子
translation_en:
…Li Shu; Zheng Boxing and Bao Chengyin, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Tang Bin, Jiang Guohua, Dong Wencai, Liang Gang, and Liu Dekuan, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners; and Nie Dajing, Ma Chengxun, and Yu Mengsun, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners in the Regional Military Commission, carried out civil administration and maintained military discipline, upheld ritual propriety, and encouraged deference. Chen Liangbi, Marquis of Taining; Wang Zhengguo, Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission; Zhou Yude, Chief Military Commissioner; Huang Guohua, Director in the Ministry of Justice; Wang Yu, Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and Zhou Yijing and Chen Wensui, Messengers in the Messenger Office, each arrived in succession on official missions and were pleased to witness the examination’s successful completion. As for Mo Ruzhong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, he had departed earlier to oversee tax collection; Li Tinglong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, happened to arrive to assume office. According to the rules, both may also be recorded here.
Xiong Zi…, Professor of the Confucian School of Yangzhou Prefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text: 臣謹序
punctuated: 臣謹序。
translation_en: …chen (completing the name Xiong Zichen) respectfully composed this preface.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
隆慶元年河南鄉試
監臨官
巡按河南監察御史成守節〔子安山東曹州籍山西太谷縣人癸丑進士〕
提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使萬衣〔章甫江西德化縣人辛丑進士〕
河南等處承宣布政使司右布政使陳典〔子厚直隸保定中衛人庚戌進士〕
監試官
河南等處提刑按察司按察使李敏德〔伯脩山西長治縣人丁未進士〕
河南等處提刑按察司僉事邵夢麟〔道徵直隸徐州人己未進士〕
===
考試官
直隸揚州府儒學教授熊子臣〔國良江西新昌縣人乙丑進士〕
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教諭鎦惔〔攻玉江西南昌縣人乙卯貢士〕
同考試官
陝西漢中府儒學教授劉一惇〔宗典四川渠縣人癸卯貢士〕
直隸池州府儒學教授唐應鯨〔子魚廣西柳州衛人乙卯貢士〕
陝西延安府綏德州米脂縣儒學教諭梅友竹〔仲節四川墊江縣人庚子貢士〕
江西九江府德化縣儒學教諭陸通霄〔汝冲湖廣江夏縣人辛酉貢士〕
浙江台州府天台縣儒學教諭陳應徵〔於亮福建閩縣人辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶元年河南鄉試

監臨官
巡按河南監察御史成守節〔子安，山東曹州籍，山西太谷縣人，癸丑進士〕。

提調官
河南等處承宣布政使司左布政使萬衣〔章甫，江西德化縣人，辛丑進士〕。
河南等處承宣布政使司右布政使陳典〔子厚，直隸保定中衛人，庚戌進士〕。

監試官
河南等處提刑按察司按察使李敏德〔伯脩，山西長治縣人，丁未進士〕。
河南等處提刑按察司僉事邵夢麟〔道徵，直隸徐州人，己未進士〕。

考試官
直隸揚州府儒學教授熊子臣〔國良，江西新昌縣人，乙丑進士〕。
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教諭鎦惔〔攻玉，江西南昌縣人，乙卯貢士〕。

同考試官
陝西漢中府儒學教授劉一惇〔宗典，四川渠縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
直隸池州府儒學教授唐應鯨〔子魚，廣西柳州衛人，乙卯貢士〕。
陝西延安府綏德州米脂縣儒學教諭梅友竹〔仲節，四川墊江縣人，庚子貢士〕。
江西九江府德化縣儒學教諭陸通霄〔汝冲，湖廣江夏縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
浙江台州府天台縣儒學教諭陳應徵〔於亮，福建閩縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Henan Provincial Examination, First Year of Longqing (1567)

Supervising Official
Cheng Shoujie, Investigating Censor assigned to巡 inspect Henan. His courtesy name was Zi’an; he was registered in Caozhou, Shandong, and was a native of Taigu County, Shanxi. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the guichou year.

Proctors
Wan Yi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name was Zhangfu; he was a native of Dehua County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the xinchou year.
Chen Dian, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name was Zihou; he was from Baoding Central Guard, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.

Examination Supervisors
Li Minde, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name was Boxiu; he was a native of Changzhi County, Shanxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.
Shao Menglin, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Henan. His courtesy name was Daozheng; he was a native of Xuzhou, Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.

Examiners
Xiong Zichen, Professor at the Confucian School of Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Guoliang; he was a native of Xinchang County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.
Liu Tan 鎦惔, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wuyi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Gongyu; he was a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and became a tribute student (gongshi) in the yimao year.

Associate Examiners
Liu Yidun, Professor at the Confucian School of Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi. His courtesy name was Zongdian; he was a native of Qu County, Sichuan, and became a tribute student in the guimao year.
Tang Yingjing, Professor at the Confucian School of Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he was from Liuzhou Guard, Guangxi, and became a tribute student in the yimao year.
Mei Youzhu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Mizhi County, Suide Subprefecture, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. His courtesy name was Zhongjie; he was a native of Dianjiang County, Sichuan, and became a tribute student in the gengzi year.
Lu Tongxiao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Dehua County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Ruchong; he was a native of Jiangxia County, Huguang, and became a tribute student in the xinyou year.
Chen Yingzheng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Tiantai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Yuliang; he was a native of Min County, Fujian, and became a tribute student in the xinyou year.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
湖廣武昌府崇陽縣儒學敎諭張敷潜〔存昭福建晉江縣人壬子貢士〕
山西平陽府蒲縣儒學敎諭宋崇獻〔汝徵武功中衛籍山東武定州人辛酉貢士〕

===

開封府通判吳鳳瑞〔舜徵，湖廣蘄州人，乙卯貢士〕。河南府推官李鳴謙〔德卿，直隸桐城縣人，乙丑進士〕。開封府許州知州甯𨥉〔大受，直隸廣德州人，乙丑進士〕。汝寧府信陽州知州葉朝陽〔文楨，浙江秀水縣籍，嘉善縣人，乙丑進士〕。汝寧府光州光山縣知縣丁懋儒〔聘卿，山東聊城縣人，乙丑進士〕。
translation_en:

Gu Zhengtai, Registrar in the Registry of the Henan Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Zhongshu and was from Huating County, Zhili. He was a student of the Imperial University.

Zhang Dahe, Prefect of Henan, had the courtesy name Yuande. He held official-household registration with the Jinyiwei (Embroidered-uniform Guard) in Zhili and was originally from Yangxin County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingchen year.

Chen Yinglin, Prefect of Zhangde, had the courtesy name Renqing. He was registered with the Jinyiwei and was originally from Yin County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.

Officials Responsible for Receiving Examination Scripts

Wu Fengrui, Assistant Prefect of Kaifeng, had the courtesy name Shunzheng and was from Qizhou, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the yimao year.

Li Mingqian, Prefectural Judge of Henan, had the courtesy name Deqing and was from Tongcheng County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.

Ye Chaoyang, Subprefect of Xinyang in Runing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Wenzhen. He was registered in Xiushui County, Zhejiang, and was originally from Jiashan County. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.

Ding Maoru, Magistrate of Guangshan County, Guangzhou Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Pinqing and was from Liaocheng County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.

translation_en:

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
爲君難爲臣不易
脩身也尊賢也親親也
盡其心者知其性也知其性則知天矣
易
飛龍在天乃位乎天德
彖曰萃聚也順以說剛中而應故聚也王
假有廟致孝享也利見大人亨聚以正
===
也用大牲吉利有攸往順天命也觀其
所聚而天地萬物之情可見矣
成性存存道義之門
雨以潤之日以晅之
書
允若兹嘉言罔攸伏野無遺賢萬邦咸寧
今王嗣厥德罔不在初
謀及乃心謀及卿士謀及庶人謀及卜筮
汝則從龜從筮從卿士從庶民從是之
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
爲君難，爲臣不易。
脩身也，尊賢也，親親也。
盡其心者，知其性也；知其性，則知天矣。

易
飛龍在天，乃位乎天德。
彖曰：「萃，聚也。順以說，剛中而應，故聚也。王假有廟，致孝享也。利見大人亨，聚以正也。用大牲吉，利有攸往，順天命也。觀其所聚，而天地萬物之情可見矣。」
成性存存，道義之門。
雨以潤之，日以晅之。

書
允若兹，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。
今王嗣厥德，罔不在初。
謀及乃心，謀及卿士，謀及庶人，謀及卜筮。汝則從，龜從，筮從，卿士從，庶民從，是之
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
“To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy.”
“Cultivating oneself, honoring the worthy, and treating one’s relatives with affection.”
“Those who fully realize their hearts know their nature. Knowing their nature, they know Heaven.”

Book of Changes (Yijing)
“‘A flying dragon in heaven’: he thus occupies a position of heavenly virtue.”
“The Commentary on the Judgment says: ‘Cui means gathering. Compliant and joyful, with the firm occupying the central position and receiving a response: hence gathering. “The king approaches his ancestral temple” means bringing filial offerings to their fullest expression. “It is beneficial to see the great man; success” means gathering in accordance with what is right. “Using a large sacrificial animal brings good fortune; it is beneficial to have somewhere to go” means following Heaven’s mandate. By observing what gathers together, one can discern the true circumstances of heaven, earth, and the myriad things.’”
“Preserving continually one’s fully formed nature is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.”
“Rain moistens them; the sun dries them.”

Book of Documents (Shujing)
“If it is truly thus, no good counsel will remain concealed, no worthy person in the countryside will be overlooked, and the myriad states will all be at peace.”
“Now that you, O King, inherit his virtue, everything depends upon the beginning.”
“Consult your own heart; consult the ministers and officers; consult the common people; consult the tortoise shell and milfoil stalks. If you assent, the tortoise shell assents, the milfoil stalks assent, the ministers and officers assent, and the common people assent, this is …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
謂大同身其康彊子孫其逢吉
則亦有熊羆之士不二心之臣保乂王家
詩
蠶月條桑取彼斧斨以伐遠揚猗彼女桑
七月鳴鵙八月載績
夜如何其夜未央庭燎之光君子至止鸞
聲將將夜如何其夜未艾庭燎晣晣君
子至止鸞聲噦噦夜如何其夜鄉晨庭
燎有煇君子至止言觀其旂
===
無念爾祖聿脩厥德
允也天子降于卿士實維阿衡實左右商
王
春秋
元年隱公元年春公會戎于潜隱公二年
諸侯遂圍許僖公二十有八年
晉侯伐鄭宣公十有四年
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈季孫斯仲孫何忌
帥師墮費十有二月公圍成公至自
punctuated:
謂大同，身其康彊，子孫其逢吉。則亦有熊羆之士、不二心之臣，保乂王家。
詩
蠶月條桑，取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚，猗彼女桑。七月鳴鵙，八月載績。
夜如何其？夜未央，庭燎之光。君子至止，鸞聲將將。夜如何其？夜未艾，庭燎晣晣。君子至止，鸞聲噦噦。夜如何其？夜鄉晨，庭燎有煇。君子至止，言觀其旂。
無念爾祖，聿脩厥德。
允也天子，降于卿士。實維阿衡，實左右商王。
春秋
元年。隱公元年。春，公會戎于潜。隱公二年。
諸侯遂圍許。僖公二十有八年。
晉侯伐鄭。宣公十有四年。
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈，季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。十有二月，公圍成。公至自
translation_en:
…is called great concord. You yourself will enjoy health and strength, and your descendants will meet with good fortune. Then there will also be warriors fierce as bears and ministers of undivided loyalty to protect and govern the royal house.

Book of Odes (Shijing)

In the silkworm month, we prune the mulberries. We take those axes and hatchets to cut away the high-reaching branches and bend down the young mulberries. In the seventh month the shrike calls; in the eighth month we begin spinning hemp.

How goes the night? The night is not yet halfway through; the courtyard torches shine. The noble lords arrive, their carriage bells jingling. How goes the night? The night is not yet over; the courtyard torches blaze brightly. The noble lords arrive, their carriage bells chiming. How goes the night? The night approaches dawn; the courtyard torches give off a glow. The noble lords arrive; we look upon their banners.

Will you not remember your ancestor and cultivate his virtue?

Truly, the Son of Heaven entrusted affairs to his high ministers. It was the Aheng, the chief minister, who aided the king of Shang.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

“The first year.” First year of Duke Yin. “In spring, the duke met with the Rong at Qian.” Second year of Duke Yin.

“The lords thereupon besieged Xu.” Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.

“The marquis of Jin attacked Zheng.” Fourteenth year of Duke Xuan.

Shusun Zhouchou led an army to demolish the fortifications of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the fortifications of Fei. In the twelfth month, the duke besieged Cheng. The duke returned from…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
圍成俱定公十有二年
禮記
君入門介拂闈大夫中棖與闈之間士介
拂棖
律小大之稱比終始之序以象事行
禮之於正國也猶衡之於輕重也繩墨之
於曲直也規矩之於方圜也
故君子與其使食浮於人也寧使人浮於
食
===
第貳場
論
孔子太和元氣
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔建元
元年
擬唐以張九齡爲中書令誥開元二十二
年
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表元祐元
punctuated:
圍成。俱定公十有二年。
禮記
君入門，介拂闈；大夫中棖與闈之間；士介拂棖。
律小大之稱，比終始之序，以象事行。
禮之於正國也，猶衡之於輕重也，繩墨之於曲直也，規矩之於方圜也。
故君子與其使食浮於人也，寧使人浮於食。
第貳場
論
孔子太和元氣。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔，建元元年。
擬唐以張九齡爲中書令誥，開元二十二年。
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表，元祐元
translation_en:
…the siege of Cheng. All these passages are from the twelfth year of Duke Ding.

Book of Rites
When a ruler enters the gate, his attendant brushes against the small central door; a grand master passes midway between the doorpost and the central door; a serviceman’s attendant brushes against the doorpost.
Regulate the appropriate proportions of greater and lesser tones, and arrange their sequence from beginning to end, to represent the conduct of affairs.
Ritual, in setting a state aright, is like a balance in determining weight, an inked line in determining straightness and crookedness, and compasses and a square in determining squareness and roundness.
Thus the gentleman would rather have the number of people exceed the provisions than have the provisions exceed the number of people.

Second Session
Discourse
Confucius as the primordial vital force of supreme harmony.

One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Draft an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty calling for the recommendation of worthy, upright men who would speak frankly and remonstrate to the utmost: Jianyuan 1.
Draft a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Zhang Jiuling Director of the Secretariat: Kaiyuan 22.
Draft a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for the appointment of Cheng Yi as Lecturer in Chongzheng Hall: Yuanyou 1…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
年
判語五條
官吏給由
賦役不均
鄉飲酒禮
優恤軍屬
脩理倉庫
第叄場
策五道
===
問帝王之統天御極也有厚德深仁以敷
被當時天下尊而親之有聖訓神謨以
佑啓來裔天下頌而戴之然莫為之後
雖盛弗傳體先以達孝成德以廣仁又
在善繼述者之所繹思於不匱也洪惟
世宗肅皇帝以
上聖之德紹
列聖之統久道孚化巍然
成功煥然
punctuated:
年。
判語五條：官吏給由、賦役不均、鄉飲酒禮、優恤軍屬、脩理倉庫。
第叄場，策五道。
問：帝王之統天御極也，有厚德深仁以敷被當時，天下尊而親之；有聖訓神謨以佑啓來裔，天下頌而戴之。然莫為之後，雖盛弗傳。體先以達孝，成德以廣仁，又在善繼述者之所繹思於不匱也。洪惟世宗肅皇帝，以上聖之德，紹列聖之統，久道孚化，巍然成功，煥然
translation_en:
…year.
Five legal judgments: issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks; unequal taxation and labor-service obligations; the village drinking ceremony; preferential relief for military dependents; repairing granaries and storehouses.
Third Session: Five Policy Questions.
Question: When emperors and kings assume Heaven’s authority and occupy the supreme position, their abundant virtue and profound benevolence extend over their age, and all under Heaven revere and cherish them. Their sagely instructions and divine counsels protect and guide their descendants, and all under Heaven praise and uphold them. Yet without successors to carry on their work, even flourishing achievements will not endure. To embody the intentions of one’s forebears and thereby fulfill filial piety, and to perfect virtue and thereby extend benevolence—these, too, require inexhaustible reflection from those who would skillfully continue and develop their predecessors’ work.
We reverently reflect that Emperor Shizong Su, with the virtue of a supreme sage, succeeded to the imperial line of the preceding sage rulers. Through long constancy in the Way, he won trust and brought about moral transformation. Lofty were his accomplishments, radiant…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
文章爲天下所
尊親者殆難殫紀邇者
遺詔一頒追惟往事拳拳望
皇上以守成之道眞湯之自責武之貽謀其視
漢文之遺詔武帝之自悔有不足言矣
天下臣民聞者莫不感涕非
聖人而能若是乎我
皇上嗣登大寶克承
先德如錄用諫臣開言路也明正刑章禁邪術
===
也停止採買恤民隱也躬親
郊廟復典禮也其餘推類以盡義通變以宜時
莫非善繼善述之事所得於快覩傳聞
者可備舉以對揚之歟夫
勵精初政咸稱盛美矣謹始愼終之道正本
澄源之學不知今以何者爲要急歟爾
多士爲時黎獻懷共臣之念久矣其亦
有能從容推本以賛
聖政於萬一者乎幸詳著于篇行將採之以
punctuated: 文章，爲天下所尊親者，殆難殫紀。邇者，遺詔一頒，追惟往事，拳拳望皇上以守成之道，眞湯之自責、武之貽謀，其視漢文之遺詔、武帝之自悔，有不足言矣。天下臣民聞者，莫不感涕，非聖人而能若是乎？我皇上嗣登大寶，克承先德，如錄用諫臣，開言路也；明正刑章，禁邪術也；停止採買，恤民隱也；躬親郊廟，復典禮也。其餘推類以盡義，通變以宜時，莫非善繼善述之事。所得於快覩傳聞者，可備舉以對揚之歟？夫勵精初政，咸稱盛美矣。謹始愼終之道，正本澄源之學，不知今以何者爲要急歟？爾多士，爲時黎獻，懷共臣之念久矣，其亦有能從容推本，以賛聖政於萬一者乎？幸詳著于篇，行將採之以
translation_en:
…his splendid cultural accomplishments—the things for which he was revered and held dear throughout the realm can scarcely be fully recorded. Recently, when his testamentary edict was promulgated, he reflected upon past affairs and earnestly charged His Majesty with the way of preserving the inherited achievement. This was truly like Tang’s self-reproach and King Wu’s provision of plans for his successors. Compared with it, the testamentary edict of Emperor Wen of Han and Emperor Wu’s expression of remorse scarcely merit mention. Among the officials and people throughout the realm who heard it, none failed to be moved to tears. Could anyone but a sage have acted thus?

Our emperor has succeeded to the imperial throne and ably carried forward his predecessor’s virtue. For example, he has appointed remonstrating officials, opening channels for frank counsel; clarified and rectified penal statutes, prohibiting heterodox arts; halted procurement, showing concern for the people’s unspoken sufferings; and personally attended the suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple, restoring the prescribed rites. His other acts extend these principles by analogy to fulfill what is right and adapt to change to suit the times: all exemplify skill in continuing his predecessor’s work and carrying out his intentions. Can you enumerate fully what you have had the pleasure of witnessing or have learned through reports, so as to acknowledge and extol these achievements?

All acclaim the magnificence of his diligent efforts at the outset of his reign. Yet, concerning the way of being careful at the beginning and mindful at the end, and the learning that rectifies the root and clears the source, what should now be regarded as most urgent? You assembled scholars are the worthy men of this age and have long cherished the aspiration to serve as reverent ministers [?]. Are there any among you who can calmly trace matters to their foundations and thereby contribute even the smallest measure to our sage sovereign’s governance? Please set forth your views fully in writing; we shall shortly select from them in order to…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
獻于
上
問君心唯在所養所以輔養君心者莫大
于講學今之
經筵進講是也稽古守成業而致盛治者莫
如周成王其所以成德則由乎諸臣之
夾輔涵養薰陶之道具在詩書周禮可
攷而知之與自漢而下銳志於學代不
乏君有講論於石渠虎觀者有講論於
===
弘文延英者有講論於邇英崇政者然
竟未見其以令主稱而治終不古若何
與迨我
太祖高皇帝
聖神文武超邁百王乃於
萬幾時暇即與輔臣講究經史如
御華蓋殿論易
武英殿論書
左閣論宋史隨
punctuated:
獻于上。

問：君心唯在所養，所以輔養君心者莫大于講學，今之經筵進講是也。稽古，守成業而致盛治者，莫如周成王。其所以成德，則由乎諸臣之夾輔，涵養薰陶之道，具在《詩》《書》《周禮》，可攷而知之與？自漢而下，銳志於學，代不乏君。有講論於石渠、虎觀者，有講論於弘文、延英者，有講論於邇英、崇政者，然竟未見其以令主稱，而治終不古若，何與？迨我太祖高皇帝，聖神文武，超邁百王，乃於萬幾時暇，即與輔臣講究經史，如御華蓋殿論《易》，武英殿論《書》，左閣論《宋史》，隨
translation_en:
…to present to His Majesty.

Question: The ruler’s mind depends upon how it is nurtured. Nothing is more important in assisting and nurturing the ruler’s mind than lectures and study; today’s lectures at the Classics Colloquium serve this purpose. Looking back into antiquity, none equaled King Cheng of Zhou in preserving his inherited achievements and bringing about flourishing government. That he perfected his virtue was due to the assistance of his ministers. The ways in which they nurtured and cultivated him are fully recorded in the Book of Odes, the Book of Documents, and the Rites of Zhou. Can these be examined to ascertain those methods? From the Han onward, no dynasty lacked rulers earnestly devoted to learning. Some held learned discussions at Shiqu and Huguan, others at Hongwen and Yanying, and still others at Erying and Chongzheng. Yet we do not find that they ultimately won renown as excellent rulers, and their government never matched that of antiquity. Why was this?

When our Emperor Taizu Gao arose, his sageliness and spiritual insight, his civil and martial accomplishments, surpassed those of the hundred kings. Yet whenever he had leisure amid the myriad affairs of government, he would investigate the classics and histories with his assisting ministers: for example, he discussed the Book of Changes while at Huagai Hall, the Book of Documents at Wuying Hall, and the History of the Song at the Left Pavilion. Wherever…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
幸輒講初無常所也至正統初年著爲禮儀
定式講學
御於文華
列聖承而因之今我
皇上
仁孝天植
學問夙成勤
視朝之典復
面奏之規至於
===
===
御經筵開日講又惓惓不致後焉此帝王兢業
之心元后緝熈之學生靈長久之慶
宗社無疆之福也然
大明會典載講書之後凡遇五府軍政六部要
務俾詹事等官詳悉敷陳則講讀之地
有都俞吁咈之風
今日可兼而復之耶昔宋儒之在經筵有畫
書無逸爲圖以進者有必欲以所言感
悟人主者有反覆開道覬有所啓悟者
punctuated:
幸輒講，初無常所也。至正統初年，著爲禮儀定式，講學御於文華。列聖承而因之。今我皇上仁孝天植，學問夙成，勤視朝之典，復面奏之規。至於御經筵，開日講，又惓惓不致後焉。此帝王兢業之心，元后緝熈之學，生靈長久之慶，宗社無疆之福也。
然《大明會典》載，講書之後，凡遇五府軍政、六部要務，俾詹事等官詳悉敷陳，則講讀之地有都俞吁咈之風。今日可兼而復之耶？昔宋儒之在經筵，有畫《書》〈無逸〉爲圖以進者，有必欲以所言感悟人主者，有反覆開道覬有所啓悟者，
translation_en:
…wherever he went, lectures were held; initially there was no fixed venue. In the early years of the Zhengtong reign, this was codified as a regular ceremonial procedure, with the emperor attending lectures at Wenhua Hall. Successive sage emperors inherited and continued this practice. Our present Emperor is endowed by Heaven with benevolence and filial devotion, and attained learning early in life. He diligently observes the rites of court audiences and has restored the procedure for presenting reports in person. As for attending the Classics Colloquium and instituting daily lectures, he has likewise shown unstinting concern and has not allowed these to fall behind. Here are the vigilant diligence of an emperor and the sovereign’s learning that continually advances toward enlightenment: a lasting blessing for the people and boundless good fortune for the ancestral temples and the altars of state.
Yet the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming records that, after lectures on the texts, whenever there were military affairs of the Five Chief Military Commissions or important business of the Six Ministries, officials such as the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent were instructed to explain these matters fully and in detail. Thus the place of lectures and readings possessed the spirit of frank exchange, with assent and dissent freely expressed. Could this practice also be restored today? Among the Song Confucian scholars who served at the Classics Colloquium, some illustrated the “Against Ease” chapter of the Book of Documents in a chart and presented it; some were determined through their words to move and awaken their ruler; and some repeatedly offered instruction and guidance, hoping to bring him to understanding…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
有進講莊嚴每繼以諷諫者今能無有
進於是與諸士際遇
明時咸願觀國之光也請颺言之以爲
國家之盛
問立人之道曰仁與義大梁之墟自孟軻
氏不遠千里而來首舉仁義以啓迪惠
王者其由來舊矣試以仁義之說相與
質之鄒孟七篇雖云詳說仁義矣然求
其大旨惟仁人心也義人路也二言示
===
人最爲切要初未嘗名言其體用爲何
如至朱子訓解則曰仁者心之德愛之
理義者心之制事之宜始該體用而形
容之先儒以爲有功於學者求於七篇
之中何者爲似其說耶仁包四德孔門
專言夫仁孟子則兼義而對言之豈以
仁義爲性之體用二者初未嘗相離與
抑以戰國之時性學不明孟氏有所爲
而别言之與原道之篇以博愛謂仁行
punctuated:
有進講莊嚴，每繼以諷諫者。今能無有進於是與？諸士際遇明時，咸願觀國之光也，請颺言之，以爲國家之盛。

問：立人之道曰仁與義。大梁之墟，自孟軻氏不遠千里而來，首舉仁義以啓迪惠王者，其由來舊矣。試以仁義之說相與質之。鄒孟七篇雖云詳說仁義矣，然求其大旨，惟「仁，人心也；義，人路也」二言，示人最爲切要。初未嘗名言其體用爲何如。至朱子訓解，則曰：「仁者，心之德，愛之理；義者，心之制，事之宜。」始該體用而形容之，先儒以爲有功於學者。求於七篇之中，何者爲似其說耶？仁包四德，孔門專言夫仁，孟子則兼義而對言之，豈以仁義爲性之體用，二者初未嘗相離與？抑以戰國之時性學不明，孟氏有所爲而别言之與？《原道》之篇以博愛謂仁，行
translation_en:
…Some delivered their lectures with solemn dignity, regularly following them with indirect remonstrance. Can we now make no further advance beyond this? You scholars have the good fortune to live in an enlightened age, and all wish to behold the glory of the realm. Please set forth your views openly, contributing to the flourishing of the state.

Question: “The Way of establishing humanity is called benevolence and righteousness.” Here at the site of Daliang, this teaching has a long history, reaching back to when Meng Ke thought a thousand li no great distance to travel and, upon arriving, first invoked benevolence and righteousness to enlighten King Hui. Let us examine together the teachings concerning benevolence and righteousness. Although the seven books of Mengzi, the Master Meng of Zou, discuss them in detail, if we seek their central purport, the two statements “Benevolence is the human heart; righteousness is the human path” offer the most direct and essential guidance. Yet they never explicitly state what their substance and function are. Only with Master Zhu’s explanatory commentary—“Benevolence is the virtue of the heart and the principle of love; righteousness is the heart’s regulation and what is fitting in affairs”—were substance and function both encompassed and described. Earlier Confucian scholars considered this a valuable contribution for learners. Looking within the seven books, which passages accord with his explanation? Benevolence embraces the four virtues, and the school of Confucius speaks specifically of benevolence, whereas Mengzi also invokes righteousness and discusses the two as a pair. Is this because benevolence and righteousness constitute the substance and function of human nature, and the two have never been separate? Or was it because learning concerning human nature was obscure in the Warring States period, and Master Meng had a particular purpose in distinguishing them? The essay On the Way defines universal love as benevolence, and acting…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
而宜之謂義程門固甞非之周子則以
愛曰仁宜曰義似與原道同也何周之
言是而韓之說非與孟子說仁義禮智
則在第二太極圖以義配利則在第三
抑果各有其說與仁是柔合屬陰也何
以屬陽義是剛合屬陽也何以屬陰禮
配夫亨於時爲夏也何以爲仁之著智
配夫貞於時爲冬也何以爲義之藏先
儒皆論之備矣果可得而發明之與凡
===
此皆諸士所習聞而誦說之者也盍究
言之以覘所性之蘊
問三代而下稱漢治烝烝近古蓋以守令
者吏民之本也史稱河南守吳公治平
爲天下第一今吳公之行載籍無所見
如京兆南陽潁川渤海皆以治行稱可
並舉而言之與唐法不刺史不得任侍
郎不郡縣不得任臺省是以冀州瀛州
滄州武陽昌邑至今言吏治者歸焉然
punctuated:
而宜之謂義，程門固甞非之。周子則以愛曰仁，宜曰義，似與《原道》同也。何周之言是，而韓之說非與？孟子說仁義禮智，則在第二；《太極圖》以義配利，則在第三。抑果各有其說與？仁是柔，合屬陰也，何以屬陽？義是剛，合屬陽也，何以屬陰？禮配夫亨，於時爲夏也，何以爲仁之著？智配夫貞，於時爲冬也，何以爲義之藏？先儒皆論之備矣，果可得而發明之與？凡此皆諸士所習聞而誦說之者也，盍究言之，以覘所性之蘊？
問：三代而下，稱漢治烝烝近古，蓋以守令者吏民之本也。史稱河南守吳公治平爲天下第一。今吳公之行，載籍無所見。如京兆、南陽、潁川、渤海，皆以治行稱，可並舉而言之與？唐法，不刺史不得任侍郎，不郡縣不得任臺省。是以冀州、瀛州、滄州、武陽、昌邑，至今言吏治者歸焉。然
translation_en:
…and acting in accordance with what is fitting is called righteousness: the Cheng school indeed once criticized this formulation. Yet Master Zhou said that love is called benevolence and fittingness is called righteousness, which seems identical to the formulation in An Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao). Why, then, is Zhou’s statement correct and Han’s explanation wrong? In Mengzi’s enumeration of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, righteousness comes second; in the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu), righteousness is paired with benefit (li) and comes third. Does each arrangement indeed have its own explanation? Benevolence is yielding and ought to belong to yin: why does it belong to yang? Righteousness is firm and ought to belong to yang: why does it belong to yin? Ritual propriety corresponds to flourishing (heng), and among the seasons to summer: why is it the manifestation of benevolence? Wisdom corresponds to constancy (zhen), and among the seasons to winter: why is it the storing away of righteousness? Earlier Confucian scholars have discussed all these matters fully. Can you indeed elucidate them? All these are matters you gentlemen have often heard and recited explanations of. Why not discuss them exhaustively, so that we may discern the depths of your inherent nature?
Question: Of the periods since the Three Dynasties, Han government is praised as having advanced steadily toward the ways of antiquity, for commandery governors and county magistrates are the foundation of administration and the people’s well-being. The histories call the orderly government of Lord Wu, Governor of Henan, the finest in the empire. Yet accounts of Lord Wu’s conduct are nowhere to be found in the surviving records. The administrators of Jingzhao, Nanyang, Yingchuan, and Bohai were all renowned for their administrative achievements: can you enumerate and discuss them together? Under Tang regulations, no one could become a Vice Minister without having served as a Prefect, or hold office in the central censorial and ministerial agencies without having served in commandery or county administration. Thus, even today, those who discuss good administration turn to the examples of Jizhou, Yingzhou, Cangzhou, Wuyang, and Changyi. Yet…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
其間亦有以偽增戶口而受賞以政拙
催科而被抑豈覈實之道有未盡歟我
祖宗設官分職守令之選尤重今
天子御極嘉惠元元
特下
明詔首飭吏治一時長吏爭自濯磨喁喁嚮風
突然人才難得賢不肖殊科豈無飭實
眩名盜隆虛譽者茲欲求吏治如吳公
輩以稱我
===
皇上重本之意不知吳公者何如人也抑何施
而得此耶今之議者必曰久任必曰超
陟不知其法果可行於今與抑別有其
說歟爾諸士行有民社之寄幸悉言之
以觀用世之學
問黃河之患所從來遠矣古稱神禹治水
封山濬川任土作貢萬世永賴今考其
行水之法載在史籍不知亦可行于今
與先儒論古今治河者莫如賈讓之三
punctuated:
其間亦有以偽增戶口而受賞，以政拙催科而被抑，豈覈實之道有未盡歟？我祖宗設官分職，守令之選尤重。今天子御極，嘉惠元元，特下明詔，首飭吏治。一時長吏爭自濯磨，喁喁嚮風。突然人才難得，賢不肖殊科，豈無飭實眩名、盜隆虛譽者？茲欲求吏治如吳公輩，以稱我皇上重本之意，不知吳公者何如人也？抑何施而得此耶？今之議者必曰久任，必曰超陟，不知其法果可行於今與？抑別有其說歟？爾諸士行有民社之寄，幸悉言之，以觀用世之學。
問：黃河之患，所從來遠矣。古稱神禹治水，封山濬川，任土作貢，萬世永賴。今考其行水之法，載在史籍，不知亦可行于今與？先儒論古今治河者，莫如賈讓之三
translation_en:
…among them there were also those rewarded for falsely inflating household and population figures, and those held back because their administration was inept at collecting taxes. Could the methods of verifying actual performance have been less than exhaustive? Our imperial ancestors established offices and apportioned duties, placing particular weight on the selection of prefects and county magistrates. Now the Son of Heaven has ascended the throne and bestowed his beneficence upon the common people. He has specially issued an illustrious edict giving first priority to rectifying local administration. At once, the chief local officials vied to cleanse and improve themselves, eagerly looking to his example. Yet [?] talented men are hard to find, and the worthy and unworthy belong to different categories. Surely there are some who embellish their actual performance and dazzle others with their names [?], fraudulently building up empty reputations? We now wish to obtain administrators like Master Wu (Wu Gong), to fulfill our emperor’s intention of giving weight to the foundations of government. What sort of man was Master Wu? What measures did he implement to achieve such results? Those discussing the matter today invariably advocate long tenure in office and exceptional promotion. Can these methods indeed be put into practice today? Or is there another explanation? You scholars will soon be entrusted with the people and the local altars of soil and grain. Please discuss this fully, so that we may assess your learning for service in the world.
Question: The troubles caused by the Yellow River have a long history. It was said in antiquity that the divine Yu brought the waters under control, marked out the mountains, dredged the rivers, and assessed tribute according to the capacities of the soil, conferring lasting benefits upon all subsequent generations. If we now examine his methods of directing the waters, as recorded in historical writings, can they also be put into practice today? Earlier Confucian scholars, discussing river management in antiquity and later times, held that nothing surpassed Jia Rang’s three…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
策而所以用其策者又莫出於賈魯之
三法焉不知亦有合于禹治水之道否
也今之時勢果皆鑿鑿可行與我
國家建都上游東南財賦皆仰給于漕運然
二洪梗澁必資河流頃因雨水溢決于徐
之飛雲浦逆流而上淤沙百餘里
先帝憂之
特遣大臣別治新河比有成績矣乃議者又以
萬里轉折東下之勢而乘之以雨水交
===
發百川灌集之威出之以秦溝一股其
勢必至於衝溢欲於上流開支河以殺
其勢不知其說然乎夫下流不濬則上
流必壅况末流巨匯勢逼
皇陵全河北徙則曹武金單皆爲巨浸也不又
可深慮耶玆欲有濟漕之利而無墊溺
之憂執畫一之策而不惑於紛紛之議
必如何而後可試詳言之毋讓
punctuated: 策，而所以用其策者，又莫出於賈魯之三法焉。不知亦有合于禹治水之道否也？今之時勢，果皆鑿鑿可行與？我國家建都上游，東南財賦皆仰給于漕運。然二洪梗澁，必資河流。頃因雨水溢決于徐之飛雲浦，逆流而上，淤沙百餘里。先帝憂之，特遣大臣別治新河，比有成績矣。乃議者又以萬里轉折東下之勢，而乘之以雨水交發、百川灌集之威，出之以秦溝一股，其勢必至於衝溢，欲於上流開支河以殺其勢。不知其說然乎？夫下流不濬，則上流必壅。况末流巨匯，勢逼皇陵，全河北徙，則曹、武、金、單皆爲巨浸也，不又可深慮耶？玆欲有濟漕之利，而無墊溺之憂，執畫一之策，而不惑於紛紛之議，必如何而後可？試詳言之，毋讓。
translation_en: …policies; and for putting those policies into practice, nothing surpasses Jia Lu’s three methods. Do these also accord with Yu’s way of controlling the waters? Given present circumstances, are they all indeed practicable? Our dynasty established its capital upstream, and its supplies of tax revenue and goods from the southeast depend entirely on grain transport by water. Yet passage through the two rapids is obstructed and difficult, and necessarily depends on the river’s flow. Recently, rainwater caused the river to overflow and breach its banks at Feiyunpu in Xu; the water backed upstream, depositing silt for more than a hundred li. Concerned about this, the late emperor specially dispatched high officials to construct a separate new channel, and results have lately been achieved. Yet some now argue that the river’s momentum as it winds eastward over ten thousand li, intensified by simultaneous rainfall and the force of a hundred converging streams, must cause destructive overflow if discharged through the single channel at Qingou. They therefore wish to open a branch channel upstream to reduce its force. Is their argument sound? If the lower reaches are not dredged, the upper reaches will inevitably become blocked. Moreover, the great accumulation of water at the river’s end threatens the imperial tombs. If the entire river shifts northward, Cao, Wu, Jin, and Shan will all become a vast inundated expanse. Is this not also cause for grave concern? We now wish to secure the benefits of facilitating grain transport without the danger of inundation and drowning, and to adopt a consistent policy without being bewildered by conflicting proposals. What must be done to achieve this? Explain in detail, without reserve.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
爲君難爲臣不易
同考試官教諭張批格局嚴整詞彩精明入講
處句句不脱難字尤爲完密而一結歸重君身上尤
見責難之意
同考試官教諭張批發明難與不易處精切懇
到瑩潔圓融而通篇貫講皆不外天命人心之意非
===
素有定見者不能至此
考試官教諭鎦批格調渾雄詞氣簡古於凡
時義之冗鑿似滌洗是能力去浮靡敦崇大雅者
考試官教授熊批見理明切屬詞嚴整而純
粹之學俊逸之才精一之思具見此作
論君臣之責而盡之皆惟其艱也蓋君臣均以
天下爲任責至重也知其重而思以盡之不亦
艱哉昔夫子告定公之意蓋謂王道本無近功
人言亦有至理君欲興邦也盍於人言觀之乎
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

爲君難，爲臣不易。

同考試官教諭張批：格局嚴整，詞彩精明，入講處句句不脱難字，尤爲完密；而一結歸重君身上，尤見責難之意。

同考試官教諭張批：發明難與不易處，精切懇到，瑩潔圓融；而通篇貫講，皆不外天命人心之意，非素有定見者不能至此。

考試官教諭鎦批：格調渾雄，詞氣簡古，於凡時義之冗鑿似滌洗，是能力去浮靡、敦崇大雅者。

考試官教授熊批：見理明切，屬詞嚴整，而純粹之學、俊逸之才、精一之思，具見此作。

論君臣之責而盡之，皆惟其艱也。蓋君臣均以天下爲任，責至重也。知其重而思以盡之，不亦艱哉？昔夫子告定公之意，蓋謂王道本無近功，人言亦有至理。君欲興邦也，盍於人言觀之乎？
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The structure is rigorous and orderly, and the diction polished and lucid. In the opening exposition, every sentence holds closely to the word “difficult,” making the treatment particularly thorough and cohesive. The conclusion places the chief responsibility upon the ruler himself, especially revealing the intention of holding the ruler to demanding standards.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The elucidation of “difficult” and “not easy” is precise, incisive, earnest, and thorough, lucid and smoothly integrated. The exposition throughout remains within the meaning of Heaven’s mandate and the hearts of the people. Someone without long-established convictions could not attain this.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The style is rounded and powerful, the diction and tone spare and antique. It seems to wash away all the prolixity and forced interpretation of contemporary examination essays. Here is someone capable of firmly rejecting superficial ornament and earnestly honoring the grand elegance of classical writing.

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: His understanding of principle is clear and incisive, and his composition rigorous and orderly. Purity of learning, outstanding talent, and concentrated, unified thought are all evident in this work.

To discuss the responsibilities of ruler and minister and fulfill them completely requires, in each case, recognizing their difficulty. For ruler and minister alike bear responsibility for all under Heaven: their charge is supremely weighty. To understand its weight and consider how to discharge it fully—is this not difficult? The meaning of the Master’s words to Duke Ding was, presumably, that the Way of Kings offers no quick achievements, yet people’s sayings may contain the highest principles. If a ruler wishes to make his state flourish, why should he not examine what people say?

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
彼其意以體元居正者君也君以制命爲尊勢
若無難爲矣然以一人爲天下之主則必以一
身理天下之繁上而天命何以凝之而靈承之
道不敢忽下而人心何以維之而保乂之澤不
容緩正直難以邇也便佞難以遠也必一用人
而克當天心焉然後天眷之斯隆也所欲難與
聚也所惡難勿施也必一行政而允協人情焉
然後人心之可保也否則命爲難諶而民罔常
懷矣可無懼乎此其位之所在固有無疆之休
===
===
而責之所在實切無疆之恤也孰謂爲君之不
難哉代君弘化者臣也臣以分理爲務職若易
於稱矣然以一身任天下之重則必以一心先
天下之憂爲上爲德何以堯舜其君而迓天休
於滋至爲下爲民何以堯舜其民而固邦本於
有孚王躬不易保也王言不易司也必啓沃贊
襄之責塞而後可以語天工之亮也四方不易
發也百辟不易式也必經營屏翰之績奏而後
可以言帝載之熙也否則上負天子而下失民
punctuated:
彼其意以體元居正者，君也。君以制命爲尊，勢若無難爲矣。然以一人爲天下之主，則必以一身理天下之繁。上而天命何以凝之，而靈承之道不敢忽；下而人心何以維之，而保乂之澤不容緩。正直難以邇也，便佞難以遠也，必一用人而克當天心焉，然後天眷之斯隆也。所欲難與聚也，所惡難勿施也，必一行政而允協人情焉，然後人心之可保也。否則命爲難諶，而民罔常懷矣，可無懼乎？此其位之所在，固有無疆之休，而責之所在，實切無疆之恤也。孰謂爲君之不難哉？

代君弘化者，臣也。臣以分理爲務，職若易於稱矣。然以一身任天下之重，則必以一心先天下之憂。爲上爲德，何以堯舜其君，而迓天休於滋至；爲下爲民，何以堯舜其民，而固邦本於有孚？王躬不易保也，王言不易司也，必啓沃贊襄之責塞，而後可以語天工之亮也。四方不易發也，百辟不易式也，必經營屏翰之績奏，而後可以言帝載之熙也。否則上負天子，而下失民
translation_en:
…His meaning is that the ruler embodies the primal principle and occupies the rightful position. The ruler’s dignity lies in issuing commands, and his position might seem to present no difficulty. Yet, as the one man who is master of all under Heaven, he must personally manage its manifold affairs. Above, how is he to secure Heaven’s mandate? He dare not neglect the way of reverently receiving it. Below, how is he to hold the people’s hearts? He cannot delay the beneficence that protects them and brings them peace. It is difficult to keep the upright close and difficult to keep glib flatterers at a distance. Every appointment must accord with Heaven’s heart; only then will Heaven’s favor grow abundant. It is difficult to gather for the people what they desire, and difficult to refrain from imposing what they detest. Every act of government must truly accord with human feelings; only then can the people’s hearts be retained. Otherwise, the mandate is hard to rely upon, and the people’s allegiance is inconstant. Can he be without fear? His position certainly brings boundless blessings, but his responsibilities press upon him with boundless cares. Who could say that being a ruler is not difficult?

It is the minister who extends the ruler’s transforming influence on his behalf. The minister’s task is to administer his allotted responsibilities, and his office might seem easy to fulfill. Yet, bearing personally the weight of all under Heaven, he must set his whole heart upon anticipating the cares of all under Heaven. In serving those above and advancing virtue, how can he make his ruler a Yao or Shun and welcome Heaven’s blessings in ever greater abundance? In serving those below and working for the people, how can he make the people like those of Yao and Shun and secure the foundation of the state through trust? It is not easy to safeguard the king’s person, nor is it easy to oversee the king’s words. Only after fulfilling his responsibility to enlighten, counsel, and assist the ruler can he speak of helping accomplish Heaven’s work. It is not easy to rouse the four quarters, nor is it easy to serve as a model for the many lords. Only after achieving results in managing affairs and serving as a protective bulwark can he speak of bringing the sovereign’s undertakings to flourishing completion. Otherwise, above he fails the Son of Heaven, and below he loses the people’s…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
望矣寧無愧乎此其無成之分若可自處其逸
而有終之代則固獨居其勞也孰謂爲臣之爲
易哉吁君臣之位雖不同而克艱之道一而已
矣時人之言如此君欲興邦可不知爲君之難
乎雖然君臣一體也然總乾綱者則其責愈重
爲君尤難於爲臣也創守一道也然撫盈成者
則其心易忽守成尤難於創業也是故繼猶判
渙是繼體之初固當存其難之慮而鮮克有終
則人君之心殆無時而可易也然君之難難於
===
禮臣臣之難難於忠君觀夫子他日之告定公
者與此蓋互相發也有君臣之責者其尚致省
於斯以相成與
脩身也尊賢也親親也
同考試官教諭陸批發揮本題步驟聨屬且以
脩身爲聖學而尊賢親親爲天德王道所從出蓋究
心體要之學者宜錄以式
考試官教諭鎦批文雖三段氣實貫通整而
punctuated:
望矣，寧無愧乎？此其無成之分，若可自處其逸，而有終之代，則固獨居其勞也。孰謂爲臣之爲易哉？吁！君臣之位雖不同，而克艱之道一而已矣。時人之言如此，君欲興邦，可不知爲君之難乎？雖然，君臣一體也，然總乾綱者，則其責愈重，爲君尤難於爲臣也。創守一道也，然撫盈成者，則其心易忽，守成尤難於創業也。是故繼猶判渙，是繼體之初，固當存其難之慮；而鮮克有終，則人君之心，殆無時而可易也。然君之難，難於禮臣；臣之難，難於忠君。觀夫子他日之告定公者，與此蓋互相發也。有君臣之責者，其尚致省於斯，以相成與！

脩身也，尊賢也，親親也。

同考試官教諭陸批：發揮本題，步驟聨屬，且以脩身爲聖學，而尊賢親親爲天德王道所從出，蓋究心體要之學者，宜錄以式。

考試官教諭鎦批：文雖三段，氣實貫通，整而
translation_en:
…the people's expectations. Could he feel no shame? In his allotted role of claiming no achievement for himself, a minister might seem free to take his ease; yet in bringing affairs to completion on the ruler's behalf, he must indeed bear the toil himself. Who could say that serving as a minister is easy? Ah! Though ruler and minister occupy different positions, their way of meeting difficulties is one and the same. Since this is what people say, can a ruler who wishes to make his state flourish fail to understand the difficulty of being a ruler?

Nevertheless, ruler and minister form one body, but the one who holds supreme authority bears the greater responsibility: being a ruler is harder still than being a minister. Founding a dynasty and preserving it follow the same way, but one who presides over established prosperity can easily grow careless: preserving an accomplished order is harder still than founding it. Thus, “succession is still divided and dispersed” [?]: at the beginning of a succession, one must certainly remain mindful of its difficulties. And since “few can bring things to a good end,” there is scarcely any time when a ruler may regard his task as easy. Yet the difficulty for a ruler lies in treating his ministers with ritual propriety; the difficulty for a minister lies in loyalty to his ruler. If we consider what the Master told Duke Ding on another occasion, it illuminates this teaching, and this teaching illuminates it in turn. May those who bear the responsibilities of ruler and minister reflect deeply upon this, so that they may bring one another to fulfillment!

“Cultivating oneself, honoring the worthy, and cherishing one's kin.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: The essay develops the subject, with its successive stages coherently connected. Moreover, it takes self-cultivation as the learning of the sages, and honoring the worthy and cherishing one's kin as the source from which Heavenly virtue and the Kingly Way emerge. Its author evidently devotes himself to learning that grasps the essentials. It should be included as a model.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Although the essay has three sections, its vital force runs through them all. It is orderly and…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
不略詳而有體
考試官敎授熊批有脉絡有精神足覘一貫
之學錄之
中庸列常道之目而先其要之所在也蓋脩身
尊賢親親九經之要也於斯三者而知所先務
焉何政之有不舉哉想夫子告魯君之意蓋謂
治道固貴有以會其全圖治尤貴有以識其要
凡爲天下國家有九經矣而其要維何彼君身
者萬化之原也不有以脩之則皇極之未建敷
===
錫之無本而取人立政之基隳矣故必中正以
大其觀而慎厥身脩懋昭夫綏猷之度反躬以
體其道而率履不越克防乎邪動之辱夫是則
一人旣協於元良而百度自貞於順應舉而措
之將無不得其理者矣脩身非九經之首務乎
脩身以道明道必資於賢也賢有不尊則俊乂
之未庸啓沃之無自身不可得而脩矣其必擴
翕受之懷而尊德以隆其禮篤籲俊之誠而樂
道以忘其勢大賢以爲師也次賢以爲友也由
punctuated:
不略，詳而有體。
考試官敎授熊批：有脉絡，有精神，足覘一貫之學，錄之。
《中庸》列常道之目，而先其要之所在也。蓋脩身、尊賢、親親，九經之要也。於斯三者而知所先務焉，何政之有不舉哉？想夫子告魯君之意，蓋謂治道固貴有以會其全，圖治尤貴有以識其要。凡爲天下國家有九經矣，而其要維何？彼君身者，萬化之原也。不有以脩之，則皇極之未建，敷錫之無本，而取人立政之基隳矣。故必中正以大其觀，而慎厥身脩，懋昭夫綏猷之度；反躬以體其道，而率履不越，克防乎邪動之辱。夫是則一人旣協於元良，而百度自貞於順應，舉而措之，將無不得其理者矣。脩身非九經之首務乎？脩身以道，明道必資於賢也。賢有不尊，則俊乂之未庸，啓沃之無自，身不可得而脩矣。其必擴翕受之懷，而尊德以隆其禮；篤籲俊之誠，而樂道以忘其勢。大賢以爲師也，次賢以爲友也。由
translation_en:
…without being cursory; detailed, yet well structured.
Examiner Xiong, an Instructor, comments: “It has a coherent thread and vitality, sufficient to reveal learning unified by a single principle. Accept it.”
The Doctrine of the Mean enumerates the enduring principles of government, placing their essentials first. Cultivating oneself, honoring the worthy, and cherishing one’s kin are the essentials of the nine guiding principles. If one knows to give priority to these three, what affair of government could remain unaccomplished? Considering the Master’s intention in addressing the ruler of Lu, he presumably meant that, although governing requires comprehending the whole, planning good government requires above all recognizing its essentials. There are nine guiding principles for governing the world and its states and families. What, then, are their essentials? The ruler’s own person is the source of all transforming influence. Unless he cultivates himself, the supreme standard will remain unestablished, its widespread bestowal will lack a foundation, and the basis for selecting men and establishing government will crumble. He must therefore enlarge his vision through centrality and rectitude, attend carefully to his own cultivation, and diligently manifest the standards of a way that brings peace. He must examine himself to embody the Way, follow its prescribed course without transgression, and guard against the disgrace of wrongful action. Thus, once the sovereign accords with supreme goodness, the hundred institutions will naturally become correct through their compliant response; whatever he puts into practice will accord with its proper principle. Is cultivating oneself not the foremost task among the nine guiding principles?
One cultivates oneself through the Way, and understanding the Way necessarily depends upon the worthy. If the worthy are not honored, men of outstanding talent will go unemployed, there will be no source of enlightening counsel, and self-cultivation will be impossible. The ruler must broaden his receptiveness, honoring virtue by according the worthy generous ceremonial respect. He must be wholehearted in summoning outstanding men, delighting in the Way so that he forgets his own exalted power. He takes the most worthy as teachers and those next in worthiness as friends. title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
是羣賢旣得於夾輔君德自懋於交脩而身之
脩者為益進矣尊賢非脩身之次者乎脩道以
仁敦仁莫先於親也親有不親則彝倫之未叙
化理之或乖道不可得而進矣其必隆一本之
恩而緣分以盡其倫洽宗盟之情而因心以廣
其愛於諸父則孝也於昆弟則友也由是敦睦
旣裕於和親王化自行於善則而道之進者將
益遠矣親親又非尊賢之次者乎是則脩身者
聖學也尊賢則天德由之有成矣親親則王道
===
由之托始矣人君知所重而兼體焉文武之政
何患於不舉哉抑是道也各言之則為三總言
之實九經之全體也蓋尊賢有等推之而大臣
之敬羣臣之體者此也親親有殺推之而庶民
之子百工之來遠人柔而諸侯懷者此也而又
脩身以端二者之本焉則齊治均平之道一以
貫之矣故曰純心要矣用賢急焉而治天下觀
於家也後之欲行九經之道者可汎而寡要哉
盡其心者知其性也知其性則知天矣
punctuated:
是羣賢旣得於夾輔，君德自懋於交脩，而身之脩者為益進矣。尊賢非脩身之次者乎？脩道以仁，敦仁莫先於親也。親有不親，則彝倫之未叙，化理之或乖，道不可得而進矣。其必隆一本之恩，而緣分以盡其倫；洽宗盟之情，而因心以廣其愛。於諸父則孝也，於昆弟則友也。由是敦睦旣裕於和親，王化自行於善則，而道之進者將益遠矣。親親又非尊賢之次者乎？是則脩身者聖學也，尊賢則天德由之有成矣，親親則王道由之托始矣。人君知所重而兼體焉，文武之政何患於不舉哉？抑是道也，各言之則為三，總言之實九經之全體也。蓋尊賢有等，推之而大臣之敬、羣臣之體者此也；親親有殺，推之而庶民之子、百工之來、遠人柔而諸侯懷者此也。而又脩身以端二者之本焉，則齊治均平之道一以貫之矣。故曰：「純心要矣，用賢急焉，而治天下觀於家也。」後之欲行九經之道者，可汎而寡要哉？

盡其心者，知其性也；知其性，則知天矣。
translation_en:
…Thus, once the assembled worthy men have been secured as assistants, the ruler’s virtue naturally grows through their concerted efforts at its cultivation, and his self-cultivation advances still further. Is honoring the worthy not the next task after cultivating oneself? The Way is cultivated through benevolence, and in strengthening benevolence nothing takes precedence over one’s kin. If one fails to treat kin with affection, the enduring human relationships remain unordered, and moral transformation and governance may go astray; the Way cannot then advance. The ruler must deepen the kindness arising from common ancestry and fulfill his familial relationships according to their respective obligations; he must nurture affection within the lineage and extend his love from his own heart. Toward his paternal uncles he must be filial, and toward his brothers, brotherly. Thus, when familial harmony amply fosters concord among kin, kingly moral transformation naturally proceeds through this good example, and progress in the Way will extend still further. Is affection for kin not, in turn, the next task after honoring the worthy?

Self-cultivation, then, is the learning of the sages; through honoring the worthy, heavenly virtue reaches fulfillment; through affection for kin, the Kingly Way finds its beginning. If the ruler knows what matters most and embodies all these principles, why fear that the government of Kings Wen and Wu cannot be put into effect? Moreover, these principles, considered separately, number three; taken together, they actually comprise the entirety of the nine guiding standards. Honoring the worthy admits of ranks: extended further, it becomes respect for high ministers and sympathetic consideration for the other ministers. Affection for kin admits of diminishing degrees: extended further, it becomes treating the common people as one’s children, attracting the various artisans, showing kindness to people from afar, and cherishing the feudal lords. When self-cultivation further sets right the root of these two principles, a single thread runs through the Way of ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing equity and peace to the realm. Thus it is said: “Purifying the heart is essential; employing the worthy is urgent; and governing all under Heaven is to be observed in the family.” Can those in later ages who wish to practice the nine guiding standards range broadly while failing to grasp their essentials?

One who fully realizes his heart knows his nature; knowing his nature, he knows Heaven.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭宋批此題惟於知性處挑剔明
白而盡心知天一以貫之矣此作認理真切而措詞
典雅是深造自得之士也
同考試官教授唐批近時過于雕斲者或失之
萎弱而逞詞藻者又難于精美是卷說理縝密而氣
復昌大錄之
同考試官教授劉批天人一貫之學難言也而
子獨能發明透徹可與論性矣
===
考試官教諭錙批理明詞鬯而氣復俊逸有
養之士也
考試官教授熊批簡明平正體認真切可以
式矣
大賢原心之所由盡而因推其達諸天焉夫性
具于人而出於天者也窮理以知性則心無不
盡矣達天之妙豈外是哉孟子言此示人以窮
理之學也蓋曰天下之理原于性而心者性之
統會者也天者性之所從出者也自夫性有未
punctuated:
同考試官教諭宋批：此題惟於知性處挑剔明白，而盡心知天一以貫之矣。此作認理真切，而措詞典雅，是深造自得之士也。

同考試官教授唐批：近時過于雕斲者，或失之萎弱，而逞詞藻者，又難于精美。是卷說理縝密，而氣復昌大，錄之。

同考試官教授劉批：天人一貫之學難言也，而子獨能發明透徹，可與論性矣。

考試官教諭錙批：理明詞鬯，而氣復俊逸，有養之士也。

考試官教授熊批：簡明平正，體認真切，可以式矣。

大賢原心之所由盡，而因推其達諸天焉。夫性具于人而出於天者也，窮理以知性，則心無不盡矣。達天之妙，豈外是哉？孟子言此，示人以窮理之學也。蓋曰：天下之理原于性，而心者，性之統會者也；天者，性之所從出者也。自夫性有未
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: In treating this topic, one need only distinguish and clarify what it means to know one's nature; fully realizing one's mind and knowing Heaven are then connected by a single thread. This composition apprehends principle truly and precisely, and its diction is classical and elegant. Its author is a scholar who has studied deeply and attained understanding for himself.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Professor: Recently, those who overwork their writing sometimes lapse into feebleness, while those who flaunt verbal ornament also find it difficult to achieve refinement and beauty. This paper expounds principle with meticulous coherence, while its vital force is also abundant and expansive. Select it.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Professor: The learning that joins Heaven and humanity in a single thread is difficult to articulate, yet you alone have elucidated it thoroughly. One may discuss human nature with you.

Comment by Examiner Zi [?], Instructor: The principles are clear, the language fluent, and the vital force is also outstanding and untrammeled. This is a scholar who has cultivated himself.

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: Concise, clear, balanced, and sound, with a true and precise personal apprehension of the subject. It may serve as a model.

The great worthy traces how the mind comes to be fully realized and, on that basis, extends his account to its comprehension of Heaven. Human nature is inherent in people but originates in Heaven. By investigating principle exhaustively so as to know one's nature, one leaves nothing in the mind unrealized. How could the subtle mystery of comprehending Heaven lie outside this? Mencius spoke these words to show people the learning that investigates principle exhaustively. His meaning was this: all principles under Heaven originate in human nature; the mind is where that nature is gathered into a unified whole, and Heaven is that from which it issues. If there is something in one's nature not yet …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
知則心有未盡而於天始不相通矣夫惟于此
心也昭曠之原以廓而湛然至虛者有以完其
體高明之量以充而瑩然至靈者有以復其常
是心無不盡矣而非心之自盡也必其道融於
研窮之後而性之原于一本者有以疏觀其蘊
奧之深理會于格致之餘而性之散于萬殊者
有以洞徹其幾微之故性之無遺知者斯心之
無遺理也是盡心固由於知性矣不可以知天
乎蓋天人一理也性命一道也達民秉之彝者
===
自有以通神明之德昭成性之存者自足以會
繼善之初命之渾淪即性之體統也不必求端
於天而其機自可以旁通矣命之流行即性之
散見也不必仰觀于天而其理自可以默識矣
謂之曰知天信乎吾性之中已具乎天載之神
而於穆之妙不出乎吾性之理矣是則莫難盡
者吾之心莫難知者天之道一性盡而貫通之
無遺焉君子事心之功大矣哉抑此孔門授受
之心法也窮理盡性孔子發其端矣格物致知
punctuated: 知，則心有未盡，而於天始不相通矣。夫惟于此心也，昭曠之原以廓，而湛然至虛者有以完其體；高明之量以充，而瑩然至靈者有以復其常。是心無不盡矣，而非心之自盡也。必其道融於研窮之後，而性之原于一本者有以疏觀其蘊奧之深；理會于格致之餘，而性之散于萬殊者有以洞徹其幾微之故。性之無遺知者，斯心之無遺理也。是盡心固由於知性矣，不可以知天乎？蓋天人一理也，性命一道也。達民秉之彝者，自有以通神明之德；昭成性之存者，自足以會繼善之初。命之渾淪，即性之體統也，不必求端於天，而其機自可以旁通矣；命之流行，即性之散見也，不必仰觀于天，而其理自可以默識矣。謂之曰知天，信乎吾性之中已具乎天載之神，而於穆之妙不出乎吾性之理矣。是則莫難盡者吾之心，莫難知者天之道，一性盡而貫通之無遺焉。君子事心之功大矣哉！抑此孔門授受之心法也。窮理盡性，孔子發其端矣；格物致知，
translation_en:
…known, then the heart-mind remains incompletely realized, and communication with Heaven is thereby obstructed. Only when this heart-mind’s luminous and expansive source is broadened can its limpid, utterly empty substance attain completeness; only when its lofty and luminous capacity is filled can its radiant, supremely numinous power recover its constant condition. The heart-mind is then fully realized, yet it does not realize itself unaided. Only after inquiry has been pursued to the utmost does the Way become thoroughly understood, allowing one to survey [?] the profound mysteries of human nature as it originates in a single root. Only through the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge is principle comprehended, allowing one to penetrate the subtle workings of human nature as it is manifested in countless particular forms. When nothing in human nature remains unknown, no principle is absent from the heart-mind. Thus, fully realizing the heart-mind assuredly proceeds from knowing human nature. Can one not thereby know Heaven?

For Heaven and humanity share one principle, and human nature and Heaven’s decree share one Way. Those who comprehend the constant norms endowed in the people thereby have the means to penetrate the efficacy of spiritual intelligence; those who illuminate what subsists as completed human nature thereby have sufficient means to comprehend the beginning in which goodness is perpetuated. Heaven’s decree in its undivided wholeness is the integral substance of human nature. One need not seek its beginnings in Heaven: its workings can of themselves be comprehended in all their connections. Heaven’s decree in its ongoing activity is human nature manifested in its various particulars. One need not look upward to observe Heaven: its principle can of itself be silently apprehended. This is called knowing Heaven. Truly, our human nature already contains the numinous power of Heaven’s workings, and the subtlety of Heaven’s profound and unceasing operation does not lie outside the principle of our nature.

Thus, nothing is harder to realize fully than our heart-mind, and nothing is harder to know than Heaven’s Way. Yet once human nature is fully realized, both are comprehended throughout, with nothing left out. How great is the achievement of the gentleman’s cultivation of the heart-mind! This, indeed, is the teaching of the heart-mind transmitted in the school of Confucius. Confucius first set forth the exhaustive investigation of principle and the full realization of human nature; as for the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
曾子闡其微矣盡心知性孟子其有所受之也
夫何異端者起不曰盡心而曰明心不曰知性
而曰見性使吾道之正晦焉而不明可慨已噫
吾心之性自瑩吾性之天自徹也善學者當自
得焉
易
飛龍在天乃位乎天德
同考試官教諭張批德位自有輕重作者多欠
===
妥帖此篇體認精切措辭昌大宜錄以式
同考試官教諭張批識見卓越體格宏遠聖人
在天子之位發揮殆盡佳士也
考試官教諭鎦批純正
考試官教授熊批明確
文言申乾爻之象而原其君道之備也蓋聖人
在天子之位君道莫備於是矣乾之九五以之
此其所以取象于飛龍也歟今夫人君之御世
也孰不有位以大一統之權而每難於有德以
punctuated:
曾子闡其微矣，盡心知性，孟子其有所受之也。夫何異端者起，不曰盡心而曰明心，不曰知性而曰見性，使吾道之正晦焉而不明，可慨已！噫！吾心之性自瑩，吾性之天自徹也，善學者當自得焉。
易
「飛龍在天，乃位乎天德。」
同考試官教諭張批：德位自有輕重，作者多欠妥帖。此篇體認精切，措辭昌大，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭張批：識見卓越，體格宏遠，聖人在天子之位，發揮殆盡，佳士也。
考試官教諭鎦批：純正。
考試官教授熊批：明確。
《文言》申乾爻之象，而原其君道之備也。蓋聖人在天子之位，君道莫備於是矣，乾之九五以之，此其所以取象于飛龍也歟？今夫人君之御世也，孰不有位以大一統之權，而每難於有德以
translation_en:
…Zengzi elucidated its subtleties. As for fully realizing the heart-mind and knowing one’s nature, Mengzi must have received this teaching through transmission. Why, then, did adherents of heterodox teachings arise, speaking not of fully realizing the heart-mind but of illuminating it, not of knowing one’s nature but of seeing it, thereby obscuring the rectitude of our Way and preventing it from shining forth? How lamentable! Ah! The nature within our heart-mind is intrinsically luminous, and Heaven within our nature is intrinsically clear. Those who learn well should apprehend this for themselves.

Book of Changes

“A flying dragon in heaven: this is to occupy a position grounded in heavenly virtue.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Virtue and position have their respective degrees of importance, and writers often fail to treat them appropriately. This essay’s understanding is precise and penetrating, and its language expansive and grand. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “His insight is outstanding, and his composition is grand in form and far-reaching in scope. He develops almost exhaustively the meaning of a sage occupying the position of the Son of Heaven. A fine scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Pure and orthodox.”

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: “Clear and precise.”

The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the image of the line in Qian and traces the grounds for the completeness of its Way of rulership. When a sage occupies the position of the Son of Heaven, the Way of rulership could be no more complete. The nine in the fifth place of Qian embodies this. Is this not why it takes the flying dragon as its image? Now, among rulers governing the world, who does not possess the position through which to magnify the authority of unified rule? Yet they invariably find it difficult to possess the virtue through which to…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
端萬化之本備是二者其惟乾之九五乎彼周
公繫之詞曰飛龍在天云者固以其得時行道
而擬諸象也其果何所取義也邪蓋以乾之九
五也剛健中正以居尊位則以言其位固天所
與也而以之昭德者有其具以言其德則天所
縱也而以之正位者有其基握乾符以凝命固
以一人而撫萬邦矣而乾元之善此其體之聰
明之克亶乃其作元后以無忝者也嚮陽明以
圖治固以四海而仰一人矣而陽道之純此其
===
全之帝德之罔愆乃其履帝位於不疚者也先
天而弘開創之仁則凡彌綸參贊以沛乘龍御
天之澤者其勢之所得為孰非德之所優為乎
大觀之在上非徒萃有位而匪孚矣後天而敷
茂育之政則凡裁成輔相以終雲行雨施之功
者其權之所獨運孰非德之所廣運乎皇極之
攸建非徒屯上施而未光矣要之德以基位則
位非虛器一龍之飛焉而神明之莫測也位以
施德則德非終窮一龍之在天而神功之顯行
punctuated: 端萬化之本。備是二者，其惟乾之九五乎？彼周公繫之詞曰「飛龍在天」云者，固以其得時行道而擬諸象也。其果何所取義也邪？蓋以乾之九五也，剛健中正以居尊位，則以言其位，固天所與也，而以之昭德者有其具；以言其德，則天所縱也，而以之正位者有其基。握乾符以凝命，固以一人而撫萬邦矣，而乾元之善，此其體之；聰明之克亶，乃其作元后以無忝者也。嚮陽明以圖治，固以四海而仰一人矣，而陽道之純，此其全之；帝德之罔愆，乃其履帝位於不疚者也。先天而弘開創之仁，則凡彌綸參贊以沛乘龍御天之澤者，其勢之所得為，孰非德之所優為乎？大觀之在上，非徒萃有位而匪孚矣。後天而敷茂育之政，則凡裁成輔相以終雲行雨施之功者，其權之所獨運，孰非德之所廣運乎？皇極之攸建，非徒屯上施而未光矣。要之，德以基位，則位非虛器，一龍之飛焉而神明之莫測也；位以施德，則德非終窮，一龍之在天而神功之顯行
translation_en:
…to set right the foundation of all transformation. Surely it is the Nine in the Fifth Place of Qian alone that possesses both these qualities? When the Duke of Zhou attached the words “A flying dragon in Heaven,” he surely framed this image because the ruler had met his proper time and was putting the Way into practice. What meaning, then, does the image convey? The Nine in the Fifth Place of Qian occupies the exalted position through strength, vigor, centrality, and correctness. In terms of his position, it is assuredly Heaven that has bestowed it, and he possesses the means to make his virtue manifest. In terms of his virtue, it is Heaven that has richly endowed him, and he possesses the foundation for securing his position aright. Holding Heaven’s tally and making firm the mandate, he assuredly comforts the myriad states as their sole ruler; yet he embodies the goodness of Qian’s primal power. Truly possessing perceptiveness and understanding, he serves as the sovereign without disgrace. Facing the brightness of yang as he plans good government, he assuredly receives the homage of all within the Four Seas as their sole ruler; yet he preserves the purity of the way of yang in its entirety. Free from fault in his imperial virtue, he occupies the imperial position without reproach.

Preceding Heaven, he extends the benevolence that inaugurates a new order. In all his work of encompassing and ordering the world and assisting its transforming and nourishing powers, he abundantly spreads the blessings of “riding the dragons to govern Heaven.” Of all that his commanding position enables him to accomplish, what does his virtue not enable him to accomplish with ample ease? A great exemplar stands above: this is no mere “Gathering Together” in which one “has the position” but lacks trust. Following Heaven, he puts forth policies that foster flourishing growth. In all his work of regulating and completing Heaven and Earth’s operations and assisting their fitting processes, he fulfills the achievement of “clouds moving and rain falling.” Of all that his authority alone directs, what does his virtue not direct far and wide? The sovereign standard is established: this is no mere “Difficulty at the Beginning,” in which benefits are dispensed from above but their light has yet to spread.

The essential point is that when virtue provides the foundation for position, position is no empty vessel: a dragon flies, its spiritual intelligence beyond fathoming. When position serves to extend virtue, virtue never reaches exhaustion: a dragon is in Heaven, and its wondrous efficacy is visibly at work…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
也此九五之象所由取而占之利見也有以哉
噫周公繫詞至此蓋亦深幸世道之隆也歟大
抵乾天也君道也故卦之六陽皆以龍稱問學
于二以充養此天德也進脩于三以涵育此天
德也奮于潜試于躍而變化于飛焉此九五所
以爲萬世君道之極也雖然行健不已者天道
所以成化也自强不息者人君所以成治也欲
繼天以立極者又不可不法天以立道
成性存存道義之門
===
同考試官教諭張 批 聖學之妙最難發揮此卷獨
見理明透敷詞純確非易義之精者其孰能之
同考試官教諭張 批 成性道義皆根知禮作者
類能言之而純雅精瑩無踰此篇
考試官教諭鎦 批 得潔靜精微之旨是必深
於易者錄之
考試官教授熊 批 通暢
聖人盡性而妙用出焉用易之極功也夫性爲
punctuated:
也。此九五之象所由取，而占之利見也，有以哉！噫！周公繫詞至此，蓋亦深幸世道之隆也歟！大抵乾，天也，君道也，故卦之六陽皆以龍稱。問學于二，以充養此天德也；進脩于三，以涵育此天德也；奮于潜，試于躍，而變化于飛焉。此九五所以爲萬世君道之極也。雖然，行健不已者，天道所以成化也；自强不息者，人君所以成治也。欲繼天以立極者，又不可不法天以立道。
成性存存，道義之門。
同考試官教諭張批：聖學之妙，最難發揮。此卷獨見理明透，敷詞純確，非易義之精者，其孰能之？
同考試官教諭張批：成性道義，皆根知禮，作者類能言之，而純雅精瑩，無踰此篇。
考試官教諭鎦批：得潔靜精微之旨，是必深於易者，錄之。
考試官教授熊批：通暢。
聖人盡性而妙用出焉，用易之極功也。夫性爲
translation_en:
…This is why the image of the Nine in the Fifth Place was chosen, and why its divination pronouncement says that it is beneficial to see the great man. There is good reason for this! Ah! When the Duke of Zhou appended his words at this point, surely he too rejoiced deeply in the flourishing of the age! In general, Qian represents Heaven and the way of the ruler; thus all six yang lines of the hexagram are described as dragons. Inquiry and learning at the second place serve to nourish this heavenly virtue fully; advancement and cultivation at the third serve to nurture this heavenly virtue. From exertion while hidden, through trial in leaping, transformation culminates in flight. This is why the Nine in the Fifth Place represents the supreme standard of rulership for all ages. Nevertheless, through ceaseless vigorous movement, the Way of Heaven brings transformation to completion; through unremitting self-strengthening, the ruler achieves good government. One who wishes to succeed Heaven and establish the supreme standard must also model himself on Heaven to establish the Way.
“Continually preserving one’s perfected nature: the gateway of the Way and righteousness.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The subtleties of sagely learning are exceedingly difficult to elucidate. This essay alone displays a clear and penetrating understanding of principle, expressed in language that is pure and precise. Who could accomplish this without mastery of the meaning of the Changes?”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Both perfected nature and the Way and righteousness are rooted in knowledge and ritual propriety. Writers can generally speak of these matters, but for purity, elegance, refinement, and clarity, none surpasses this essay.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It grasps the purport of purity and stillness, subtlety and precision. This must be someone deeply versed in the Changes. Accept it.”
Examiner Xiong, Professor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”
The sage fully realizes his nature, and its wondrous functioning emerges: this is the consummate achievement of applying the Changes. Now, human nature is…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
天下之大本也智禮純于內則性無不盡矣而
道義之用有不以時出之者乎大傳賛易之至
而及聖人用易之極功也至此若謂大哉易乎
以神造化之功者此也以妙聖學之全者此也
是故兩儀奠位而變化行天地則有然者聖人
之智禮成性也其妙果何如哉彼性莫不有是
智也聖人之智崇效乎天則高朗之有融者緝
熙之罔間一高明之無疆焉亦莫不有是禮也
聖人之禮卑法乎地則敦厚之有常者至誠之
===
無息一博厚之無窮焉蘊之爲天衷之降者非
有所存而自不忘也亹亹乎道心之爲主私欲
不得以間之矣本之爲天命之良者非有所理
而自不亂也肫肫乎德性之常用外誘不足以
撓之矣此固聖人自盡其性也而何以爲道義
之門耶殊不知性非內也道義之所爲存主者
也道義非外也成性之所爲散殊者也今性旣
存矣吾知性立其有者情效其動而措則正施
則行其履之爲道者莫不由是以妙率循之則
punctuated: 天下之大本也。智禮純于內，則性無不盡矣，而道義之用有不以時出之者乎？大傳賛易之至，而及聖人用易之極功也。至此，若謂大哉易乎！以神造化之功者，此也；以妙聖學之全者，此也。是故兩儀奠位而變化行，天地則有然者。聖人之智禮成性也，其妙果何如哉？彼性莫不有是智也，聖人之智崇效乎天，則高朗之有融者，緝熙之罔間，一高明之無疆焉。亦莫不有是禮也，聖人之禮卑法乎地，則敦厚之有常者，至誠之無息，一博厚之無窮焉。蘊之爲天衷之降者，非有所存而自不忘也，亹亹乎道心之爲主，私欲不得以間之矣。本之爲天命之良者，非有所理而自不亂也，肫肫乎德性之常用，外誘不足以撓之矣。此固聖人自盡其性也，而何以爲道義之門耶？殊不知性非內也，道義之所爲存主者也；道義非外也，成性之所爲散殊者也。今性旣存矣，吾知性立其有者，情效其動，而措則正，施則行，其履之爲道者，莫不由是以妙率循之則。
translation_en:
…the great foundation of all under Heaven. When wisdom and ritual propriety are pure within, human nature is fully realized in every respect. Could the workings of the Way and righteousness then fail to emerge as the occasion requires? The Great Commentary praises the Changes to the utmost, reaching even to the sage’s supreme achievement in putting the Changes into practice. At this point, it is as though it were saying: How great are the Changes! Here is what makes the work of creation and transformation numinous; here is what brings the entirety of sagely learning to wondrous perfection. Thus, when the two primal powers take their established places, change and transformation proceed: this is so of Heaven and Earth. What, then, is the wonder of the sage’s wisdom and ritual propriety becoming his nature?

Every person’s nature possesses this wisdom. The sage’s wisdom is exalted, taking Heaven as its exemplar: its lofty clarity shines forth, its continuing illumination knows no interruption, and it is wholly one with Heaven’s boundless height and brightness. Every person’s nature likewise possesses this ritual propriety. The sage’s ritual propriety is humble, taking Earth as its model: its generous substantiality is constant, its utmost sincerity never ceases, and it is wholly one with Earth’s inexhaustible breadth and depth.

What he harbors within is the Heaven-bestowed moral endowment: without deliberately holding it in mind, he naturally never forgets it. Tirelessly, the moral mind rules, and selfish desires cannot intrude. What he takes as his foundation is the goodness bestowed by Heaven’s mandate: without deliberately putting it in order, it naturally remains free of disorder. With wholehearted sincerity, his moral nature operates constantly, and external temptations cannot disturb it. This is indeed the sage’s full realization of his own nature. But how does it constitute the gateway to the Way and righteousness?

One fails to understand that nature is not merely something internal: it is where the Way and righteousness abide and find their governing source. Nor are the Way and righteousness merely external: they are the differentiated manifestations of fully realized nature. Now that this nature is preserved, I know that nature establishes what it inherently possesses, while the feelings manifest its activity. Whatever is put into practice is correct; whatever is applied proceeds successfully. As for conduct that constitutes the Way, all of it draws upon this to bring to perfection the standards by which one follows it…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
體貞夫一者用達夫順而以守經以行權其裁
之爲義者莫不由是以啓推行之機其涵智之
理于吾心也所以周知乎道義而不遺者取之
逢源而不匱也萬感雖紛紜而性其樞紐之矣
其裕禮之體于吾內也所以允迪乎道義而不
過者出之有本而不窮也百爲雖泛應而性其
宰制之矣至是則成性之渾淪者猶天地之奠
位也道義之時出者猶變化之顯行也聖人之
德業斯其有全功歟然皆有資于易焉易道不
===
其至哉抑此知行合一之學也智以崇德禮以
廣業聖人盡性之妙從容中道者也致知以爲
入門踐履以爲實地學者致曲之功擇善固執
者也誠能由勉而安希賢而聖則知行竝進而
德業有基易不在聖人而在吾心矣善學易者
當自得之
書
允若茲嘉言罔攸伏野無遺賢萬邦咸寧
punctuated:
體貞夫一者，用達夫順，而以守經，以行權。其裁之爲義者，莫不由是以啓推行之機。其涵智之理于吾心也，所以周知乎道義而不遺者，取之逢源而不匱也。萬感雖紛紜，而性其樞紐之矣。其裕禮之體于吾內也，所以允迪乎道義而不過者，出之有本而不窮也。百爲雖泛應，而性其宰制之矣。至是，則成性之渾淪者，猶天地之奠位也；道義之時出者，猶變化之顯行也。聖人之德業，斯其有全功歟？然皆有資于易焉，易道不其至哉！抑此知行合一之學也。智以崇德，禮以廣業，聖人盡性之妙，從容中道者也；致知以爲入門，踐履以爲實地，學者致曲之功，擇善固執者也。誠能由勉而安，希賢而聖，則知行竝進，而德業有基，易不在聖人而在吾心矣。善學易者，當自得之。

書

允若茲，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。
translation_en:
…Its substance is steadfast in unity, and its functioning fully accords with what is fitting, thereby maintaining constant principles and exercising discretion. Its judgments, which constitute righteousness, all proceed from this to open the way for putting them into practice. By nurturing the principles of wisdom in our minds, it enables us to comprehend the Way and righteousness comprehensively, omitting nothing: wherever we draw upon them, we encounter their source and never exhaust it. Though the myriad things that move us are tangled and diverse, our nature serves as their pivot. By enriching within us the substance of ritual propriety, it enables us faithfully to follow the Way and righteousness without transgression: what issues forth has a root and is inexhaustible. Though our countless actions respond to every sort of circumstance, our nature governs them all.

At this point, the undivided wholeness of perfected nature resembles Heaven and Earth taking their established positions; the timely emergence of the Way and righteousness resembles the manifest operation of transformation. Would not the sage’s virtue and accomplishments thus attain their full realization? Yet all this depends upon the Changes. Is not the Way of the Changes indeed supreme! This, moreover, is the learning that unites knowledge and action. To exalt virtue through wisdom and broaden accomplishments through ritual propriety is the wondrous way in which sages fully realize their nature, effortlessly hitting the mean of the Way.
