To take the extension of knowledge as the entrance and actual practice as the firm ground is the work by which learners bring particular aspects of their goodness to fulfillment, choosing the good and holding firmly to it. If we can truly pass from effort to ease, aspire to worthiness and attain sagehood, then knowledge and action will advance together, and virtue and accomplishments will have a foundation. The Changes will reside not only in the sages but in our own minds. Those who study the Changes well should attain this understanding for themselves.

Book of Documents

“If you truly act thus, no excellent counsel will remain concealed, no worthy person in the countryside will be overlooked, and the myriad states will all be at peace.”

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陸批講效中歸重君臣克艱意
深得本章旨趣可錄
考試官教諭鎦批平正通達
考試官教授熊批渾厚典雅
聖君推言君臣克盡其艱而獲效為甚大焉蓋
克艱貴于實盡也果能此道矣則治效之大也
不可以預期哉昔舜推廣禹謨也意曰君臣之
分不同而當盡之責則一誠如禹言上下交脩
而精神之運于內者罔非克艱之實心明良協
===
濟而事業之措諸外者罔非克艱之實政則效
之所臻豈止于政治民化而已哉吾知天下之
嘉言因時而為顯晦也今吾克艱而虛受之有
地矣則善論入陳攄其忠以熈帝載也昌言日
賛效其直以沃君心也無復自甘退默而以言
為諱矣夫何有于伏乎天下之賢相時而為行
藏也今吾克艱而感召之有機矣則奮迹于潛
出而為勵翼之臣也觀光于國起而為浚明之
助也無復自賁丘園而以隱為高矣夫何有于
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陸批：講效中歸重君臣克艱意，深得本章旨趣，可錄。
考試官教諭鎦批：平正通達。
考試官教授熊批：渾厚典雅。
聖君推言君臣克盡其艱，而獲效為甚大焉。蓋克艱貴于實盡也，果能此道矣，則治效之大也，不可以預期哉？昔舜推廣禹謨也，意曰：君臣之分不同，而當盡之責則一。誠如禹言，上下交脩，而精神之運于內者，罔非克艱之實心；明良協濟，而事業之措諸外者，罔非克艱之實政，則效之所臻，豈止于政治民化而已哉？吾知天下之嘉言，因時而為顯晦也。今吾克艱，而虛受之有地矣，則善論入陳，攄其忠以熈帝載也；昌言日賛，效其直以沃君心也。無復自甘退默，而以言為諱矣，夫何有于伏乎？天下之賢，相時而為行藏也。今吾克艱，而感召之有機矣，則奮迹于潛，出而為勵翼之臣也；觀光于國，起而為浚明之助也。無復自賁丘園，而以隱為高矣，夫何有于
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “In discussing the results, this answer places due emphasis on the ruler and ministers fully acknowledging the difficulty of their responsibilities. It grasps the purport of this passage very well and merits inclusion.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Balanced, sound, and clear.”
Examiner Xiong, Professor, comments: “Substantial, dignified, and elegant.”
The sage ruler elaborates on how ruler and ministers, fully meeting the difficulties of their responsibilities, achieve exceedingly great results. For what matters in meeting these difficulties is genuinely fulfilling one’s responsibilities. If this way can indeed be followed, can one not anticipate the greatness of its results in government?
Long ago, when Shun expanded upon Yu’s counsels, his meaning was this: “The positions of ruler and ministers differ, but their obligation to fulfill their responsibilities is the same. If, truly following Yu’s words, those above and below cultivate one another, then all the workings of their spirits within will express a sincere resolve to meet these difficulties. If an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers cooperate, then all the undertakings they carry out externally will constitute practical government directed toward meeting these difficulties. Could the results attained extend only to orderly government and the transformation of the people?
“I know that excellent counsel throughout the realm comes to light or remains obscure according to the times. Now, if I meet these difficulties and provide an opening for receiving counsel with humility, sound proposals will be presented at court: men will express their loyalty to advance the sovereign’s work. Fine counsel will daily offer assistance: men will exercise their candor to nourish the ruler’s mind. No longer will they willingly withdraw into silence and regard speaking out as taboo. How, then, could counsel remain concealed?
“The worthy men of the realm judge the times in deciding whether to serve or withdraw. Now, if I meet these difficulties and create the means to inspire and attract them, they will rouse themselves from obscurity and come forth as ministers who encourage and assist me. They will behold the glory of the realm and rise to help advance enlightened rule. No longer will they adorn their lives among hills and gardens and regard reclusion as lofty. How, then, could there be …”

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
遺乎以至萬邦則盡乎民矣然亦視上以爲休
戚者也今吾克艱則文命四訖合九有以同仁
德澤誕敷冒萬物而竝育樂利溥而生成遂也
亨嘉會而熈皥成也將無一夫之不獲矣又何
有于弗寧哉是則治道至是而後謂之大道治
功至是而後謂之成功爲吾君臣者容可不盡
克艱之實哉抑舜應運而興紹堯而治而禹以
大聖之資輔之則當時治道宜無足慮者然克
艱之謨禹則惓惓而舜亦深契焉何哉蓋賢臣
===
甞危明主而聖人則憂治世是以臣告君而非
傷于瀆君契臣而不嫌于同上下勤恤交脩益
至此有虞之治所以已隆而益隆也與
今王嗣厥德罔不在初
同考試官教諭陸 批 謹始意說得詳盡得伊尹
告君口氣
考試官教諭鎦 批 深得伊尹慮始之意
考試官教授熊 批 瑩徹明爽誠爲作手
punctuated:
遺乎？以至萬邦，則盡乎民矣，然亦視上以爲休戚者也。今吾克艱，則文命四訖，合九有以同仁；德澤誕敷，冒萬物而竝育。樂利溥而生成遂也，亨嘉會而熈皥成也。將無一夫之不獲矣，又何有于弗寧哉？是則治道至是而後謂之大道，治功至是而後謂之成功。爲吾君臣者，容可不盡克艱之實哉？抑舜應運而興，紹堯而治，而禹以大聖之資輔之，則當時治道宜無足慮者。然克艱之謨，禹則惓惓，而舜亦深契焉，何哉？蓋賢臣甞危明主，而聖人則憂治世。是以臣告君而非傷于瀆，君契臣而不嫌于同。上下勤恤，交脩益至，此有虞之治所以已隆而益隆也與！
今王嗣厥德，罔不在初。
同考試官教諭陸批：謹始意說得詳盡，得伊尹告君口氣。
考試官教諭鎦批：深得伊尹慮始之意。
考試官教授熊批：瑩徹明爽，誠爲作手。
translation_en:
…be left overlooked? As for the myriad states, these encompass all the people, yet their well-being or distress likewise depends upon their ruler. If we now recognize the difficulty of our responsibilities, our civilizing teachings will reach the four quarters, uniting the nine regions under a common benevolence. The blessings of our virtue will spread widely, encompassing all things and nourishing them together. Happiness and benefit will extend everywhere, and all things will attain their full growth. All that is flourishing and auspicious will converge, bringing about radiant harmony. Not a single person will fail to find fulfillment: how, then, could there be any lack of peace? Only when the way of government reaches this point can it be called the great Way; only when the achievements of government reach this point can they be called accomplished success. Can we, as ruler and ministers, possibly fail to realize fully what it means to recognize the difficulty of our responsibilities?

Moreover, Shun arose in accordance with Heaven’s appointed time and succeeded Yao in governing, while Yu assisted him with the endowments of a great sage. The way of government at that time should therefore have offered no grounds for concern. Yet Yu earnestly urged recognition of the difficulty of their responsibilities, and Shun deeply embraced his counsel. Why was this? Worthy ministers have ever made enlightened rulers mindful of danger, while sages have felt concern even in well-governed ages. Thus, when a minister admonishes his ruler, he commits no offense of importunity; when a ruler concurs with his minister, there is no suspicion of mere conformity. Those above and below diligently attend to their responsibilities, and their mutual cultivation becomes ever more complete. Surely this is why the government of Shun, already flourishing, flourished still further!

“You, the present king, inherit his virtue; everything depends upon the beginning.”

Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “The importance of taking care at the beginning is explained thoroughly and in detail. It captures the tone of Yi Yin admonishing his ruler.”

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It deeply grasps Yi Yin’s concern for the beginning.”

Examiner Xiong, Professor, comments: “Limpid, penetrating, clear, and lucid: truly an accomplished writer.”

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
大臣勉後王之繼先德而當致慎於其始焉蓋
慎始所以善終也後王嗣德而能於始焉圖之
君道有不盡哉伊尹訓太甲及此若曰人君之
為治也固以法祖為先尤以虔始為要先王之
位以德而受於天者也今王嗣之維何是故承
丕基之授則先德之締造者不可無駿惠之心
仰令緒之貽則先德之凝承者不可忘作求之
念敬德而克配上帝一代之心法存焉而吾則
善繼之昔以之創業者今嗣之以守成也懋德
===
而垂裕後昆一代之家法存焉而吾則善述之
昔以之開國者今嗣之以承家也夫嗣德如此
然其時奚以哉蓋出震履乾萬民正始之初也
凡丕承先志而作則于天下者惟因其可為之
時體元居正百官承式之初也凡克紹前烈而
敷治于四方者惟乘其一新之會上而天命於
茲而繫其去留焉祈天永命而延國祚于靈長
者在斯時也失此而不知法祖以敬天焉是始
之不慎矣而能善其終于無窮也何可得哉下
punctuated: 大臣勉後王之繼先德，而當致慎於其始焉。蓋慎始所以善終也。後王嗣德，而能於始焉圖之，君道有不盡哉？伊尹訓太甲及此，若曰：人君之為治也，固以法祖為先，尤以虔始為要。先王之位，以德而受於天者也，今王嗣之維何？是故承丕基之授，則先德之締造者，不可無駿惠之心；仰令緒之貽，則先德之凝承者，不可忘作求之念。敬德而克配上帝，一代之心法存焉，而吾則善繼之；昔以之創業者，今嗣之以守成也。懋德而垂裕後昆，一代之家法存焉，而吾則善述之；昔以之開國者，今嗣之以承家也。夫嗣德如此，然其時奚以哉？蓋出震履乾，萬民正始之初也，凡丕承先志而作則于天下者，惟因其可為之時；體元居正，百官承式之初也，凡克紹前烈而敷治于四方者，惟乘其一新之會。上而天命，於茲而繫其去留焉，祈天永命而延國祚于靈長者，在斯時也。失此而不知法祖以敬天焉，是始之不慎矣，而能善其終于無窮也，何可得哉？下
translation_en:
The great minister exhorts the succeeding king to carry on his predecessor’s virtue and to exercise particular care at the beginning. For care at the beginning is the means to a good outcome. If the succeeding king plans from the outset how to inherit that virtue, what part of the ruler’s Way will remain unfulfilled? In instructing Tai Jia on this matter, Yi Yin seems to say: In governing, a ruler must certainly give priority to following his ancestors’ example, but above all he must begin with reverent care. The former king received his throne from Heaven through his virtue. How, then, should the present king succeed him?

Thus, in receiving this great foundation, you must wholeheartedly follow the virtue through which your predecessor established it; in looking up to the splendid legacy he bequeathed, you must not forget to pursue the virtue through which he secured and sustained it. By reverencing virtue, he became worthy to stand beside the Lord on High: herein lies the dynasty’s teaching of the heart, which I must carry on well. The virtue with which he formerly founded his enterprise I now inherit to preserve his achievement. By cultivating virtue, he bequeathed abundance to later descendants: herein lies the dynasty’s rule for its house, which I must faithfully perpetuate. The virtue with which he formerly founded the state I now inherit to sustain the royal house.

Such is the inheritance of virtue. But what role does timing play? Emerging from Zhen, the trigram of the eldest son, to take the place of Qian, the trigram of the sovereign, marks the outset when all the people receive a correct beginning. All that you do to carry forward your predecessor’s intentions and set an example for the world depends on seizing the time when it can be done. Embodying the primal beginning and occupying the rightful position marks the outset when the hundred officials receive their model. All that you do to continue your predecessor’s glorious achievements and extend good government throughout the four quarters depends on taking advantage of this moment of universal renewal.

Above, whether Heaven’s Mandate departs or remains depends upon this moment. This is the time to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate and prolong the dynasty’s blessed tenure into the distant future. If you let this opportunity slip and fail to follow your ancestors’ example in reverencing Heaven, you have been careless at the beginning. How, then, could you bring matters to a good conclusion that endures forever? Below…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
而民心於玆而决其向背焉保民圖治而致世
道之雍熈者在斯時也失此而不知法祖以勤
民焉是初之不謹矣而能保其後之無悔也又
可得哉是則嗣德則能端本以善則矣虞始則
能因時以圖治矣後王盡斯道也於天下也何
有哉抑人臣事君貴防其漸君子脩德則愼于
微古之聖帝明王德業懋隆而為萬世法者凡
用是道焉耳太甲即位伊尹知其初志之未定
也而以虞始之道望之不可謂善于迪君而忠
===
愛之至矣乎後世人臣輔繼體之君者是可以
式矣
詩
夜如何其夜未央庭燎之光君子至止鸞
聲將將夜如何其夜未艾庭燎晣晣君
子至止鸞聲噦噦夜如何其夜鄕晨庭
燎有煇君子至止言觀其旂
同考試官敎諭宋 批 發明周王警惕之心宛然
punctuated:
而民心於玆而决其向背焉。保民圖治而致世道之雍熈者，在斯時也。失此而不知法祖以勤民焉，是初之不謹矣，而能保其後之無悔也，又可得哉？是則嗣德，則能端本以善則矣；虞始，則能因時以圖治矣。後王盡斯道也，於天下也何有哉？抑人臣事君，貴防其漸；君子脩德，則愼于微。古之聖帝明王，德業懋隆而為萬世法者，凡用是道焉耳。太甲即位，伊尹知其初志之未定也，而以虞始之道望之，不可謂善于迪君而忠愛之至矣乎？後世人臣輔繼體之君者，是可以式矣。

詩

夜如何其？夜未央，庭燎之光。君子至止，鸞聲將將。夜如何其？夜未艾，庭燎晣晣。君子至止，鸞聲噦噦。夜如何其？夜鄕晨，庭燎有煇。君子至止，言觀其旂。

同考試官敎諭宋 批：發明周王警惕之心，宛然
translation_en:
…and the people's hearts determine at this moment whether to give or withhold their allegiance. This is the time to protect the people, strive for good government, and bring the world into harmony and prosperity. If one lets this opportunity slip and fails to emulate one's ancestors in diligent care for the people, one has been incautious at the outset. How, then, could one ensure that no regrets follow? Thus, by carrying on ancestral virtue, one can set the foundations right and establish good standards; by taking thought for the beginning, one can act in accordance with the times to pursue good government. If later kings fully practice this Way, what difficulty will they have in governing all under Heaven? Moreover, in serving their ruler, ministers must guard against faults as they first develop; in cultivating virtue, the gentleman must be watchful over the smallest things. The sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity, whose virtue and achievements flourished so greatly that they became models for all ages, simply employed this Way. When Tai Jia ascended the throne, Yi Yin knew that his intentions were not yet settled, and expected him to follow the Way of taking thought for the beginning. Can this not be called skill in guiding a ruler, and the utmost loyalty and devotion? Ministers of later ages who assist rulers succeeding to the throne may take this as their model.

Book of Odes

How far has the night advanced? The night is not yet halfway through; the courtyard torches shine. The lords arrive, their carriage bells ringing out.
How far has the night advanced? The night is not yet spent; the courtyard torches blaze brightly. The lords arrive, their carriage bells chiming.
How far has the night advanced? The night approaches dawn; the courtyard torches give off a smoky glow. The lords arrive; one can see their banners.

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: It elucidates the Zhou king's vigilant and apprehensive state of mind, vividly …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
在目
同考試官教授唐批說出王者勤政意而詞不
纏擾宜錄以式
同考試官教授劉批詞理透徹
考試官教諭錙批發揮明盡
考試官教授熊批精確典雅渾然天成
觀賢王屢審視朝之期而警惕之心見矣蓋勵
精圖治人君之盛節也王者於視朝之期而屢
致其審焉警惕之心不可見乎想其意以君人
===
者萬化之原也憂勤者興王之本也故於將起
視朝之際不安於寢而問夜之早晚曰雞鳴而
起君臣會朝之時也今夜如何哉意者其未央
乎然庭燎之設已燦然其有光矣君子之鸞聲
已將將其載道矣即此推之殆不止於未央也
不然燎之光也鸞之鳴也何爲而遽有耶載寢
載興或者未可安乎儆戒之心未已恐晚之念
益勤又問之曰宵衣求理人君視朝之節也今
夜如何哉意者其未艾乎然庭燎之明乆而晣
punctuated:
在目。

同考試官教授唐批：說出王者勤政意，而詞不纏擾，宜錄以式。

同考試官教授劉批：詞理透徹。

考試官教諭錙批：發揮明盡。

考試官教授熊批：精確典雅，渾然天成。

觀賢王屢審視朝之期，而警惕之心見矣。蓋勵精圖治，人君之盛節也。王者於視朝之期而屢致其審焉，警惕之心不可見乎？想其意，以君人者，萬化之原也；憂勤者，興王之本也。故於將起視朝之際，不安於寢，而問夜之早晚，曰：「雞鳴而起，君臣會朝之時也。今夜如何哉？意者其未央乎？然庭燎之設，已燦然其有光矣；君子之鸞聲，已將將其載道矣。即此推之，殆不止於未央也。不然，燎之光也，鸞之鳴也，何爲而遽有耶？載寢載興，或者未可安乎？」儆戒之心未已，恐晚之念益勤，又問之曰：「宵衣求理，人君視朝之節也。今夜如何哉？意者其未艾乎？然庭燎之明，乆而晣
translation_en:
…before one’s eyes.

Associate Examiner Tang, a Prefectural School Professor, comments: “It expresses the king’s intention to attend diligently to government, without becoming tangled or prolix in its wording. It merits inclusion as a model.”

Associate Examiner Liu, a Prefectural School Professor, comments: “Thoroughly clear in both expression and reasoning.”

Examiner Zi [?], a County School Instructor, comments: “The exposition is clear and exhaustive.”

Examiner Xiong, a Prefectural School Professor, comments: “Precise and classically elegant, with a wholly natural coherence.”

Observe how the worthy king repeatedly ascertains the time for holding court: his vigilant mind is thereby revealed. Applying oneself wholeheartedly to achieving good government is a sovereign’s great virtue. When a king repeatedly takes care to ascertain the time for holding court, can we not discern his vigilance? We may imagine his thinking: the ruler of men is the source of all transforming influences, and anxious diligence is the foundation of flourishing kingship. Thus, as the time approaches to rise and hold court, he cannot rest easily in bed and asks how far the night has advanced, saying: “One rises at cockcrow; that is the time for ruler and ministers to assemble at court. How far has the night advanced now? Perhaps it has not yet reached its midpoint? Yet the torches set out in the courtyard already shine brightly, and the jingling of the gentlemen’s carriage bells already fills the roads. Judging from this, it must be past the middle of the night. Otherwise, why should the torches’ light and the ringing of the bells have appeared so soon? Lying down and rising again—perhaps I cannot yet rest at ease?”

His watchfulness does not cease, and his concern lest he be late grows still more pressing. Again he asks: “Dressing before dawn to seek good government is the proper discipline of a sovereign who holds court. How far has the night advanced now? Perhaps it is not yet over? Yet the courtyard torches have been burning for some time and shine brightly…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
晰矣君子之鸞近而噦噦矣即此推之殆不止
於未艾也不然燎之晰晰也鸞之噦噦也何爲
而遽變耶乃安乃寢或者可以興乎憂惕之意
愈深審候之言愈切又問之曰夜如何哉夜已
向晨而離明可見也庭燎有煇而煙光相雜也
斯時也君子之集於朝者無不萃其止矣龍旂
之建於車者可以辯其色矣事不可廢時之不
可失也尚可以甘寢乎是則由未央未艾以至
於鄕晨時以漸而移矣自一問再問以至於三
===
問心以漸而切矣憂勤惕勵之懷終夜弗寧如
此不觀有周王者孰知爲君之難乎說者謂此
爲宣王之詩夷考其時室家之聚見於無羊復
古之規見於車攻以至蒸民之任相采芑之任
將內治外嚴業稱中興則此詩之憂勤基之而
脫珥之助亦不可誣也雖然文之不遑暇食武
之以敬勝怠其心法之傳遠矣欲求帝王之盛
治者宜於此觀之
無念爾祖聿脩厥德
punctuated:
晰矣，君子之鸞近而噦噦矣。即此推之，殆不止於未艾也。不然，燎之晰晰也，鸞之噦噦也，何爲而遽變耶？乃安乃寢，或者可以興乎？」憂惕之意愈深，審候之言愈切，又問之曰：「夜如何哉？夜已向晨，而離明可見也。庭燎有煇，而煙光相雜也。斯時也，君子之集於朝者，無不萃其止矣；龍旂之建於車者，可以辯其色矣。事不可廢，時之不可失也，尚可以甘寢乎？」是則由未央、未艾，以至於鄕晨，時以漸而移矣；自一問、再問，以至於三問，心以漸而切矣。憂勤惕勵之懷，終夜弗寧如此，不觀有周王者，孰知爲君之難乎？說者謂此爲宣王之詩。夷考其時，室家之聚見於《無羊》，復古之規見於《車攻》，以至《蒸民》之任相、《采芑》之任將，內治外嚴，業稱中興，則此詩之憂勤基之，而脫珥之助亦不可誣也。雖然，文之不遑暇食，武之以敬勝怠，其心法之傳遠矣。欲求帝王之盛治者，宜於此觀之。

無念爾祖，聿脩厥德。
translation_en:
…clear, and the gentlemen’s carriage bells are drawing near, ringing out. Judging from this, surely the night has advanced beyond the point when it is not yet spent. Otherwise, why should the brightness of the torches and the ringing of the bells have changed so suddenly? Having settled down and slept, might it now be time to rise?” His anxious vigilance grows deeper, and his inquiries about the hour grow more urgent. Again he asks: “How far has the night advanced? Night is already approaching dawn, and the light of day is becoming visible. The courtyard torches give off a glow, their smoke mingling with their light. At this hour, the gentlemen assembling at court have all arrived at their places; the colors of the dragon banners mounted on their carriages can be distinguished. Affairs must not be neglected, nor the proper time missed. Can I still sleep soundly?” Thus, from the night’s being not yet half over, to its being not yet spent, and finally to approaching dawn, time gradually advances. From the first inquiry to the second and then the third, his concern grows steadily more urgent. His anxious diligence and vigilant resolve leave him no peace throughout the night. Without looking to the kings of Zhou, who could understand the difficulty of being a ruler?

Commentators say that this poem concerns King Xuan. Examining his age impartially, we find the gathering of households reflected in “No Sheep” (Wu yang), and the plans for restoring ancient institutions reflected in “Our Chariots Were Strong” (Che gong). Further, “The Multitude of the People” (Zheng min) concerns the appointment of a chief minister, and “Gathering the White Millet” (Cai qi) the appointment of a general. With good government within and strict military preparedness without, his achievements were acclaimed as a restoration. The anxious diligence expressed in this poem laid its foundation, and the assistance afforded by the removal of earrings—the queen’s act of remonstrance—cannot be denied. Nevertheless, King Wen’s having no leisure even to eat, and King Wu’s overcoming indolence through reverence, show how far back this teaching concerning the mind had been transmitted. Those who seek the flourishing government of emperors and kings should examine it here.

Be mindful of your ancestor; cultivate his virtue.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭宋批說理渾融措詞雅健經義
之佳者
同考試官教授唐批說周公進戒之意藹然溢
于言表
同考試官教授劉批詞不煩而意自足取之
考試官教諭錙批典實
考試官教授熊批雅鬯
大臣戒君以法祖亦惟自昭其德而已矣夫德
===
者凝命之本也嗣王之法祖舍脩德其奚以哉
此周公追述文王之德以戒成王至此蓋曰大
興王之業者固有開而必先守盈成之運者在
體志而無違是故假哉天命爾祖之德格天者
至矣爾荷申錫之慶得無駿惠之志乎侯服於
周爾祖之德得人者深矣爾承燕翼之休得無
繹思之心乎要必仰前脩以致愛念玆皇祖而
陟降之不忘也懷世德以作求永言孝思而羹
墻之如見也然念之也而豈徒哉亦惟脩德而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭宋批：說理渾融，措詞雅健，經義之佳者。
同考試官教授唐批：說周公進戒之意，藹然溢于言表。
同考試官教授劉批：詞不煩而意自足，取之。
考試官教諭錙批：典實。
考試官教授熊批：雅鬯。
大臣戒君以法祖，亦惟自昭其德而已矣。夫德者，凝命之本也。嗣王之法祖，舍脩德，其奚以哉？此周公追述文王之德以戒成王，至此蓋曰：大興王之業者，固有開而必先；守盈成之運者，在體志而無違。是故「假哉天命」，爾祖之德格天者至矣，爾荷申錫之慶，得無駿惠之志乎？「侯服於周」，爾祖之德得人者深矣，爾承燕翼之休，得無繹思之心乎？要必仰前脩以致愛，念玆皇祖而陟降之不忘也；懷世德以作求，永言孝思而羹墻之如見也。然念之也，而豈徒哉？亦惟脩德而
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Song, an Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is integrated and harmonious, and the wording elegant and vigorous: an excellent exposition of the meaning of the Classic.”

Associate Examiner Tang, a Professor, comments: “In explaining the intent of the Duke of Zhou’s admonition, a warmth of feeling abundantly shines through the words.”

Associate Examiner Liu, a Professor, comments: “The wording is concise, yet the meaning complete. Accept it.”

Examiner Zi [?], an Instructor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial.”

Examiner Xiong, a Professor, comments: “Elegant and lucid.”

When a great minister admonishes his ruler to emulate his ancestors, he asks only that the ruler himself make his virtue manifest. Virtue is the foundation for securing the Mandate. How could a succeeding king emulate his ancestors except by cultivating virtue? Here the Duke of Zhou recalls King Wen’s virtue to admonish King Cheng. At this point, his meaning is approximately this: in the great undertaking of establishing kingship, a founder must first open the way; preserving an era of flourishing accomplishment depends upon embodying his intentions without departing from them.

Thus, “Great indeed is Heaven’s Mandate”: your ancestor’s virtue reached Heaven to the utmost. Having received the blessing of its renewed bestowal, can you lack the resolve to follow him faithfully? “The lords submitted to Zhou”: your ancestor’s virtue won people’s allegiance profoundly. Having inherited the blessings of his provision for his descendants, can you lack a heart that reflects upon him continually? You must look up to the virtuous men of old with utmost love, remembering this august ancestor and never forgetting him as he ascends and descends. You must cherish the virtue of past generations and strive to carry it forward, constantly nurturing filial thoughts, as though seeing him before you in your soup and against the wall. Yet could such remembrance be merely an empty exercise? It consists only in cultivating virtue …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
已矣蓋德也者爾祖之所由以凝命而亦爾之
所賴以保命者也不脩其德命無自而保矣是
必兢業以自持而明德之懋昭者遠宗乎緝煕
之範時幾以自敕而天德之允迪者上遡乎敬
止之傳以端心法則翼翼恒存焉皇極之建獨
觀乎萬化之源務使祖以德而開國爾亦以德
而承家斯可矣以端身法則亹亹罔間焉道揆
之立懋建夫四方之極務使祖以德而垂統爾
亦以德而守成斯可矣如是則厥德允脩旣本
===
諸身而無愧則祖訓是式自質之先而有光上
以承靡常之天命者此也下以萃侯服之人心
者此也多福之求不於此而有本耶嗣王其念
之哉抑周公陳說於君獨舉文王受命之事諄
諄不置何耶蓋人君之德莫大於法天與法祖
法天則必思所以祈天永命之本法祖則必求
所以善繼善述之道他日成王學有緝煕基命
宥密卒能明文昭定武烈為有周令主嗚呼其
得於周公啓沃者深矣
punctuated:
已矣。蓋德也者，爾祖之所由以凝命，而亦爾之所賴以保命者也。不脩其德，命無自而保矣。是必兢業以自持，而明德之懋昭者，遠宗乎緝煕之範；時幾以自敕，而天德之允迪者，上遡乎敬止之傳。以端心法，則翼翼恒存焉，皇極之建，獨觀乎萬化之源，務使祖以德而開國，爾亦以德而承家，斯可矣；以端身法，則亹亹罔間焉，道揆之立，懋建夫四方之極，務使祖以德而垂統，爾亦以德而守成，斯可矣。如是，則厥德允脩，旣本諸身而無愧，則祖訓是式，自質之先而有光。上以承靡常之天命者，此也；下以萃侯服之人心者，此也。多福之求，不於此而有本耶？嗣王其念之哉！

抑周公陳說於君，獨舉文王受命之事，諄諄不置，何耶？蓋人君之德，莫大於法天與法祖。法天，則必思所以祈天永命之本；法祖，則必求所以善繼善述之道。他日成王學有緝煕，基命宥密，卒能明文昭、定武烈，為有周令主。嗚呼！其得於周公啓沃者深矣！
translation_en:
…and nothing more. For virtue is what enabled your ancestor to secure the Mandate, and it is also what you must rely upon to preserve it. Without cultivating virtue, there is no means of preserving the Mandate. You must therefore maintain yourself in vigilance and reverence: in striving to manifest your luminous virtue, follow the distant model of continuous illumination. Admonish yourself at each incipient moment [?]: in faithfully practicing Heaven’s virtue, trace your way back to the transmitted teaching of abiding in reverence. To rectify the discipline of your mind, preserve an ever-reverent attitude. In establishing the sovereign’s supreme standard, attend with singleness of purpose to the source of all transformations. Strive to ensure that, just as your ancestor founded the state through virtue, you too inherit the royal house through virtue: this will suffice. To rectify the discipline of your conduct, exert yourself tirelessly. In establishing the guiding principles of the Way, strive to set up a standard for the four quarters. Strive to ensure that, just as your ancestor handed down the succession through virtue, you too preserve his achievements through virtue: this will suffice.

In this way, your virtue will indeed be cultivated. Once it is rooted in your own person and leaves you nothing to be ashamed of, you will take your ancestor’s instructions as your model, and, submitting yourself for judgment before your forebears, bring them honor. This is how, above, you sustain Heaven’s inconstant Mandate; this is how, below, you gather together the hearts of those who serve as your feudatories. Does not the quest for manifold blessings have its foundation here? Let the succeeding king keep this in mind!

Yet why, in addressing his ruler, did the Duke of Zhou single out King Wen’s reception of the Mandate, earnestly expounding it without cease? Because no virtue of a ruler is greater than taking Heaven and his ancestors as models. In modeling himself on Heaven, he must consider the foundation upon which to pray to Heaven for an enduring Mandate. In modeling himself on his ancestors, he must seek the way to carry on their purposes and fulfill their undertakings well. In later days, King Cheng attained continuous illumination through learning and grounded the Mandate in broad and profound deliberation. Ultimately, he was able to make manifest King Wen’s glory and secure King Wu’s achievements, becoming an excellent ruler of Zhou. Ah! How profoundly he benefited from the Duke of Zhou’s enlightening instruction!

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
春秋
元年隱公元年春公會戎于潜隱公二年
同考試官教諭梅批講王德王道體用處氣格
渾成而傳意自見乃深於是經者
考試官教諭錙批點化體用處有典則
考試官教授熊批古雅
聖人脩經有紀元以明王德之體者有外戎以
明王道之用者夫德無不容道則有別王者所
===
以為體用也春秋紀元而外戎有以哉今夫王
人者中天地而主華夷者也不有以容天下則
無以昭理之一不有以別天下則無以明分之
殊是故於隱公首年之紀而見王德之體焉蓋
天下有大分量天地覆載是已此乾元以資始
稱大坤元以資生稱至易所以發其義也王者
體乾坤之元以為職其可以無容乎故疆域異
制雖不無內外之殊而華夷一統實有以擴包
荒之量中國吾蒞之也曰夏曰
punctuated:
春秋

「元年」，隱公元年。「春，公會戎于潜」，隱公二年。

同考試官教諭梅批：講王德、王道體用處，氣格渾成，而傳意自見，乃深於是經者。

考試官教諭錙批：點化體用處有典則。

考試官教授熊批：古雅。

聖人脩經，有紀元以明王德之體者，有外戎以明王道之用者。夫德無不容，道則有別，王者所以為體用也。《春秋》紀元而外戎，有以哉！今夫王人者，中天地而主華夷者也。不有以容天下，則無以昭理之一；不有以別天下，則無以明分之殊。是故於隱公首年之紀，而見王德之體焉。蓋天下有大分量，天地覆載是已。此乾元以資始稱大，坤元以資生稱至，《易》所以發其義也。王者體乾坤之元以為職，其可以無容乎？故疆域異制，雖不無內外之殊，而華夷一統，實有以擴包荒之量。中國吾蒞之也，曰夏曰
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“First year”—the first year of Duke Yin. “In spring, the duke met the Rong at Qian”—the second year of Duke Yin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Mei, Instructor: “In its discussion of the substance and functioning of royal virtue and the kingly Way, the essay’s spirit and style form an integrated whole, and the meaning of the commentarial tradition emerges naturally. Its author has a profound understanding of this classic.”

Comment by Examiner Zi [?], Instructor: “The illuminating treatment of substance and functioning follows established standards.”

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: “Classical and elegant.”

In editing the classic, the Sage designated the first year as yuan, ‘the beginning,’ to clarify the substance of royal virtue; he treated the Rong as outsiders to clarify the functioning of the kingly Way. Virtue embraces everything, whereas the Way makes distinctions: these constitute the substance and functioning of kingship. There is indeed a reason why the Spring and Autumn Annals records the beginning and treats the Rong as outsiders!

Now, one who rules over men [?] stands at the center of Heaven and Earth and presides over both the Hua and the Yi. Without embracing all under Heaven, he cannot manifest the unity of principle; without distinguishing among all under Heaven, he cannot make clear their differing stations. Thus, in the recording of Duke Yin’s first year, we see the substance of royal virtue.

There is a great capacity for embracing all under Heaven: Heaven’s covering and Earth’s bearing exemplify it. Thus the primal power of Qian is called ‘great’ because all things depend upon it for their beginnings, and the primal power of Kun is called ‘supreme’ because all things depend upon it for their birth. This is how the Book of Changes expounds that meaning. The king takes as his duty the embodiment of the primal powers of Qian and Kun. How could he fail to embrace all? Hence, although territories differ in their institutions and there are distinctions between inner and outer domains, the Hua and the Yi are united under one rule, thereby truly enlarging the capacity to embrace even the uncultivated. The Central States are what I govern; those called Xia and those called …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
夷莫不各得其所而德之渾然無間者固有洋
溢中國而施及蠻貊者矣其斯爲王者之體乎
春秋於隱公首年之紀而謂一爲元義蓋如此
其舜典紀元日商訓稱元祀之意歟於我公會
潛之戎而見王道之用焉蓋天下有大界限華
夷內外是已此內陽外陰爲泰內陰外陽爲否
易所以著其象也王者察否泰之幾以爲治其
可以無別乎故覆載所及雖欲竝生於化育之
中而政敎不加實當嚴斥於要荒之地中國吾
===
內之也四夷吾外之也曰夏曰夷莫不各止其
所而道之井然不紊者固有內則順治而外則
威嚴者矣其斯以爲王者之用乎春秋於隱公
會潛之戎而以號舉義蓋如此其大禹敘西戎
周公膺戎狄之意歟雖然無不覆載可也而以
天可汗自稱者失則亂經內夏外夷可也而使
幕南無王庭者失則黷武是皆不講於春秋之
義者也周禮九服之制職方氏掌之柔遠之典
懷方氏司之道德竝運體用不遺嗚呼盡之矣
punctuated:
夷，莫不各得其所，而德之渾然無間者，固有洋溢中國而施及蠻貊者矣。其斯爲王者之體乎？春秋於隱公首年之紀，而謂一爲元，義蓋如此。其舜典紀元日、商訓稱元祀之意歟？於我公會潛之戎，而見王道之用焉。蓋天下有大界限，華夷內外是已。此內陽外陰爲泰、內陰外陽爲否，易所以著其象也。王者察否泰之幾以爲治，其可以無別乎？故覆載所及，雖欲竝生於化育之中，而政敎不加，實當嚴斥於要荒之地。中國吾內之也，四夷吾外之也。曰夏曰夷，莫不各止其所，而道之井然不紊者，固有內則順治而外則威嚴者矣。其斯以爲王者之用乎？春秋於隱公會潛之戎，而以號舉，義蓋如此。其大禹敘西戎、周公膺戎狄之意歟？

雖然，無不覆載可也，而以天可汗自稱者，失則亂經；內夏外夷可也，而使幕南無王庭者，失則黷武。是皆不講於春秋之義者也。周禮九服之制，職方氏掌之；柔遠之典，懷方氏司之。道德竝運，體用不遺。嗚呼，盡之矣！
translation_en:
…Yi peoples: all obtain their proper place. This virtue, whole and undivided, indeed overflows throughout the Central States and extends even to the Man and Mo peoples. Is this not the fundamental substance of true kingship? Such, broadly, is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals calling the first year “the inaugural year” (yuan) in its record of Duke Yin’s opening year. Is this not also the intent of the Canon of Shun in recording “the inaugural day,” and of the Instructions of Shang in speaking of “the inaugural year of sacrifice”?

In the Rong whom our duke met at Qian, we see the operation of the kingly Way. For the world has a great boundary: that between Hua and Yi, inner and outer. This is what the Changes makes manifest through its images: yang within and yin without constitute Peace (Tai); yin within and yang without constitute Obstruction (Pi). A true king governs by discerning the incipient tendencies toward Obstruction and Peace. How could he dispense with distinctions? Thus, although he wishes all within heaven’s covering and earth’s support to live together amid their transforming and nurturing influence, those whom his governance and instruction do not reach must indeed be strictly kept apart in the remote outer domains. The Central States we treat as within; the Yi of the four directions we treat as without. Whether called Xia or Yi, all remain in their proper places. This Way, orderly and unconfused, indeed brings harmonious government within and imposing authority without. Is this not the operation of true kingship? Such, broadly, is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals identifying by their collective designation the Rong whom Duke Yin met at Qian. Is this not also the intent of Yu the Great in ordering the Western Rong, and of the Duke of Zhou in subduing the Rong and Di?

Nevertheless, it is right to shelter and sustain all without exception; but to style oneself “Heavenly Qaghan” is to err by subverting the normative order. It is right to treat the Xia as within and the Yi as without; but to leave no royal court south of the desert is to err through wanton warfare. These are all failures to understand the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals. In the Rites of Zhou, the Director of Territorial Administration administers the system of nine service zones, while the Conciliator of Regions oversees the rules for conciliating distant peoples. The Way and virtue operate together; neither substance nor function is neglected. Ah, how complete it is!

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
然則春秋之法其周公之志乎故曰孔子欲行
周公之道
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈季孫斯仲孫何忌
帥師墮費十有二月公圍成公至自
圍成俱定公十有二年
同考試官教諭梅批以禮政二字發揮聖人用
魯甚是
考試官教諭錙批詞嚴意雋
===
考試官教授熊批莊重
卽望國革僣有從違而其機皆决於聖人焉甚
矣聖人有𮗚於魯甚大也為國以禮而得政未
朞此三邑之墮所以有從違歟且郈費成者何
三家之邑也其城之以自固也久矣迺定公十
有二年者州仇倡之於先斯忌隨之於後將以
上卿帥以大衆而郈費於是迭墮焉魯何以得
此於二氏哉君子曰其聖人為國之以禮乎禮
國之坊也是經世之大本也大夫植私以固其
punctuated:
然則《春秋》之法，其周公之志乎？故曰：「孔子欲行周公之道。」
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈，季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。十有二月，公圍成。公至自圍成。俱定公十有二年。
同考試官教諭梅批：「以禮政二字發揮聖人用魯，甚是。」
考試官教諭錙批：「詞嚴意雋。」
考試官教授熊批：「莊重。」
卽望國革僣，有從違，而其機皆决於聖人焉。甚矣，聖人有𮗚於魯甚大也！為國以禮，而得政未朞，此三邑之墮所以有從違歟？且郈、費、成者何？三家之邑也。其城之以自固也久矣。迺定公十有二年者，州仇倡之於先，斯、忌隨之於後，將以上卿，帥以大衆，而郈、費於是迭墮焉。魯何以得此於二氏哉？君子曰：「其聖人為國之以禮乎！」禮，國之坊也，是經世之大本也。大夫植私以固其
translation_en:
…Then are the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals the intentions of the Duke of Zhou? Hence the saying: “Confucius wished to put the Duke of Zhou’s Way into practice.”
“Shusun Zhouchou led an army to demolish the fortifications of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the fortifications of Bi. In the twelfth month, the duke besieged Cheng. The duke returned from besieging Cheng.” All these entries belong to the twelfth year of Duke Ding.
Associate Examiner Mei, an Instructor, comments: “Using the two terms ‘ritual’ and ‘government’ to elucidate the sage’s exercise of authority in Lu is most apt.”
Examiner Zi [?], an Instructor, comments: “The language is rigorous and the meaning profound.”
Examiner Xiong, a Professor, comments: “Dignified and weighty.”
In a prestigious state, the elimination of usurpations [?] met with both compliance and resistance, yet the impulse behind it all was determined by the sage. How far-reaching was the sage’s vision for Lu! He governed the state through ritual, but had held political authority for less than a full year. Was this why the demolition of the three towns’ fortifications met with both compliance and resistance? What, then, were Hou, Bi, and Cheng? They were the towns of the three great families. Those families had long fortified them to secure their own positions. Then, in the twelfth year of Duke Ding, Zhouchou took the initiative, and Si and Heji followed. With senior ministers as commanders and large bodies of troops under their command, the fortifications of Hou and Bi were demolished in succession. How did Lu obtain this cooperation from the two families? The gentleman says: “Was it not because the sage governed the state through ritual?” Ritual is the state’s protective barrier and the great foundation of ordering the world. The grandees cultivated their private interests to strengthen their…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
城陪臣效尤以逆其主此其患亦已極矣而聖
人者以先王治世之禮律我魯衰世之臣不曰
家不藏甲則曰邑無百雉二氏之同心以相從
也此其機之相感者也非聖人而能若是乎郈
費墮則成當從矣夫何我公圍之也其攻也若
敵國其返也若外至邑强於下主危於上而成
於是獨不墮焉魯何以致此於孟氏哉君子曰
其聖人得政之未專乎政國之柄也定用世之
大權也行乎季孫而三月不違墮乎名城而二
===
家效順此其兆足以行矣而聖人者顧專得魯
政之未能則辯言亂政之猶在不曰子僞不知
則曰我將不墮孟氏之違二家以相抗也此其
機之相悖者也使魯專用聖人而豈至是乎是
故二邑之墮吾不曰二氏而曰孔子成邑之不
墮吾不曰孔子而曰定公蓋其所能者人也其
所不能者天也聖人如彼何哉雖然此未足以
爲夫子病也昔舜伐苗弗克至班師脩德而後
格焉則以用大禹之言也使魯終用孔子而需
punctuated: 城，陪臣效尤以逆其主，此其患亦已極矣。而聖人者，以先王治世之禮律我魯衰世之臣，不曰「家不藏甲」，則曰「邑無百雉」。二氏之同心以相從也，此其機之相感者也。非聖人而能若是乎？郈費墮，則成當從矣。夫何我公圍之也？其攻也若敵國，其返也若外至。邑强於下，主危於上，而成於是獨不墮焉。魯何以致此於孟氏哉？君子曰：「其聖人得政之未專乎？」政，國之柄也，定用世之大權也。行乎季孫而三月不違，墮乎名城而二家效順，此其兆足以行矣。而聖人者，顧專得魯政之未能，則辯言亂政之猶在，不曰「子僞不知」，則曰「我將不墮」。孟氏之違二家以相抗也，此其機之相悖者也。使魯專用聖人，而豈至是乎？是故二邑之墮，吾不曰二氏而曰孔子；成邑之不墮，吾不曰孔子而曰定公。蓋其所能者，人也；其所不能者，天也。聖人如彼何哉？雖然，此未足以爲夫子病也。昔舜伐苗弗克，至班師脩德而後格焉，則以用大禹之言也。使魯終用孔子而需
translation_en: …their walls, while their retainers followed their example and defied their own masters: the trouble had already reached its extreme. Yet the sage applied the rites with which the former kings had governed an orderly age to the ministers of our Lu in an age of decline. He would say either, “A ministerial household must not store armor,” or, “A dependent town must not have walls a hundred zhi in extent.” That the two clans united in following him arose from their responsive accord at this critical juncture. Could anyone but the sage have achieved this? Once the walls of Hou and Fei were demolished, Cheng should have followed. Why, then, did our duke have to besiege it? His attack resembled an attack upon an enemy state; his return resembled a return from abroad. The dependent town was powerful below, while its lord was endangered above, and Cheng alone consequently remained undemolished. How had Lu come to this with the Meng clan? The gentleman says, “Was it because the sage had not yet obtained sole authority over government?” Government is the controlling handle of the state, the great authority that determines how one acts in the world. His policies were put into practice through Jisun, who did not depart from them for three months; the walls of renowned strongholds were demolished, and the two clans submitted. These signs were sufficient grounds for proceeding. Yet the sage had still been unable to obtain sole control over Lu’s government, and so those who disrupted government with specious arguments remained. They would say either, “You should pretend not to know,” or, “I shall not demolish the walls.” That the Meng clan opposed the two other clans and resisted arose from their contrary impulses at this critical juncture. Had Lu entrusted affairs entirely to the sage, could matters have reached this point? Thus, for the demolition of the two towns’ walls, I credit not the two clans but Confucius; for the failure to demolish Cheng’s walls, I blame not Confucius but Duke Ding. What the sage could accomplish lay within human agency; what he could not accomplish lay with Heaven. What could the sage do about that? Nevertheless, this is insufficient grounds for finding fault with the Master. In ancient times, Shun attacked the Miao but failed to overcome them. Only after withdrawing his army and cultivating virtue did he bring them to submission, because he followed the words of Yu the Great. Had Lu employed Confucius to the end and waited…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
以歲月則感德格心成將不兵自墮矣惜乎孔
子有大禹之德而其君不舜焉女樂受而冕且
不暇脫矣安望其從容以終革僭之功哉噫此
君子所以爲魯慨也
禮記
律小大之稱比始終之序以象事行
同考試官教諭陳批象事行衆多體認未真而
詞涉浮晦惟此作就題發揮明暢典實可取
===
考試官教諭鎦批深得題意佳士也取之
考試官教授熊批典贍
樂得其節而理因寓焉可以觀其義之深矣甚
矣樂通倫理者也先王廣樂以教人而寓事行
於法象焉其義不亦深乎樂記君子之意蓋曰
先王作樂其始也固原于本文之具備其既也
尤妙於感化之及人則夫廣樂以成教於天下
豈止於繩德厚哉彼樂音有大小其辨分於損
益之異數者本若是乎不齊也今則以法度整
punctuated:
以歲月，則感德格心，成將不兵自墮矣。惜乎！孔子有大禹之德，而其君不舜焉。女樂受，而冕且不暇脫矣，安望其從容以終革僭之功哉？噫！此君子所以爲魯慨也。
禮記
律小大之稱，比始終之序，以象事行。
同考試官教諭陳批：象事行，衆多體認未真，而詞涉浮晦。惟此作就題發揮，明暢典實，可取。
考試官教諭鎦批：深得題意，佳士也，取之。
考試官教授熊批：典贍。
樂得其節，而理因寓焉，可以觀其義之深矣。甚矣，樂通倫理者也！先王廣樂以教人，而寓事行於法象焉，其義不亦深乎？樂記君子之意，蓋曰：先王作樂，其始也，固原于本文之具備；其既也，尤妙於感化之及人。則夫廣樂以成教於天下，豈止於繩德厚哉？彼樂音有大小，其辨分於損益之異數者，本若是乎不齊也。今則以法度整
translation_en:
…given time, their hearts would have been moved by his virtue and brought into accord, and Cheng would have dismantled its fortifications of its own accord, without military action. Alas! Confucius possessed the virtue of Yu the Great, but his ruler was no Shun. Once the female musicians were accepted, he had not even the leisure to remove his ceremonial cap before departing. How could one expect him to complete at ease the work of eliminating usurpation? Ah! This is why the gentleman laments the fate of Lu.
Book of Rites
“Regulate the proportion between the small and the great, arrange the sequence of beginning and end, and thereby represent affairs and conduct.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Many candidates have failed truly to grasp “represent affairs and conduct,” and their language tends toward superficiality and obscurity. This essay alone develops the topic clearly and fluently, with classical grounding and substance. It merits selection.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: He has grasped the topic’s meaning deeply. A fine scholar: select him.
Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: Classically grounded and rich in substance.
When music attains its proper measure, principle resides within it: here one can perceive the depth of its meaning. How profoundly music accords with ethical relationships! The former kings extended music to teach the people, lodging affairs and conduct within its rules and representations. Is its meaning not profound? The intent of the gentleman who composed the Record of Music was, surely, this: when the former kings created music, its inception was rooted in the completeness of both its fundamental substance and its patterned expression; once completed, its particular subtlety lay in the transformative influence it exerted upon people. Thus, in extending music to accomplish the teaching of all under Heaven, how could their purpose have been merely to take abundant virtue as their standard? Musical tones differ in magnitude. Their distinctions, determined by differing numerical measures of diminution and augmentation, are inherently unequal in this way. Now, however, they are regulated by established rules …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
齊之羽音至小使宫之大者無相凌奪焉而商
而角猶是也宫音至大使羽之小者無相凌僭
焉而徵而商猶是也斯則整飭以恊其宜若有
所配合而彼此之相稱矣非律小大之稱矣乎
樂音有始終其辨析於先後之異宜者本若是
乎不紊也今則以次序聯合之始於黃鍾而非
止於黃鍾焉他律亦以次而相應終於仲吕而
非止於仲吕焉其次亦循環而無端斯則播比
以聯其間若有所嗣續而先後之互根矣非比
===
始終之序矣乎夫樂得其節如此是豈徒爲娱
樂之具哉止以法象其事之所行耳蓋事行皆
倫理所寓其初固隱於難知也今則器數之中
秩然不亂而以類聚者以羣分自莫掩其得失
之彰節奏之內皦然不雜而以統同者以辨異
自各歸其善惡之分不惟八音克諧無相奪倫
者吾得而知之也事之所施或有自從於匪彝
者亦必於小大之稱見之矣有能自遁其情哉
不惟正聲感人順氣成象者吾得而知之也行
punctuated: 齊之。羽音至小，使宫之大者無相凌奪焉，而商而角猶是也；宫音至大，使羽之小者無相凌僭焉，而徵而商猶是也。斯則整飭以恊其宜，若有所配合而彼此之相稱矣，非律小大之稱矣乎？樂音有始終，其辨析於先後之異宜者，本若是乎不紊也。今則以次序聯合之，始於黃鍾而非止於黃鍾焉，他律亦以次而相應；終於仲吕而非止於仲吕焉，其次亦循環而無端。斯則播比以聯其間，若有所嗣續而先後之互根矣，非比始終之序矣乎？夫樂得其節如此，是豈徒爲娛樂之具哉？止以法象其事之所行耳。蓋事行皆倫理所寓，其初固隱於難知也。今則器數之中，秩然不亂，而以類聚者以羣分，自莫掩其得失之彰；節奏之內，皦然不雜，而以統同者以辨異，自各歸其善惡之分。不惟八音克諧、無相奪倫者，吾得而知之也；事之所施，或有自從於匪彝者，亦必於小大之稱見之矣，有能自遁其情哉？不惟正聲感人、順氣成象者，吾得而知之也；行
translation_en: …bring them into alignment. The yu tone is the smallest: the greater gong tone is kept from overpowering and displacing it, and the same applies to shang and jue. The gong tone is the greatest: the smaller yu tone is kept from encroaching upon and usurping its place, and the same applies to zhi and shang. Thus they are regulated to accord with what is fitting, as though matched together so that each is proportionate to the others. Is this not regulating the proper proportions of the small and the great? Musical tones have beginnings and endings. Their distinctions, according to the different requirements of what comes earlier and later, are inherently thus free from disorder. Now they are joined in sequence. They begin with Huangzhong, the Yellow Bell pitch, but do not stop there: the other pitches respond in turn. They end with Zhonglü, the Middle Regulator pitch, but do not stop there either: their succession also revolves without end. Thus they are arrayed and coordinated to connect the intervals between them, as though continuing one another, with earlier and later mutually rooted in each other. Is this not coordinating the sequence of beginning and end? When music attains its proper measure in this way, could it be merely an instrument of amusement? It serves to model and represent the carrying out of affairs. For affairs and conduct alike embody ethical relationships and principles, which are at first concealed and difficult to discern. Now, within the instruments and their numerical arrangements, there is orderly arrangement without confusion; things gathered by kind are divided into groups, and the evident distinction between what is right and what is wrong cannot be concealed. Within the rhythms, there is clarity without admixture; what is united through commonality is distinguished through difference, and each finds its place in the division between good and evil. It is not only that I can recognize how the eight classes of musical sound harmonize without disrupting one another’s proper order. If, in the conduct of affairs, anything departs from the constant norms, it too must become apparent in the proportions of the small and the great. Could its true character escape detection? It is not only that I can recognize how correct sounds move people and harmonious vital energies take visible form. As for conduct…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
之所成或有自入於回邪者亦必於始終之序
見之矣有能自掩其微哉謂之曰以象事行信
乎存之則爲倫理發之則爲事行越之聲音則
爲大樂其感人動物一至此也樂之所觀不旣
深乎雖然此特自其樂之感化言之耳究其原
則根之性情以端其本歸於天人以達其和玆
所以致率神敦和樂行倫清之化而後有作者
弗可及已後世不知出此乃徒求竘應於鍾律
之間察高下於絲竹之末導欲增悲正樂亡而
===
天下無風俗矣惜哉
禮之於正國也猶衡之於輕重也繩墨之
於曲直也規矩之於方圜也
同考試官教諭陳 批 此題認引喻看者非是惟
此作通就禮上說而規格詞氣俱有可觀宜錄以式
考試官教諭鎦 批 衡繩墨等處講甚得體
考試官教授熊 批 詞理兩備非苟作者
記者論禮切於治國以示君子之當審也甚矣
punctuated:
之所成，或有自入於回邪者，亦必於始終之序見之矣，有能自掩其微哉？謂之曰「以象事行」，信乎！存之則爲倫理，發之則爲事行，越之聲音則爲大樂。其感人動物，一至此也，樂之所觀不旣深乎？雖然，此特自其樂之感化言之耳。究其原，則根之性情以端其本，歸於天人以達其和。玆所以致率神敦和、樂行倫清之化，而後有作者弗可及已。後世不知出此，乃徒求竘應於鍾律之間，察高下於絲竹之末，導欲增悲，正樂亡而天下無風俗矣。惜哉！

禮之於正國也，猶衡之於輕重也，繩墨之於曲直也，規矩之於方圜也。

同考試官教諭陳批：此題認引喻看者非是，惟此作通就禮上說，而規格詞氣俱有可觀，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭鎦批：衡、繩墨等處，講甚得體。
考試官教授熊批：詞理兩備，非苟作者。

記者論禮切於治國，以示君子之當審也。甚矣，
translation_en:
…what conduct brings about: if any of it strays into perversity, this too will necessarily become apparent in the ordering of the beginning and end. Can anyone conceal its subtleties? How true it is to say that music “represents affairs and conduct”! Preserved within, it constitutes ethical relationships; expressed outwardly, it constitutes affairs and conduct; issued in sounds, it constitutes great music. Its power to move people and stir other beings reaches such an extent. Does not music offer profound insight?

Yet this speaks only of music’s transformative influence. If we investigate its source, it is rooted in human nature and feelings, thereby rectifying its foundation; it returns to Heaven and humanity, thereby achieving harmony. This is how it brings about a transformation that draws the spirits together and deepens harmony, in which music prevails and ethical relationships become clear. Later composers could never equal this achievement. Subsequent generations did not understand how to proceed from this source. They merely sought correspondence [?] among bells and pitch standards and examined high and low notes in the peripheral details of strings and pipes, encouraging desire and increasing sorrow. Correct music vanished, and the world lost its proper customs. Alas!

“Ritual, in rectifying the state, is like the balance in determining weight, the carpenter’s inked cord in determining crookedness and straightness, and the compass and square in determining squareness and roundness.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Those who treat this topic as a matter of drawing analogies are mistaken. This composition alone discusses ritual throughout, and its form, diction, and tone all have merit. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The passages concerning the balance, inked cord, and so forth are explained very aptly.”

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished. This is no carelessly written composition.”

The recorder discusses ritual’s essential bearing on governing the state, to show that the gentleman must examine it carefully. How great indeed …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
禮為治國之本也觀器以利用而禮之所關亦
大矣君子可不審所尚哉見於經解者若謂君
人之道在能治其國而已矣治國之要在能謹
於禮而已矣是禮也豈曰器數之末無關於治
道已哉蓋其本之天然自有之中而品節詳明
誠為軌衆齊物之具達為中正無邪之理而經
制大備允為治世宰物之宜脩諸朝廷之上而
經緯有章則出入起居由之終身而不可斯須
去焉形諸邦國之間而軌物不亂則辨分定志
===
資以周旋而不可頃刻離焉擬而議之其諸器
之可以前民用者乎蓋禮有大小與物之有輕
重一也以禮正國則大者不可損有以飾亨嘉
之會小者不可益有以崇白賁之規其視衡之
稱物低昂屢變而不失其平者無異矣是禮其
正國之衡也哉禮有煩簡與物之有曲直一也
以禮正國則煩者從其煩式示多儀之美簡者
從其簡不失要約之歸其視繩墨之準物卷舒
有定而各得其宜者無異矣是禮其正國之繩
punctuated: 禮為治國之本也！觀器以利用，而禮之所關亦大矣，君子可不審所尚哉？見於經解者，若謂君人之道，在能治其國而已矣；治國之要，在能謹於禮而已矣。是禮也，豈曰器數之末，無關於治道已哉？蓋其本之天然自有之中，而品節詳明，誠為軌衆齊物之具；達為中正無邪之理，而經制大備，允為治世宰物之宜。脩諸朝廷之上，而經緯有章，則出入起居由之，終身而不可斯須去焉；形諸邦國之間，而軌物不亂，則辨分定志，資以周旋，而不可頃刻離焉。擬而議之，其諸器之可以前民用者乎？蓋禮有大小，與物之有輕重一也。以禮正國，則大者不可損，有以飾亨嘉之會；小者不可益，有以崇白賁之規。其視衡之稱物，低昂屢變而不失其平者，無異矣。是禮其正國之衡也哉！禮有煩簡，與物之有曲直一也。以禮正國，則煩者從其煩，式示多儀之美；簡者從其簡，不失要約之歸。其視繩墨之準物，卷舒有定而各得其宜者，無異矣。是禮其正國之繩
translation_en:
…ritual is the foundation of governing a state! When we consider instruments that facilitate practical use, we see that what ritual bears upon is likewise momentous. Can the gentleman fail to examine carefully what he esteems? The passage in “Explanations of the Classics” seems to say that the way of ruling people consists simply in being able to govern one's state, and that the essential requirement for governing a state consists simply in attending carefully to ritual. Can ritual, then, be dismissed as the minutiae of ceremonial vessels and numerical prescriptions, unrelated to the way of government?

Rooted in the mean inherent in the natural order, with its distinctions and regulations clearly articulated, ritual truly provides the means to guide the multitude and bring things into order. Expressed as principles of centrality and correctness, free from deviation, and fully furnished with institutions and regulations, it is indeed suited to governing the age and directing affairs. Cultivated at court, where its ordering patterns are clearly defined, it guides one's movements and daily conduct throughout life and cannot be set aside even for an instant. Manifested among the states, where norms and observances remain orderly, it distinguishes social stations and settles people's purposes; they rely upon it in their dealings and cannot depart from it for a moment. If we consider it by analogy, is it not like the instruments that guide the people's practical activities?

Ritual has greater and lesser forms, just as objects have differing weights. When ritual is used to set the state right, its greater forms must not be diminished, thereby providing the adornment appropriate to gatherings of flourishing excellence; its lesser forms must not be augmented, thereby honoring the standard of unadorned simplicity. This is no different from a balance weighing objects: though it repeatedly rises and falls, it never loses its equilibrium. Is ritual not, then, the balance for setting the state right?

Ritual has elaborate and simple forms, just as objects may be crooked or straight. When ritual is used to set the state right, elaborate forms retain their elaboration, displaying the beauty of manifold observances; simple forms retain their simplicity, preserving their essential concision. This is no different from an inked marking line used to gauge objects: its winding and unwinding follow a fixed standard, and each application is appropriate. Is ritual not, then, the marking line for setting the state…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
墨也哉禮有常變與物之有方圜一也國而有
禮則可以體常而守經以立本可以盡變而行
權以趨時誠猶用規以爲圜而圜不至於苦窳
用矩以爲方而方不至於不觚者矣禮非正國
之規矩矣乎夫知物之有資於器則知國之有
資於禮矣知器之爲萬物式則知禮之爲萬民
式矣信乎安上治民莫善於禮而隆禮由禮固
存乎人焉耳彼以虛文視之者謂之何哉然則
隆而由之宜何如亦曰盡其敬讓之道而已蓋
===
敬讓呀本諸心者也無體之禮也吾能先以是存
諸心而流深於制作則惟吾所施可以持情合
危可以同民强世而多變之人情亦將就吾條
理而不亂矣否則出乎身加乎民將有千里之
外違之者況望其能正國乎哉故曰有純王之
心而後有純王之政詎不信夫
第貳場
論
孔子太和元氣
punctuated:
墨也哉！禮有常變，與物之有方圜一也。國而有禮，則可以體常而守經以立本，可以盡變而行權以趨時。誠猶用規以爲圜，而圜不至於苦窳；用矩以爲方，而方不至於不觚者矣。禮非正國之規矩矣乎？夫知物之有資於器，則知國之有資於禮矣；知器之爲萬物式，則知禮之爲萬民式矣。信乎，安上治民莫善於禮，而隆禮由禮，固存乎人焉耳。彼以虛文視之者，謂之何哉？然則隆而由之，宜何如？亦曰盡其敬讓之道而已。蓋敬讓呀，本諸心者也，無體之禮也。吾能先以是存諸心，而流深於制作，則惟吾所施，可以持情合危，可以同民强世，而多變之人情，亦將就吾條理而不亂矣。否則，出乎身，加乎民，將有千里之外違之者，況望其能正國乎哉？故曰：「有純王之心，而後有純王之政。」詎不信夫！

第貳場

論

孔子太和元氣
translation_en:
…and ink-line for setting the state in order!

Ritual has its constants and its adaptations, just as objects have square and round forms. When a state possesses ritual, it can embody the constant and uphold enduring norms to establish its foundation; it can also respond fully to change and exercise discretion to suit the times. This is truly like using a compass to make a circle without its becoming misshapen, or using a square to make a square without its losing its corners. Is ritual not the compass and square for setting the state in order?

To understand that objects depend upon tools is to understand that the state depends upon ritual. To understand that tools provide standards for all objects is to understand that ritual provides standards for all the people. Truly, nothing surpasses ritual in securing those above and governing the people; yet honoring ritual and following it ultimately depend upon human beings. What can those who regard it as empty formalities say to this? How, then, should one honor and follow it? Simply by fully realizing the way of reverence and deference.

For reverence and deference [?] are rooted in the heart: they are ritual without outward form. If I can first preserve these in my heart and let them permeate the establishment of institutions [?], then whatever I put into practice can regulate feelings and bring peril into harmony [?], unite the people, and strengthen the age. Even the ever-changing feelings of human beings will come within my ordering principles and cease to be unruly. Otherwise, what proceeds from oneself and is imposed upon the people will meet with resistance a thousand li away. How much less could one hope that it would set the state in order? Thus it is said: “Only after possessing the heart of a true king can one have the government of a true king.” Is this not indeed true!

Second Session

Discourse

Confucius as the Primordial Vital Force of Supreme Harmony

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張批體格俊偉辭氣暢裕博大
春融有如元氣周流渾然無迹秩然有條宜錄以式
同考試官教諭張批推明孔子太和元氣之義
以神化一貫時中作主可謂善發聖人天道之蘊者
考試官教諭鎦批措詞雅健議論精詳
考試官教授熊批議論醇正
聖人之道天道也天之道何道也流行者其化
也充周者其神也神不可測體之所以立也其
===
在聖人則爲存主之心焉化不容間用之所以
行也其在聖人則爲妙應之事焉是心也是事
也聖人之所同也顧道有偏全分有多寡一念
之純皆聖人之心也而非所以語莫測之體一
節之高皆聖人之事也而非所以語無間之化
猶之四時之序莫非天道之所在要之默運於
太虛之中而神不可測流通於四序之內而化
不容間則太和元氣之所以爲妙也是故四時
莫不有元氣各具一太極也元氣流行於四時
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張批：體格俊偉，辭氣暢裕，博大春融，有如元氣周流，渾然無迹，秩然有條，宜錄以式。

同考試官教諭張批：推明孔子太和元氣之義，以神化一貫、時中作主，可謂善發聖人天道之蘊者。

考試官教諭鎦批：措詞雅健，議論精詳。

考試官教授熊批：議論醇正。

聖人之道，天道也。天之道，何道也？流行者其化也，充周者其神也。神不可測，體之所以立也；其在聖人，則爲存主之心焉。化不容間，用之所以行也；其在聖人，則爲妙應之事焉。是心也，是事也，聖人之所同也。顧道有偏全，分有多寡。一念之純，皆聖人之心也，而非所以語莫測之體；一節之高，皆聖人之事也，而非所以語無間之化。猶之四時之序，莫非天道之所在。要之，默運於太虛之中而神不可測，流通於四序之內而化不容間，則太和元氣之所以爲妙也。是故四時莫不有元氣，各具一太極也；元氣流行於四時，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Its form is distinguished and grand; its language flows freely and amply. Expansive and suffused with the warmth of spring, it resembles primal vital energy circulating everywhere: an integrated whole without visible traces, yet orderly in its structure. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: It elucidates the meaning of Confucius as the primal vital energy of Great Harmony, taking as its guiding principles the unity of spiritual efficacy and transformation, and accordance with the mean as circumstances require. It may be said to reveal skillfully the profundities of the sage and the Way of Heaven.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The phrasing is elegant and vigorous; the argument is precise and thorough.

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: The argument is pure and orthodox.

The Way of the sage is the Way of Heaven. What is the Way of Heaven? What flows and moves is its transformation; what fills and pervades is its spiritual efficacy. Spiritual efficacy is unfathomable: through it, substance is established. In the sage, it is the mind that preserves and presides. Transformation admits no interruption: through it, function operates. In the sage, it is the activity of responding wondrously to circumstances. This mind and this activity are common to sages. Yet their embodiment of the Way may be partial or complete, and their allotted share greater or smaller. A single pure thought is in every case the mind of a sage, but it does not suffice to describe unfathomable substance. A single instance of lofty conduct is in every case the activity of a sage, but it does not suffice to describe uninterrupted transformation. It is like the succession of the four seasons: there is none in which the Way of Heaven is not present. Ultimately, silently operating within the Great Void with unfathomable spiritual efficacy, and circulating through the four seasons with uninterrupted transformation—this is what makes the primal vital energy of Great Harmony wondrous. Thus none of the four seasons lacks primal vital energy: each possesses a Supreme Ultimate in itself. Primal vital energy flows through the four seasons …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
統體一太極也則夫合聖人之心而幾緘之不
露是卽元氣之蘊四時之所統也所謂神之不
可測者此也合聖人之事而時出之不窮是卽
四時之行元氣之所運也所謂化之不容間者
此也分之爲萬善之各足合之爲一理之完具
此孔子所以爲太和元氣之流行於四時而非
伯夷伊尹柳下惠之若是班也請因朱子之言
而論之易曰大哉乾元萬物資始至哉坤元萬
物資生此元氣之說所由始也又曰乾道變化
===
各正性命保合太和乃利貞此太和之說所由
始也是氣也根柢於無物之先而流通於有物
之後自此氣之動也則爲春而萬物以生自此
氣之暢也則爲夏而萬物以長自此氣之斂也
則爲秋自此氣之肅也則爲冬而萬物以收萬
物以藏人見夫春之主於生而不能長不能收
不能藏也以爲春有春之氣耳而不知春之氣
卽夏之氣秋之氣冬之氣也流行於春則爲春
耳人見夫夏之主於長而不能生不能收不能
punctuated: 統體一太極也。則夫合聖人之心，而幾緘之不露，是卽元氣之蘊，四時之所統也。所謂神之不可測者，此也。合聖人之事，而時出之不窮，是卽四時之行，元氣之所運也。所謂化之不容間者，此也。分之爲萬善之各足，合之爲一理之完具。此孔子所以爲太和元氣之流行於四時，而非伯夷、伊尹、柳下惠之若是班也。請因朱子之言而論之。《易》曰：「大哉乾元，萬物資始！至哉坤元，萬物資生！」此元氣之說所由始也。又曰：「乾道變化，各正性命，保合太和，乃利貞。」此太和之說所由始也。是氣也，根柢於無物之先，而流通於有物之後。自此氣之動也，則爲春，而萬物以生；自此氣之暢也，則爲夏，而萬物以長；自此氣之斂也，則爲秋；自此氣之肅也，則爲冬，而萬物以收，萬物以藏。人見夫春之主於生，而不能長，不能收，不能藏也，以爲春有春之氣耳，而不知春之氣卽夏之氣、秋之氣、冬之氣也，流行於春則爲春耳。人見夫夏之主於長，而不能生，不能收，不能
translation_en: …taken as a whole, it is one Supreme Ultimate. Thus, considered in its entirety, the sage’s mind keeps its incipient workings concealed and unexposed [?]: this is precisely primordial vital energy held in reserve, that which unifies the four seasons. This is what is meant by the unfathomability of spiritual efficacy. Considered in their entirety, the sage’s deeds emerge at their proper times without exhaustion: this is precisely the course of the four seasons, set in motion by primordial vital energy. This is what is meant by transformation admitting no interruption. Viewed separately, the myriad forms of goodness are each sufficient; viewed together, the one principle is fully complete. This is why Confucius is like the primordial vital energy of Supreme Harmony circulating through the four seasons, rather than being of the same sort as Bo Yi, Yi Yin, and Liu Xiahui [?]. Allow me to discuss this by following Master Zhu’s words. The Book of Changes says: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! The myriad things draw upon it for their beginning. Perfect indeed is the primal power of Kun! The myriad things draw upon it for their birth.” This is the origin of the account of primordial vital energy. It also says: “The Way of Qian changes and transforms; each thing attains its proper nature and allotted destiny. It preserves and unites Supreme Harmony; hence benefit and steadfastness.” This is the origin of the account of Supreme Harmony. This vital energy is rooted in the time before things existed and circulates after things have come into existence. When this energy stirs, it becomes spring, and through it the myriad things are born. When this energy flows freely, it becomes summer, and through it the myriad things grow. When this energy draws inward, it becomes autumn; when this energy becomes austere, it becomes winter: through it the myriad things are gathered in and stored away. People see that spring presides over birth but cannot bring growth, gathering, or storage, and suppose that spring merely has its own vital energy. They do not understand that spring’s vital energy is precisely the vital energy of summer, autumn, and winter: it is called spring merely because it circulates in spring. People see that summer presides over growth but cannot bring birth, cannot bring gathering, cannot…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
藏也以爲夏有夏之氣耳而不知夏之氣卽春
之氣秋之氣冬之氣也流行於夏則爲夏耳又
見夫秋之主於收而不能生不能長不能藏冬
之主於藏而不能生不能長不能收也以爲秋
有秋之氣冬有冬之氣耳而不知秋之氣卽春
之氣夏之氣冬之氣冬之氣卽春之氣夏之氣
秋之氣也流行於秋則爲秋流行於冬則爲冬
耳然由元氣而言之則四時會通於一由四時
而言之則元氣各彰其化是故春有春之令焉
===
生之不可以爲長不可以爲收不可以爲藏猶
長與收藏之不可以爲生也夏有夏之令焉長
之不可以爲生不可以爲收不可以爲藏猶生
與收藏之不可以爲長也秋有秋之令冬有冬
之令焉收之不可以爲生不可以爲長不可以
爲藏猶生長與藏之不可以爲收藏之不可以
爲生不可以爲長不可以爲收猶生長與收之
不可以爲藏也元氣不息其運而四時各有所
寄運者其全也寄者其偏也運者其合也寄者
punctuated: 藏也，以爲夏有夏之氣耳，而不知夏之氣卽春之氣、秋之氣、冬之氣也，流行於夏則爲夏耳。又見夫秋之主於收而不能生、不能長、不能藏，冬之主於藏而不能生、不能長、不能收也，以爲秋有秋之氣，冬有冬之氣耳，而不知秋之氣卽春之氣、夏之氣、冬之氣，冬之氣卽春之氣、夏之氣、秋之氣也，流行於秋則爲秋，流行於冬則爲冬耳。然由元氣而言之，則四時會通於一；由四時而言之，則元氣各彰其化。是故春有春之令焉，生之不可以爲長，不可以爲收，不可以爲藏，猶長與收藏之不可以爲生也。夏有夏之令焉，長之不可以爲生，不可以爲收，不可以爲藏，猶生與收藏之不可以爲長也。秋有秋之令，冬有冬之令焉，收之不可以爲生，不可以爲長，不可以爲藏，猶生長與藏之不可以爲收；藏之不可以爲生，不可以爲長，不可以爲收，猶生長與收之不可以爲藏也。元氣不息其運，而四時各有所寄。運者其全也，寄者其偏也；運者其合也，寄者
translation_en: …store away, they suppose that summer has its own qi alone, without realizing that summer’s qi is precisely the qi of spring, autumn, and winter: circulating in summer, it simply becomes summer. Again, they see that autumn governs gathering in but cannot bring forth, foster growth, or store away, while winter governs storing away but cannot bring forth, foster growth, or gather in. They suppose that autumn has its own qi and winter its own qi, without realizing that autumn’s qi is precisely the qi of spring, summer, and winter, and winter’s qi is precisely the qi of spring, summer, and autumn. Circulating in autumn, it simply becomes autumn; circulating in winter, it simply becomes winter. Yet viewed in terms of primordial qi, the four seasons converge and unite as one; viewed in terms of the four seasons, primordial qi manifests its transforming activity distinctly in each. Thus spring has its seasonal ordinance: bringing forth cannot serve as fostering growth, gathering in, or storing away, just as fostering growth, gathering in, and storing away cannot serve as bringing forth. Summer has its seasonal ordinance: fostering growth cannot serve as bringing forth, gathering in, or storing away, just as bringing forth, gathering in, and storing away cannot serve as fostering growth. Autumn has its seasonal ordinance, and winter has its seasonal ordinance: gathering in cannot serve as bringing forth, fostering growth, or storing away, just as bringing forth, fostering growth, and storing away cannot serve as gathering in; storing away cannot serve as bringing forth, fostering growth, or gathering in, just as bringing forth, fostering growth, and gathering in cannot serve as storing away. Primordial qi never ceases its circulation, yet in each of the four seasons it finds a particular expression. In circulation it is whole; in its particular expression it is partial. In circulation it is united; in its particular expression…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
其分也運者其一也寄者其萬也謂元氣有外
於四時固不可但就其一時之化而謂元氣盡
於此焉亦不可也觀此而孔子之於伯夷伊尹
柳下惠不有可言者乎天以元氣四時之理而
畀之於人本至一而不二至完而不缺至純而
不雜也但五行之生也各一其性稟受不同而
成就亦異伯夷得之而爲清焉不視惡色不聽
惡聲非君不事非民不使夷之清蓋極其清矣
伊尹得之而爲任焉何事非君何使非民治亦
===
進亂亦進尹之任蓋極其任矣柳下惠得之而
爲和焉不羞汙君不卑小官佚逸不怨阨窮不
憫惠之和蓋極其和矣夫夷之清聖人之清也
而曰任曰和則有所不足尹之任聖人之任也
而曰清曰和則有所未備惠之和聖人之和也
而曰清曰任則有所未全此豈其道有不同哉
道無爾我而見有通塞清之理卽任之理和之
理也夷則有見於清而無見於任與和焉耳任
之理卽清之理和之理也尹則有見於任而無
punctuated:
其分也；運者其一也，寄者其萬也。謂元氣有外於四時，固不可；但就其一時之化，而謂元氣盡於此焉，亦不可也。觀此，而孔子之於伯夷、伊尹、柳下惠，不有可言者乎？

天以元氣四時之理而畀之於人，本至一而不二，至完而不缺，至純而不雜也。但五行之生也，各一其性，稟受不同，而成就亦異。伯夷得之而爲清焉，不視惡色，不聽惡聲，非君不事，非民不使，夷之清蓋極其清矣。伊尹得之而爲任焉，何事非君？何使非民？治亦進，亂亦進，尹之任蓋極其任矣。柳下惠得之而爲和焉，不羞汙君，不卑小官，佚逸不怨，阨窮不憫，惠之和蓋極其和矣。

夫夷之清，聖人之清也，而曰任曰和，則有所不足；尹之任，聖人之任也，而曰清曰和，則有所未備；惠之和，聖人之和也，而曰清曰任，則有所未全。此豈其道有不同哉？道無爾我，而見有通塞。清之理卽任之理、和之理也，夷則有見於清，而無見於任與和焉耳。任之理卽清之理、和之理也，尹則有見於任而無
translation_en:
…what is lodged in particular seasons is its differentiation; what circulates is its oneness, while what is lodged in particular seasons is its multiplicity. Certainly, one cannot say that primordial vital energy exists apart from the four seasons. Yet neither can one consider the transformations of a single season and say that primordial vital energy is exhausted therein. In light of this, is there not something to be said about Confucius in relation to Bo Yi, Yi Yin, and Liu Xiahui?

Heaven bestows upon human beings the principle of primordial vital energy and the four seasons. In its origin, this is utterly one, without duality; utterly complete, without deficiency; and utterly pure, without admixture. Yet in the generation of the Five Phases, each has its own particular nature. What people receive as their endowments differs, and so too do their attainments. Bo Yi received it and became pure: he would not look upon evil sights or listen to evil sounds; he would serve only a ruler he deemed worthy and employ only people he deemed fit. Bo Yi’s purity indeed reached the utmost in purity. Yi Yin received it and became one who assumed responsibility: what ruler could he serve who was not his ruler? What people could he employ who were not his people? He entered office in times of order and also in times of disorder. Yi Yin’s assumption of responsibility indeed reached its utmost. Liu Xiahui received it and became harmonious: he was not ashamed to serve a corrupt ruler and did not disdain a lowly office; when left idle [?], he bore no resentment, and in straitened circumstances he felt no distress. Liu Xiahui’s harmony indeed reached the utmost in harmony.

Bo Yi’s purity was the purity of a sage, yet in responsibility and harmony he fell short. Yi Yin’s responsibility was the responsibility of a sage, yet in purity and harmony he was not fully equipped. Liu Xiahui’s harmony was the harmony of a sage, yet in purity and responsibility he was not complete. Could this mean that their Ways differed? The Way makes no distinction between you and me, but understanding may be open or obstructed. The principle of purity is precisely the principle of responsibility and of harmony. Bo Yi simply had insight into purity but lacked insight into responsibility and harmony. The principle of responsibility is precisely the principle of purity and of harmony. Yi Yin had insight into responsibility but lacked…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
見於清與和焉耳和之理即清之理任之理也
惠則有見於和而無見於清與任焉耳譬則春
夏秋冬莫非元氣但得之而爲春者則成其所
以爲春不能通乎夏通乎秋通乎冬也得之而
爲夏者則成其所以爲夏不能通乎春通乎秋
通乎冬也得之而爲秋者則成其所以爲秋不
能通乎春通乎夏通乎冬得之而爲冬者則成
其所以爲冬不能通乎春通乎夏通乎秋也雖
其生生化化形形色色無非化育流行之用要
===
之各司其職各□其化終非太和元氣之全體
也孔子之聖固無外於清任與和也外清任與
和亦無所謂聖也但其天縱之能太極之所由
以全也一貫之妙陰陽之所由以會也時中之
道動靜之所以無端也曰清曰任曰和以一心
而會其精矣曰夷曰尹曰惠以一身而備其德
矣自其道之流行於夷者言之吾見其清矣而
清固不足以盡之也自其道之流行於尹者言
之吾見其任矣而任固不足以盡之也自其道
punctuated:
見於清與和焉耳。和之理即清之理、任之理也，惠則有見於和而無見於清與任焉耳。譬則春夏秋冬，莫非元氣，但得之而爲春者，則成其所以爲春，不能通乎夏、通乎秋、通乎冬也；得之而爲夏者，則成其所以爲夏，不能通乎春、通乎秋、通乎冬也；得之而爲秋者，則成其所以爲秋，不能通乎春、通乎夏、通乎冬；得之而爲冬者，則成其所以爲冬，不能通乎春、通乎夏、通乎秋也。雖其生生化化、形形色色，無非化育流行之用，要之，各司其職，各□其化，終非太和元氣之全體也。
孔子之聖，固無外於清、任與和也；外清、任與和，亦無所謂聖也。但其天縱之能，太極之所由以全也；一貫之妙，陰陽之所由以會也；時中之道，動靜之所以無端也。曰清、曰任、曰和，以一心而會其精矣；曰夷、曰尹、曰惠，以一身而備其德矣。自其道之流行於夷者言之，吾見其清矣，而清固不足以盡之也；自其道之流行於尹者言之，吾見其任矣，而任固不足以盡之也；自其道
translation_en:
…insight into purity and harmony. The principle of harmony is precisely the principle of purity and of responsibility; yet Liuxia Hui has insight into harmony alone, without insight into purity and responsibility. By analogy, spring, summer, autumn, and winter are all manifestations of primordial qi. Yet that which receives it and becomes spring fulfills what makes it spring, but cannot extend to summer, autumn, or winter. That which receives it and becomes summer fulfills what makes it summer, but cannot extend to spring, autumn, or winter. That which receives it and becomes autumn fulfills what makes it autumn, but cannot extend to spring, summer, or winter. That which receives it and becomes winter fulfills what makes it winter, but cannot extend to spring, summer, or autumn. Although their ceaseless generation and transformation, in all their forms and colors, are nothing other than the workings of the ongoing process of transformation and nurture, ultimately each performs its own office and each [?] its own transforming activity. They never constitute the complete substance of the primordial qi of Supreme Harmony.
The sagehood of Kongzi certainly does not lie outside purity, responsibility, and harmony; apart from these, there is likewise nothing that can be called sagehood. Yet his Heaven-endowed capacity is that through which the Supreme Ultimate attains completeness; the marvel of his single unifying thread is that through which yin and yang converge; and his Way of attaining due balance as circumstances require is that through which movement and stillness have no beginning or end. As for purity, responsibility, and harmony, he unites their essence in a single mind. As for Bo Yi, Yi Yin, and Liuxia Hui, he possesses their virtues fully in his own person. Speaking of the operation of his Way in Bo Yi, I see his purity, yet purity alone certainly cannot exhaust it. Speaking of the operation of his Way in Yi Yin, I see his responsibility, yet responsibility alone certainly cannot exhaust it. Speaking of his Way…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
之流行於惠者言之吾見其和矣而和固不足
以盡之也當其清時任之理和之理未嘗不在
也時清而清無意於清焉伯夷之清莫非孔子
之清也當其任時清之理和之理未嘗不在也
時任而任無意於任焉伊尹之任莫非孔子之
任也當其和時清之理任之理未嘗不在也時
和而和無意於和焉柳下惠之和莫非孔子之
和也明日去衞接淅去齊不脫冕而去魯孔子
之清豈伯夷之所謂清哉未嘗不清而不倚於
===
清清矣而有任與和存乎其間也夢見周公志
英三代知其不可而猶爲孔子之任豈伊尹之
所謂任哉未嘗不任而不倚於任任矣而有清
與和存乎其間也陽貨可往南子可見魯人獵
較而可從孔子之和豈柳下惠之所謂和哉未
嘗不和而不倚於和和矣而有清與任存乎其
間也故自其全者而言之謂之曰清不可謂之
曰任不可謂之曰和亦不可自其分者而言之
謂其爲夷可也謂其爲尹可也謂其爲惠亦可
punctuated: 之流行於惠者言之，吾見其和矣，而和固不足以盡之也。當其清時，任之理、和之理未嘗不在也。時清而清，無意於清焉，伯夷之清莫非孔子之清也。當其任時，清之理、和之理未嘗不在也。時任而任，無意於任焉，伊尹之任莫非孔子之任也。當其和時，清之理、任之理未嘗不在也。時和而和，無意於和焉，柳下惠之和莫非孔子之和也。明日去衞，接淅去齊，不脫冕而去魯，孔子之清豈伯夷之所謂清哉？未嘗不清而不倚於清，清矣而有任與和存乎其間也。夢見周公，志英三代，知其不可而猶爲，孔子之任豈伊尹之所謂任哉？未嘗不任而不倚於任，任矣而有清與和存乎其間也。陽貨可往，南子可見，魯人獵較而可從，孔子之和豈柳下惠之所謂和哉？未嘗不和而不倚於和，和矣而有清與任存乎其間也。故自其全者而言之，謂之曰清不可，謂之曰任不可，謂之曰和亦不可。自其分者而言之，謂其爲夷可也，謂其爲尹可也，謂其爲惠亦可
translation_en:
…speaking of the Way as it finds expression in Liu Xiahui, I see his harmony; yet harmony alone certainly cannot encompass it. When Confucius practiced purity, the principles of responsibility and harmony were never absent. When the circumstances called for purity, he was pure, without deliberately striving for purity. All of Bo Yi’s purity was also Confucius’s purity. When he undertook responsibility, the principles of purity and harmony were never absent. When the circumstances called for responsibility, he undertook it, without deliberately striving to do so. All of Yi Yin’s responsibility was also Confucius’s responsibility. When he practiced harmony, the principles of purity and responsibility were never absent. When the circumstances called for harmony, he was harmonious, without deliberately striving for harmony. All of Liu Xiahui’s harmony was also Confucius’s harmony.

He left Wei the next day; he left Qi carrying rice that was still being rinsed; he left Lu without even removing his ceremonial cap. Was Confucius’s purity merely what is called purity in Bo Yi? He was never without purity, yet did not incline exclusively toward it. Even in his purity, responsibility and harmony were present. He dreamed of the Duke of Zhou, set his aspirations upon the Three Dynasties [?], and acted even though he knew his purpose could not be accomplished. Was Confucius’s responsibility merely what is called responsibility in Yi Yin? He never failed to undertake responsibility, yet did not incline exclusively toward it. Even in his responsibility, purity and harmony were present. He could visit Yang Huo, could meet Nanzi, and could join the people of Lu in their hunting contests. Was Confucius’s harmony merely what is called harmony in Liu Xiahui? He was never without harmony, yet did not incline exclusively toward it. Even in his harmony, purity and responsibility were present.

Thus, speaking of him in his entirety, one cannot call him simply pure, cannot call him simply responsible, and cannot call him simply harmonious. Speaking of his individual aspects, however, one may call him a Bo Yi, one may call him a Yi Yin, and one may also call him a Liu Xiahui…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
也不猶之太和無象元氣無心而四時之流行
循環無端者哉然孔子之元氣非特流行於四
時而已也祖述憲章流行於帝王矣上律下襲
流行於天地矣繼往開來流行於古今矣太和
元氣奚獨在成周宇宙間哉嗟夫元者天地生
物之心其在聖人則爲仁是故四時莫非元氣
則亦莫非生物也三德莫非元理則亦莫非仁
心也生於春長於夏而肅殺於秋冬肅殺亦所
以生之也任以救民和以容衆而清操以獨善
===
獨善亦所以兼善也然則太和元氣之說不惟
見孔子之道兼全乎三子且足以見孔子之心
常在於仁天下
表
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表元祐元
年
同考試官教諭陸批忠愛溢於鋪敘之外規諷
含於陳謝之中渢渢乎不獨詞藻之工而已用錄以
punctuated:
也。不猶之太和無象、元氣無心，而四時之流行循環無端者哉？然孔子之元氣，非特流行於四時而已也。祖述憲章，流行於帝王矣；上律下襲，流行於天地矣；繼往開來，流行於古今矣。太和元氣，奚獨在成周宇宙間哉？嗟夫！元者，天地生物之心，其在聖人則爲仁。是故四時莫非元氣，則亦莫非生物也；三德莫非元理，則亦莫非仁心也。生於春，長於夏，而肅殺於秋冬，肅殺亦所以生之也。任以救民，和以容衆，而清操以獨善，獨善亦所以兼善也。然則太和元氣之說，不惟見孔子之道兼全乎三子，且足以見孔子之心常在於仁天下。
表
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表。元祐元年。
同考試官教諭陸批：忠愛溢於鋪敘之外，規諷含於陳謝之中。渢渢乎！不獨詞藻之工而已，用錄以
translation_en:
… too. Is this not like Supreme Harmony, which has no visible form, and primordial vital energy, which has no conscious intent, while the four seasons flow in an endless cycle? Yet Confucius’s primordial vital energy did not flow through the four seasons alone. By transmitting the ways of earlier sovereigns and taking their institutions as models, it flowed through emperors and kings; by following Heaven above and according with Earth below, it flowed through Heaven and Earth; by carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future, it flowed through antiquity and the present. How could Supreme Harmony and primordial vital energy have existed only within the world of the Zhou dynasty?
Ah! The primal is the heart of Heaven and Earth that brings living things into being; in the sage, it is benevolence. Thus, since all four seasons embody primordial vital energy, all bring living things into being. Since all three virtues embody the primal principle, all likewise embody the benevolent heart. Things are born in spring and grow in summer, but are cut down by the severity of autumn and winter; this cutting down is also a means of bringing life into being. Taking responsibility serves to save the people, harmony to embrace the multitude, and pure conduct to perfect oneself alone; yet perfecting oneself alone is also a means of perfecting others together with oneself. Thus, the account of Supreme Harmony and primordial vital energy shows not only that Confucius’s Way fully encompassed the virtues of the three masters, but also that his heart was constantly set on extending benevolence to all under Heaven.
Memorial
A model memorial of thanks on the Song appointment of Cheng Yi as Expositor in the Hall for Venerating Governance (Chongzheng Hall). First year of Yuanyou.
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: Loyalty and devotion overflow beyond the exposition; admonition and remonstrance are contained within the expressions of thanks. How ample and flowing! Its merit lies in more than skillful diction alone. It is therefore selected for inclusion to …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
式多士
考試官教諭鎦批玩之蒼然而有光讀之鏗
然而有節是四六之優者
考試官教授熊批駢麗典則得宋人陳謝之
體錄之以式
元祐元年某月某日伏蒙
聖恩以臣頤爲
崇政殿說書稱
謝者
===
明王圖治親賢唯重於格心
聖主崇文畜德聿先於稽古爰慎師儒之選庸
資啓沃之功道與時行感隨懼至臣頤誠
惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟帝王之學與韋布
不同精一之傳厥淵源有自成湯元聖惟
先學於有莘大武丕承遂訪書於尚父周
禮所載官屬滋多慎起居必擇前後左右
言道德非獨師保疑丞迨正學之旣湮乃
講儀之徒事稱制親决漢何取於橫經入
punctuated:
式多士。
考試官教諭鎦批：玩之蒼然而有光，讀之鏗然而有節，是四六之優者。
考試官教授熊批：駢麗典則，得宋人陳謝之體，錄之以式。
元祐元年某月某日，伏蒙聖恩，以臣頤爲崇政殿說書，稱謝者。
明王圖治，親賢唯重於格心；聖主崇文，畜德聿先於稽古。爰慎師儒之選，庸資啓沃之功。道與時行，感隨懼至。臣頤誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟帝王之學，與韋布不同；精一之傳，厥淵源有自。成湯元聖，惟先學於有莘；大武丕承，遂訪書於尚父。周禮所載，官屬滋多；慎起居，必擇前後左右；言道德，非獨師保疑丞。迨正學之旣湮，乃講儀之徒事。稱制親决，漢何取於橫經入
translation_en:
…to serve as a model for the assembled scholars.

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Savor it: it has an antique gravity and a radiance. Read it aloud: it rings out with measured cadence. This is an excellent example of four-and-six prose.”

Examiner Xiong, Professor, comments: “Its parallel phrasing is elegant, classical, and well ordered, capturing the form of Song memorials of thanks. It is recorded here as a model.”

On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of Yuanyou, having humbly received the imperial favor appointing your servant Yi as Lecturer in the Chongzheng Hall, I submit this expression of thanks.

When an enlightened king seeks good government, in drawing worthy men close he places the greatest weight on rectifying his heart. When a sagely sovereign honors learning, in nurturing virtue he gives first place to examining antiquity. Thus you have carefully selected a learned teacher, to benefit from his work of enlightening and enriching your understanding. The Way advances with its time; gratitude comes together with apprehension. Your servant Yi, truly trembling and truly fearful, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly knocks his forehead upon it.

I humbly consider that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoners clad in plain cloth. The transmission of the teaching of refinement and single-mindedness has its own deep origins. Cheng Tang, that supreme sage, first learned from the sage of Youshen; the great King Wu [?], magnificently continuing the inheritance, thereupon sought instruction in the Documents from Shangfu. The Rites of Zhou records a great many attendant offices. To exercise care in his daily conduct, the ruler must select those stationed before, behind, to his left, and to his right. Those who speak to him of the Way and virtue are not confined to preceptors, protectors, advisers, and assistants. Once orthodox learning had become obscured, however, only the formalities of lecturing were pursued. Exercising sovereign authority and deciding affairs in person, what benefit did the Han rulers derive from men entering with the Classics laid across their laps…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
侍質疑唐竟更於直日恭逢
熈代克舉曠儀
藝祖崇儒開寶肇延於
便殿
神皇重道太平繼啓乎
經筵
闢龍圖
建資善

===
直秘閣
侍禁中
累朝盛事曁傳景祐拓崔館以更崇政之名載
命昌朝拜講官而兼說書之職地聨
蘭省官列蓬瀛誦禮樂詩書之文上窺蘊奧
嘉唐虞商周之治直接眞傳面

黼筵而論道
九重恩動縹緗道德進斯勢分俱忘觀聽專則
punctuated: 侍質疑，唐竟更於直日。恭逢熈代，克舉曠儀。藝祖崇儒，開寶肇延於便殿；神皇重道，太平繼啓乎經筵。闢龍圖，建資善，列聖傳心；直秘閣，侍禁中，累朝盛事。曁傳景祐，拓崔館以更崇政之名，載命昌朝，拜講官而兼說書之職。地聨蘭省，官列蓬瀛。誦禮樂詩書之文，上窺蘊奧；嘉唐虞商周之治，直接眞傳。面丹扆以談經，萬卷光浮几席；對黼筵而論道，九重恩動縹緗。道德進斯勢分俱忘，觀聽專則
translation_en:
…attending to resolve doubts; under the Tang, this ultimately changed to service on assigned days. Fortunately, in an age of flourishing peace, these long-neglected ceremonies could be restored. The founding emperor esteemed Confucian learning and, in the Kaibao era, first invited scholars into a side hall of the palace. The divine emperor honored the Way and, in the Taiping era, continued by inaugurating the Classics Colloquium. The Longtu Pavilion was opened and the Zishan Hall established: successive sage emperors transmitted the teaching of the mind. Scholars served in the Secret Archives and attended within the palace: these were illustrious undertakings of successive reigns.

When the succession reached the Jingyou era, the lofty hall [?] was enlarged and renamed Chongzheng. Changchao was then appointed a Lecturer, concurrently holding the office of Expositor. His station linked him to the Department of State Affairs, and his office ranked him among the immortals of Penglai and Yingzhou. Reciting texts on ritual and music and the Odes and Documents, he probed their profound meanings for the sovereign; extolling the government of Tang, Yu, Shang, and Zhou, he directly received their authentic transmission. Facing the vermilion throne screen, he expounded the classics, and the radiance of ten thousand volumes shone over the desks and mats. Before the embroidered imperial seat, he discussed the Way, and imperial favor stirred among the silk-bound books. As virtue and the Way advanced, distinctions of power and rank were entirely forgotten; when attention in watching and listening was concentrated, then …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
威儀益肅寔以假輔導之寄非止備顧問
之資恭惟
〇〇〇〇
英姿神授
睿質天成毓德
青宮懋著
燕貽之表則握符
紫禦聿昭
龍德之正中間當
===
踐阼之初已銳勵精之志謂明道有資講學
弘開延訪之誠以輔德必賴儒臣益廣聘
徵之典是宜旁求碩彥豈意錄及疎庸校
理之司方承
恩而入對講幃之任復荷
命以兼榮竊念臣頤伊洛寒儒章縫末品雖師
承之有在愧聖道之未聞學究誠明竊傳
主靜之旨治分王霸僭陳立政之書猥私
授於家庭詎明揚於
punctuated:
威儀益肅，寔以假輔導之寄，非止備顧問之資。恭惟〇〇〇〇，英姿神授，睿質天成。毓德青宮，懋著燕貽之表則；握符紫禦，聿昭龍德之正中。間當踐阼之初，已銳勵精之志。謂明道有資講學，弘開延訪之誠；以輔德必賴儒臣，益廣聘徵之典。是宜旁求碩彥，豈意錄及疎庸？校理之司，方承恩而入對；講幃之任，復荷命以兼榮。
竊念臣頤，伊洛寒儒，章縫末品。雖師承之有在，愧聖道之未聞。學究誠明，竊傳主靜之旨；治分王霸，僭陳立政之書。猥私授於家庭，詎明揚於
translation_en:
…and ceremonial deportment becomes still more solemn. Indeed, this entrusts them with the responsibility of guidance and instruction, rather than merely making them available for consultation. I reverently consider that Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇] possesses a heroic bearing bestowed by the spirits and a sagacious nature formed by Heaven. Nurturing virtue in the crown prince’s palace, you splendidly manifested the exemplary legacy bequeathed by your forebears; taking up the sovereign tally in the imperial precincts [?], you revealed the perfect centrality of the dragon’s virtue. At the very beginning of your accession, you already firmly resolved to devote yourself energetically to government. Holding that elucidating the Way benefits from lectures and study, you generously expressed your sincere desire to invite counsel; believing that the cultivation of virtue necessarily depends upon Confucian officials, you further expanded the practice of summoning worthy men to service. It was fitting, therefore, to seek eminent scholars far and wide; who could have imagined that the selection would extend to someone as inept and ordinary as myself? As an Editorial Assistant, I had just received the favor of admission to an imperial audience; now I have again been honored by a command concurrently appointing me to lecture before you.
I humbly reflect that I, your servant Yi, am an obscure scholar from the Yi and Luo region, a man of the lowest standing among those who wear the Confucian cap. Although I have received instruction through an established lineage of teachers, I am ashamed that I have yet to apprehend the Way of the sages. In scholarship I investigate sincerity and illumination, venturing to transmit the principle of making stillness the foundation; in government I distinguish the kingly way from the hegemonic way, presuming to present a writing on establishing governance. Unworthily, I have taught privately within my household; how could I have expected to be publicly commended at…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
朝宁顧興道致治必始夫一心而君子小人
難與之雜進况幽閑得肆之地實兢惕喫
緊之圖惟
聖明時富春秋乃
道德日勤講讀臣敢不殫心論述畢力敷陳
嘉謨嘉猷必入告于
元后有典有則冀上對乎
先王思孫奭之圖忠暴昭素之銘直倘陳一得
少助
===
萬幾忠信不欺雖罔諧於時好莊嚴自勵或
仰契乎
宸衷伏願
皇猷允塞
聖德緝煕
虛受於咸楚語勿咻齊傅
辨幾於豫一暴無間十寒用舊人而舊業愈
光克盡善繼善述之道罷新法而新猷益
壯用弘可久可大之規臣無任瞻
punctuated: 朝宁。顧興道致治，必始夫一心，而君子小人難與之雜進。况幽閑得肆之地，實兢惕喫緊之圖。惟聖明時富春秋，乃道德日勤講讀。臣敢不殫心論述，畢力敷陳？嘉謨嘉猷，必入告于元后；有典有則，冀上對乎先王。思孫奭之圖忠，暴昭素之銘直，倘陳一得，少助萬幾。忠信不欺，雖罔諧於時好；莊嚴自勵，或仰契乎宸衷。伏願皇猷允塞，聖德緝煕。虛受於咸，楚語勿咻齊傅；辨幾於豫，一暴無間十寒。用舊人而舊業愈光，克盡善繼善述之道；罷新法而新猷益壯，用弘可久可大之規。臣無任瞻
translation_en:
…at the imperial court. Yet promoting the Way and achieving good government must begin with the single heart, and gentlemen and petty men cannot readily be advanced together.
