Moreover, a secluded setting where one may give oneself free rein is precisely where vigilance and apprehension are most urgently needed. Your enlightened Majesty is in the prime of life and daily applies himself to lectures and readings on the Way and virtue. How could your servant fail to devote his whole mind to exposition and all his strength to setting matters forth? Good counsels and good plans must be brought before the sovereign; established precedents and standards may, I hope, enable us to answer worthily to the former kings. Mindful of Sun Shi’s resolve to serve loyally, and making manifest Zhaosu’s forthright admonition [?], I might offer even one useful insight and thereby lend some small assistance to the myriad affairs of government. Loyal, trustworthy, and without deception, I may fail to accord with the fashions of the time; solemn and dignified in disciplining myself, I may nevertheless accord with Your Majesty’s heart.
I humbly pray that imperial counsels may be fully realized and Your Majesty’s sagely virtue shine ever more brightly. Receive others with an open mind, as taught by the hexagram Influence (Xian): let no clamour of Chu speech drown out the tutor from Qi. Discern the first stirrings of events, as taught by the hexagram Enthusiasm (Yu): let no ten days of cold interrupt a single day’s warming. Employ former servants so that the inherited undertaking shines still more brightly, fully realizing the way of worthily continuing and carrying forward your predecessor’s work. Abolish the New Policies so that new counsels gain still greater strength, thereby enlarging a design capable of enduring and attaining greatness. Your servant cannot contain his feelings as he gazes…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策五道
第一問
===
===
同考試官教諭張批我
皇考啓佑之仁
皇上繼述之孝蓋曠□僅見者子能□□揚其
盛而末復以
心與幾爲致治要務蓋涵濡
聖化而有得者錄之以式多士
同考試官教諭張批我
世宗
皇上聖聖相傳授守一道天下臣民傳聞快覩矣而以疑
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屏營之至。謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁塲，策五道。
第一問。
同考試官教諭張批：我皇考啓佑之仁，皇上繼述之孝，蓋曠□僅見者。子能□□揚其盛，而末復以心與幾爲致治要務，蓋涵濡聖化而有得者，錄之以式多士。
同考試官教諭張批：我世宗、皇上，聖聖相傳，授守一道，天下臣民傳聞快覩矣，而以疑
translation_en:
… looking up to Heaven and revering Your Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third session: five policy questions.
First question.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The benevolence with which our late imperial father opened the way and aided his successor, and the filial devotion with which His Majesty carries on his predecessor’s work, are scarcely ever seen [?]. You have been able to […] extol their magnificence, and at the end you further identify the mind and the incipient signs of change as essential concerns in achieving good government. Surely you have absorbed the sage’s transforming influence and gained something from it. This is recorded as a model for the assembled scholars.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Our Shizong and His Majesty, one sage succeeding another, have transmitted and preserved a single Way. The officials and people throughout the realm have heard of this and delighted to witness it; and through doubt [?] …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
帝命以迓
天休萬世無疆者端在於是子能仰窺而對揚之是亦涵濡
泰和而能識其大者
考試官教諭鎦批我
皇考
皇上仁孝相承後先濟美真繪天地者難爲工也子能闡揚其
盛而末所敷陳尤見忠
君之悃可嘉
考試官教授熊批揄揚我
===
世宗
皇上仁孝最爲精詳至謹始慎終正本澄源處復以
世宗敬一心法
獻之尤見親切玩之有餘味其必素懷忠愛而思以自效者
帝王之垂裕後昆也固貴有燕貽之仁而
其克紹前烈也尤貴有駿惠之孝夫先天
下而作之者嗣服所由以昭也使垂裕之
未善則無以盛其傳矣豈燕貽之仁乎後
天下而述之者世德所由以延也使克紹
punctuated:
帝命，以迓天休，萬世無疆者，端在於是。子能仰窺而對揚之，是亦涵濡泰和而能識其大者。
考試官教諭鎦批：我皇考、皇上仁孝相承，後先濟美，真繪天地者難爲工也。子能闡揚其盛，而末所敷陳，尤見忠君之悃，可嘉。
考試官教授熊批：揄揚我世宗、皇上仁孝，最爲精詳。至謹始慎終、正本澄源處，復以世宗敬一心法獻之，尤見親切。玩之有餘味，其必素懷忠愛而思以自效者。
帝王之垂裕後昆也，固貴有燕貽之仁；而其克紹前烈也，尤貴有駿惠之孝。夫先天下而作之者，嗣服所由以昭也。使垂裕之未善，則無以盛其傳矣，豈燕貽之仁乎？後天下而述之者，世德所由以延也。使克紹
translation_en:
…the imperial mandate [?], thereby welcoming Heaven’s blessings without limit for ten thousand generations: this depends precisely upon the foregoing. You have discerned its import from below and fittingly extolled it. You too are one who, steeped in supreme harmony, can recognize its greatness.
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: Our late imperial father and His Majesty have carried on benevolence and filial devotion in succession, the successor complementing the predecessor’s excellence. Truly, even one who paints Heaven and Earth would find it difficult to do them justice. You have elucidated and extolled their greatness; what you set forth at the end especially reveals your heartfelt loyalty to the sovereign. This merits praise.
Examiner Xiong, Professor, comments: Your praise of the benevolence and filial devotion of our Shizong and His Majesty is exceptionally perceptive and detailed. When you come to being circumspect at the beginning and careful at the end, rectifying the root and clarifying the source, you further present Shizong’s teaching of the mind, “Reverent Concentration on the One.” This is especially pertinent and, upon reflection, leaves much to savor. You must surely be someone who has long cherished loyalty and affection and wishes to demonstrate them through service.
When emperors and kings bequeath abundance to their descendants, they assuredly prize the benevolence that leaves a legacy of peace; when they successfully continue their predecessors’ glorious achievements, they especially prize the filial devotion that faithfully follows them. For those who take the lead in establishing things for all under Heaven provide the means by which their successors’ rule is made illustrious. If their provision for posterity were inadequate, there would be no means to make their legacy flourish. Could this be the benevolence that leaves a legacy of peace? Those who come afterward and carry on these achievements for all under Heaven provide the means by which the dynasty’s virtue is perpetuated. If their continuation of their predecessors’ achievements…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
之未光則無以彰其美矣豈駿惠之孝乎
然仁曰燕貽非專指當時之政言之也凡
夫作於前而冀於後著於謨而垂於訓者
亦莫非其仁之可傳者也孝曰駿惠非專
指已成之迹言之也凡夫不同其迹而同
其心不協其事而協其理者亦莫非其孝
之可盡者也是故有燕貽之仁則後昆於
此乎裕矣有駿惠之孝則前烈於此乎光
矣知此則於
===
世宗肅皇帝之遺詔望我
皇上以守成之道及我
皇上之善繼善述以克承
先德者可以對揚其盛而所謂謹始愼終之道
正本澄源之學亦不出乎此矣請因明問
而敬陳之書曰有典有則貽厥子孫夫啓
之賢聖守成之令主也而猶以典則貽之
者蓋前王之謨訓異世以之爲視傚者也
是故不以其賢而忘典則之貽此正大禹
punctuated:
之未光，則無以彰其美矣，豈駿惠之孝乎？然仁曰燕貽，非專指當時之政言之也。凡夫作於前而冀於後，著於謨而垂於訓者，亦莫非其仁之可傳者也。孝曰駿惠，非專指已成之迹言之也。凡夫不同其迹而同其心，不協其事而協其理者，亦莫非其孝之可盡者也。是故有燕貽之仁，則後昆於此乎裕矣；有駿惠之孝，則前烈於此乎光矣。知此，則於世宗肅皇帝之遺詔望我皇上以守成之道，及我皇上之善繼善述以克承先德者，可以對揚其盛，而所謂謹始愼終之道、正本澄源之學，亦不出乎此矣。
請因明問而敬陳之。《書》曰：「有典有則，貽厥子孫。」夫啓之賢聖，守成之令主也，而猶以典則貽之者，蓋前王之謨訓，異世以之爲視傚者也。是故不以其賢而忘典則之貽，此正大禹
translation_en:
…if the continuation of earlier achievements fails to bring them glory, there is no means of making their excellence manifest. How could this be the filial devotion of faithfully following one’s forebears? Yet to speak of benevolence as providing ease for posterity does not refer solely to the government of one’s own time. Whatever is instituted by a predecessor in hope of its continuation by successors, set forth in plans and handed down in instructions, is likewise an expression of benevolence that can be transmitted. To speak of filial devotion as faithfully following one’s forebears does not refer solely to deeds already accomplished. Where the outward deeds differ but the underlying intention remains the same, and where the undertakings differ but their principles accord, filial devotion can likewise be fully realized. Thus, through benevolence that provides ease for posterity, later generations enjoy abundance; through filial devotion that faithfully follows one’s forebears, earlier achievements gain glory. Understanding this, we can fittingly extol the magnificence both of Emperor Shizong Su’s testamentary edict, which charged our Emperor with preserving the established achievement, and of our Emperor’s skill in continuing and carrying forward his predecessor’s work, thereby inheriting his virtue. The way of taking care at the beginning and remaining cautious to the end, and the learning that rectifies the root and clears the source, likewise fall within this principle.
Allow me respectfully to set this forth in response to your discerning question. The Book of Documents says: “There are statutes and standards, bequeathed to their descendants.” Qi, in his worthiness and sagacity, was an excellent ruler who preserved the established achievement. Yet statutes and standards were still bequeathed to him, because the plans and instructions of former kings serve as models for later ages. Thus, his worthiness was no reason to neglect bequeathing statutes and standards to him. This is precisely how Yu the Great…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
垂裕之道盡善盡美而為仁之至也傳曰
武王周公其達孝矣乎夫武之制作先王
之未為也而獨以達孝稱之者蓋後王之
施為先業賴之以纘承者也是故不以迹
異而阻因心之孝此正武王成先之德善
繼善述而為孝之至也夫惟知禹之所以
貽典則也而可以語我
世宗肅皇帝燕貽之仁矣知武周之所以為達
孝也而可以語我
===
皇上駿惠之孝矣嘗觀
世宗肅皇帝以
剛健中正之資
聖神文武之德自辛巳之夏入繼
大統四十餘年其深仁厚澤浹洽人心者未暇
殫述姑舉其大者如
正
郊丘分合之規
崇朝日夕月之制
punctuated:
垂裕之道，盡善盡美，而為仁之至也。傳曰：「武王、周公，其達孝矣乎！」夫武之制作，先王之未為也，而獨以達孝稱之者，蓋後王之施為，先業賴之以纘承者也。是故不以迹異而阻因心之孝，此正武王成先之德，善繼善述，而為孝之至也。夫惟知禹之所以貽典則也，而可以語我世宗肅皇帝燕貽之仁矣；知武周之所以為達孝也，而可以語我皇上駿惠之孝矣。
嘗觀世宗肅皇帝以剛健中正之資、聖神文武之德，自辛巳之夏入繼大統，四十餘年，其深仁厚澤浹洽人心者，未暇殫述。姑舉其大者，如正郊丘分合之規，崇朝日夕月之制，
translation_en:
…the way of leaving abundant blessings to posterity, perfect in goodness and beauty, and the utmost expression of benevolence. The transmitted text says: “Were not King Wu and the Duke of Zhou consummate in their filial piety!” King Wu established institutions that the former kings had not created; yet he was singled out for praise as consummately filial because the undertakings of later kings are what carry forward and perpetuate their predecessors’ achievements. Thus, differences in outward actions do not obstruct filial devotion arising from the heart. This precisely describes King Wu’s virtue in completing his predecessors’ work: he ably continued their purposes and carried forward their undertakings, attaining the utmost filial piety. Only by understanding why Yu bequeathed models and rules can we speak of the benevolence of our Emperor Shizong Su in leaving blessings to posterity; only by understanding why King Wu and the Duke of Zhou were consummately filial can we speak of our reigning Emperor’s filial piety in reverently following his predecessor.
I have observed that Emperor Shizong Su, endowed with strength, vigor, balance, and rectitude, and possessing sagely insight and civil and martial virtues, succeeded to the imperial throne in the summer of the xinsi year [1521]. Over more than forty years, his profound benevolence and abundant beneficence thoroughly permeated the people’s hearts; there is no time here to recount them exhaustively. Let me merely cite the major instances, such as his rectification of the rules governing the separation and combination of the suburban sacrifices at the altars to Heaven and Earth, and his enhancement of the rites for worshipping the sun in the morning and the moon in the evening…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
作
欽天之頌
隆祈報之典所以篤敬
天之誠也
著明倫之典
制大狩之錄纘
興都之誌賦
祖德之詩所以昭
孝思之心也
===
名豳風之亭
續念農之詩
作喜雨之吟
製農桑之賦所以
憫農家之苦也
幸國子監易
先師像重道崇儒之義也
建無逸殿
作敬一箴
punctuated:
作《欽天之頌》，隆祈報之典，所以篤敬天之誠也。著《明倫之典》，制《大狩之錄》，纘《興都之誌》，賦《祖德之詩》，所以昭孝思之心也。

名豳風之亭，續念農之詩，作喜雨之吟，製農桑之賦，所以憫農家之苦也。幸國子監，易先師像，重道崇儒之義也。建無逸殿，作《敬一箴》，
translation_en:
…He composed the Ode on Revering Heaven and enhanced the rites of supplication and thanksgiving, thereby deepening his sincerity in revering Heaven. He authored the Canon Clarifying Human Relations, produced the Record of the Great Hunt, compiled the Gazetteer of Xingdu, and composed poems on ancestral virtue, thereby manifesting his filial devotion.

He named the Airs of Bin Pavilion, continued his poems expressing concern for farming, composed verses rejoicing in rain, and wrote a rhapsody on farming and sericulture, thereby expressing compassion for the hardships of farming households. He visited the Directorate of Education and replaced the image of the First Teacher, expressing his commitment to honoring the Way and esteeming Confucian learning. He built the Hall of No Ease and composed the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
憂勤惕勵之念也在內申三覆之規在外重
審錄之典
好生矜恤之仁也
勅輔臣與言官以開言路防壅蔽之心也
諭輔臣察貪官以懲黷貨清政本之意也其久
道孚化巍然成功煥然文章信足以遠紹
三皇五帝之規近接
二祖
七宗之統而為天下臣民尊而親之者矣雖
===
神化已臻其極而謙冲猶厪於懷載覩
遺詔畧曰朕遠奉
列聖之家法近承
皇考之身教一念惓惓惟敬
天勤民是務祗緣多病過求長生
郊廟之祀不親朝講之儀久廢蓋愆成美端仗
後賢又曰
自即位至今建言得罪之臣悉從錄用方士
誑惑之徒悉正刑章齋醮工作採買不急之
punctuated:
憂勤惕勵之念也。在內申三覆之規，在外重審錄之典，好生矜恤之仁也。勅輔臣與言官，以開言路，防壅蔽之心也。諭輔臣察貪官，以懲黷貨，清政本之意也。其久道孚化，巍然成功，煥然文章，信足以遠紹三皇五帝之規，近接二祖七宗之統，而為天下臣民尊而親之者矣。
雖神化已臻其極，而謙冲猶厪於懷。載覩遺詔，畧曰：「朕遠奉列聖之家法，近承皇考之身教，一念惓惓，惟敬天勤民是務。祗緣多病，過求長生，郊廟之祀不親，朝講之儀久廢。蓋愆成美，端仗後賢。」又曰：「自即位至今，建言得罪之臣悉從錄用，方士誑惑之徒悉正刑章，齋醮、工作、採買不急之
translation_en:
…expressed his concern, diligence, vigilance, and resolve. At court he reaffirmed the rule requiring three reviews of capital sentences; in the provinces he emphasized the procedures for reviewing judicial cases—expressions of his benevolence in cherishing life and showing compassion. He instructed the grand secretaries and remonstrance officials to open channels of counsel, showing his concern to prevent obstruction and concealment. He directed the grand secretaries to investigate corrupt officials and punish venality, showing his intention to purify the foundations of government. Through long adherence to the Way, he inspired moral transformation; his achievements stood lofty, and his cultural accomplishments shone resplendent. These were indeed sufficient to carry forward the distant example of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and continue the more recent succession of the Two Founders and Seven Ancestors, earning him the reverence and affection of officials and subjects throughout the realm.
Although his transformative influence had reached its utmost perfection, humility remained close to his heart. We have now read his testamentary edict, which says in part: “I have honored the ancestral rules of the successive sage emperors of earlier times and received the personal instruction of my late imperial father. With single-minded devotion, I have sought only to revere Heaven and labor diligently for the people. Yet because I was often ill, I pursued longevity to excess. I did not personally attend the sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and the ceremonies of court audiences and lectures were long neglected. To make amends for these faults and bring what is good to completion, I must rely entirely upon worthy successors.” It further says: “All officials who, from my accession until now, incurred punishment for offering counsel shall be considered for appointment. All practitioners of occult arts who deceived and misled shall be duly punished according to law. Daoist ritual offerings, construction projects, and purchases that are not urgently…”

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
務悉皆停止噫是
詔也大哉洋洋乎其真湯之六事自責武之
貽厥孫謀而漢文之遺詔武帝之自悔殆
不足以彷彿其萬一矣此其燕貽之仁所
以啓我
皇上纘承之烈者不其盡善而盡美矣乎我
皇上以
聰明睿智之資
恭儉溫文之德自丙寅之冬遵奉
===
遺詔
出震握乾其
盛德至善蘊於淵衷者未易窺測姑即其大
者如錄用建言得罪之臣開言路也明正
方士誑惑之罪禁邪術也停止採買工作
不急之務恤民隱也躬親
郊廟之祀復典禮也其所以恪遵
遺詔光紹前烈信乎真足以仰體我
世宗圖治未遑之心而爲繼體守成之
punctuated:
務，悉皆停止。」噫！是詔也，大哉，洋洋乎！其真湯之六事自責、武之貽厥孫謀，而漢文之遺詔、武帝之自悔，殆不足以彷彿其萬一矣。此其燕貽之仁，所以啓我皇上纘承之烈者，不其盡善而盡美矣乎？

我皇上以聰明睿智之資、恭儉溫文之德，自丙寅之冬，遵奉遺詔，出震握乾。其盛德至善蘊於淵衷者，未易窺測。姑即其大者，如錄用建言得罪之臣，開言路也；明正方士誑惑之罪，禁邪術也；停止採買工作不急之務，恤民隱也；躬親郊廟之祀，復典禮也。其所以恪遵遺詔、光紹前烈，信乎真足以仰體我世宗圖治未遑之心，而爲繼體守成之
translation_en:
…all such undertakings shall cease.” Ah! How great and far-reaching is this edict! It truly matches Tang’s self-reproach on six counts and Wu’s provision of plans for his descendants. Even the testamentary edict of Emperor Wen of Han and Emperor Wu’s expression of remorse scarcely approximate one ten-thousandth of it. Was not this benevolence in providing for his descendants, thereby opening the way for Our Emperor’s achievements in continuing the succession, wholly good and wholly perfect?

Our Emperor, endowed with intelligence and sagacious wisdom, and with the virtues of reverence, frugality, gentleness, and refinement, has respectfully obeyed the testamentary edict since the winter of the bingyin year [1566], emerging from the position of the heir to assume sovereign authority. The abundant virtue and utmost goodness stored in the depths of his heart are not easily fathomed. Let us consider only the principal instances: employing officials who incurred punishment for speaking out opens the channels of remonstrance; publicly and duly punishing the masters of occult arts for their deception prohibits heterodox practices; halting nonessential procurement and construction shows compassion for the people’s hardships; personally performing the sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temple restores the established rites. Through scrupulously obeying the testamentary edict and gloriously continuing his predecessor’s achievements, he is indeed fully able to embody the aspirations for good government that Our Shizong had not yet had leisure to realize, and to become, in inheriting the throne and preserving its accomplishments, a…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
令主矣其他推類以盡義通變以宜民如
踐祚之初屢卻羣臣勸進之章非即
世宗孝思之心乎
登極之詔盡
蠲遠年逋負之租非即
世宗憫農之意乎至於開
經筵之講
幸
先師之廟即
===
世宗重道崇儒之義也
勤視朝之典復
面奏之儀即
世宗憂勤惕勵之念也申
赦宥之條辯寃抑之獄即
世宗好生矜恤之仁也噫是
心也一哉淵淵乎真有以默會
世宗之心而不泥於迹永惟
成憲之監而不拘於事矣此其駿惠之孝所
punctuated: 令主矣。其他推類以盡義，通變以宜民，如踐祚之初，屢卻羣臣勸進之章，非即世宗孝思之心乎？登極之詔，盡蠲遠年逋負之租，非即世宗憫農之意乎？至於開經筵之講，幸先師之廟，即世宗重道崇儒之義也；勤視朝之典，復面奏之儀，即世宗憂勤惕勵之念也；申赦宥之條，辯寃抑之獄，即世宗好生矜恤之仁也。噫！是心也，一哉！淵淵乎，真有以默會世宗之心而不泥於迹，永惟成憲之監而不拘於事矣。此其駿惠之孝所
translation_en: …an excellent ruler indeed. As for his other acts, he extends these principles by analogy to fulfill what is right, adapting to change for the people's benefit. For example, at the beginning of his accession, he repeatedly declined the memorials in which his ministers urged him to assume the throne: was this not the very same heart of filial devotion as Shizong's? His accession edict remitted in full the tax arrears accumulated in distant years: was this not the very same concern for farmers as Shizong's? His inauguration of lectures at the Classics Colloquium and his visit to the temple of the First Teacher, Confucius, embodied Shizong's commitment to honoring the Way and exalting Confucian learning. His diligent attendance at court audiences and restoration of the procedure for presenting memorials in person embodied Shizong's anxious diligence and vigilant resolve. His reaffirmation of provisions for pardon and clemency and his examination of cases involving wrongful conviction and oppression embodied Shizong's benevolence in cherishing life and showing compassion. Ah! These hearts are one! How profound! Truly, he has inwardly grasped Shizong's heart without clinging to its outward traces, and constantly reflects upon established precedents as a guide without being bound to particular acts. It is through this filial devotion, grandly following his predecessor, that…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
以嗣我
世宗永終之譽者不其善繼而善述矣乎夫有
是
燕貽之仁則固可以俟之後而不惑有是
駿惠之孝則亦可以考之前而不謬
前聖
後聖殊途同歸授守一道矣此固
宗社無疆之福生靈長久之慶也執事又謂
謹始慎終之道正本澄源之學此誠惓惓
===
愛
君無已之心也夫天下之治不難於始而難於
終治亂之幾不始於著而始於微我
皇上大德天縱
學問夙成致治保邦之圖謹始慎終之道固
已裕養於中矣然無已而言之惟在純心
與察幾而已夫心者萬化之原而幾者動
之微吉之先見者也要必於是心也主敬
以涵養之閑邪以固守之遠左右嬖倖之
punctuated:
以嗣我世宗永終之譽者，不其善繼而善述矣乎？夫有是燕貽之仁，則固可以俟之後而不惑；有是駿惠之孝，則亦可以考之前而不謬。前聖後聖，殊途同歸，授守一道矣。此固宗社無疆之福，生靈長久之慶也。

執事又謂謹始慎終之道、正本澄源之學，此誠惓惓愛君無已之心也。夫天下之治，不難於始而難於終；治亂之幾，不始於著而始於微。我皇上大德天縱，學問夙成，致治保邦之圖、謹始慎終之道，固已裕養於中矣。然無已而言之，惟在純心與察幾而已。夫心者，萬化之原；而幾者，動之微，吉之先見者也。要必於是心也，主敬以涵養之，閑邪以固守之，遠左右嬖倖之
translation_en:
…whereby he carries forward our Emperor Shizong’s enduring renown to the very end—is this not skillful succession and skillful continuation of his predecessor’s work? With such benevolence in bequeathing peace to posterity, one may indeed await those who come after without doubt; with such filial devotion in nobly following his predecessor, one may likewise be measured against those who came before without error. The former sage and the later sage reach the same destination by different paths; transmitting and preserving the legacy follow a single Way. This is indeed a boundless blessing for the ancestral temples and the altars of state, and a lasting cause for rejoicing among the people.

You also speak of the way of being circumspect at the beginning and careful to the end, and of the learning that rectifies the root and clarifies the source. This truly expresses your earnest and unceasing love for your sovereign. In governing all under Heaven, the difficulty lies not in the beginning but in the end; the incipient signs of order and disorder arise not in what is manifest but in what is subtle. Our emperor is endowed by Heaven with great virtue, and his learning matured early. His plans for bringing about good government and safeguarding the realm, and his commitment to circumspection at the beginning and care to the end, have surely already been amply nurtured within him. Yet, if one is to speak further, all depends upon purifying the heart and discerning incipient signs. The heart is the source of all transformations; incipient signs are the subtle beginnings of movement, the first manifestations of good fortune. What is essential, then, is to nurture this heart by making reverent attentiveness its governing principle, to guard it firmly by warding off depravity, and to keep at a distance the … of the favorites attending him…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
昵懼以淫吾之心也絶宮室輿馬之好懼
以侈吾之心也戒遊畋狩獵之行懼以馳
吾之心也却奇巧玩好之供懼以蕩吾之
心也拒左右近習之讒懼以惑吾之心也
於是幾也至明以察之至健以决之禁外
戚之乞恩防僭妄之幾也戒內豎之進言
杜竊柄之幾也去浮浪之費止奢侈之幾
也總獨斷之權防下移之幾也黜扶同之
訛禁黨與之幾也夫然後能純其心者自
===
可以臻純王之治而能察其幾者自可以
慎未然之防而與
世宗敬一之心法可以異世同符矣否則心有
不純則謹於始者怠於終幾有不察則所
謂端本澄源之道亦徒言而無益於實用
也雖然純心察幾斯二者則又有賴於親
賢焉蓋賢者所以講明吾心之理而剖析
是非之幾者也不親乎賢吾恐一心之微
衆欲攻之引之而去不難矣又安能以辨
punctuated: 昵，懼以淫吾之心也；絶宮室輿馬之好，懼以侈吾之心也；戒遊畋狩獵之行，懼以馳吾之心也；却奇巧玩好之供，懼以蕩吾之心也；拒左右近習之讒，懼以惑吾之心也。於是幾也，至明以察之，至健以决之。禁外戚之乞恩，防僭妄之幾也；戒內豎之進言，杜竊柄之幾也；去浮浪之費，止奢侈之幾也；總獨斷之權，防下移之幾也；黜扶同之訛，禁黨與之幾也。夫然後能純其心者，自可以臻純王之治；而能察其幾者，自可以慎未然之防，而與世宗敬一之心法，可以異世同符矣。否則，心有不純，則謹於始者怠於終；幾有不察，則所謂端本澄源之道，亦徒言而無益於實用也。雖然，純心察幾，斯二者則又有賴於親賢焉。蓋賢者，所以講明吾心之理，而剖析是非之幾者也。不親乎賢，吾恐一心之微，衆欲攻之，引之而去不難矣，又安能以辨
translation_en: …intimacy with them, for fear that it will corrupt one's heart; renounce a fondness for palaces, carriages, and horses, for fear that it will make one's heart extravagant; guard against excursions and hunting, for fear that they will set one's heart racing astray; decline offerings of ingenious curiosities and playthings, for fear that they will unsettle one's heart; and reject slander from intimate attendants, for fear that it will bewilder one's heart. As for these incipient tendencies, discern them with the utmost clarity and act upon them with the utmost resolution. Forbid imperial relatives by marriage from begging favors, to guard against the beginnings of presumptuous usurpation; guard against eunuchs' representations, to forestall the beginnings of their seizure of power; eliminate frivolous expenditure, to stop the beginnings of extravagance; retain sole authority to decide, to prevent power from passing downward; and reject the falsehoods of collusive assent, to prevent the beginnings of factionalism. Only then can one who purifies his heart attain the government of true kingship, and one who discerns incipient tendencies take careful precautions before troubles arise. Thus, though living in a different age, one may accord with Shizong's teaching of the mind, grounded in reverent attentiveness and singleness of purpose. Otherwise, if the heart is impure, care at the beginning will give way to negligence at the end; if incipient tendencies go unexamined, the so-called Way of rectifying the root and clearing the source will amount to empty words, without benefit in practice. Yet purifying the heart and discerning incipient tendencies both depend, in turn, upon drawing close to worthy men. For worthy men elucidate the principles within one's heart and distinguish the incipient tendencies toward right and wrong. Without drawing close to the worthy, I fear that the heart, subtle and vulnerable as it is, will be assailed by manifold desires and easily led astray. How, then, could one distinguish…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
天下之幾乎故曰純心要矣用賢急焉噫
此聖學致治之要機善繼善述之先務也
愚敢以是爲
今日獻
第二問
同考試官敎諭陸批我
皇上緝熈聖學媲美
皇祖超軼成周子能闡揚而歸重格心足占忠悃
===
考試官敎諭鎦批條答詳悉對揚得體殆窺
聖學之蘊奧者
考試官敎授熊批闡揚
聖學始終詳盡歸本正心忠愛藹然宜錄以式
人君有純王之道者有達天之德者也人
臣有輔德之功者有格心之學者也蓋天
德者王道之本君心者萬化之原是故人
君脩德以致治者必以務學爲急人臣輔
君以成德者必以正心爲要不然則其涵
punctuated:
天下之幾乎？故曰：純心要矣，用賢急焉。噫！此聖學致治之要機，善繼善述之先務也。愚敢以是爲今日獻。

第二問

同考試官敎諭陸批：我皇上緝熈聖學，媲美皇祖，超軼成周。子能闡揚而歸重格心，足占忠悃。

考試官敎諭鎦批：條答詳悉，對揚得體，殆窺聖學之蘊奧者。

考試官敎授熊批：闡揚聖學，始終詳盡，歸本正心，忠愛藹然，宜錄以式。

人君有純王之道者，有達天之德者也；人臣有輔德之功者，有格心之學者也。蓋天德者，王道之本；君心者，萬化之原。是故人君脩德以致治者，必以務學爲急；人臣輔君以成德者，必以正心爲要。不然，則其涵
translation_en:
…the subtle incipient developments throughout the realm? Thus I say: purifying the mind is essential; employing worthy men is urgent. Ah! These are the crucial means by which sagely learning brings about good government, and the foremost tasks in carrying forward and fulfilling one’s predecessors’ work. I venture to offer these thoughts for the present day.

Second Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: “Our Emperor continues and illuminates sagely learning, matching the excellence of his imperial ancestor and surpassing the perfected Zhou order. You have expounded this and placed the emphasis on rectifying the ruler’s mind, sufficiently revealing your loyal sincerity.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The answers to the individual points are thorough and detailed, and the response fittingly extols the imperial intentions. The writer seems to have glimpsed the profound mysteries of sagely learning.”

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: “The exposition of sagely learning is thorough from beginning to end and traces its foundation to rectifying the mind. Loyalty and affection are abundantly evident. It should be recorded as a model.”

A ruler who possesses the Way of pure kingly government possesses virtue that reaches Heaven; a minister who achieves merit in assisting the ruler’s virtue possesses the learning required to rectify the ruler’s mind. For heavenly virtue is the foundation of the kingly Way, and the ruler’s mind is the source of all transformation. Thus, a ruler who cultivates virtue to bring about good government must make diligent learning his urgent concern; a minister who assists his ruler in perfecting virtue must make rectifying the ruler’s mind his essential task. Otherwise, his nurturing…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
養本源之地者無以達乎天德又何以輔
理成化而致主於王道之隆也哉嗚呼知
此則知我
皇上之經筵日講必有以輔養
聖德而弼成盛治矣請得而詳言之夫天下之
治君爲之也人君之治天下心爲之也人
君以一心之微當衆欲之攻聲色貨利乘
間而竊發便嬖使令伺隙而暗投使非輔
導之以正人講明之以正學則本源一偏
===
末流滋甚是心也烏可不知所以養之也
哉稽古創業之君若堯舜禹之精一執中
湯文武之懋德建極卓乎不可尚矣至於
守成令主則莫如周成王而當時所以涵
育薰陶之者實由於輔導之力今考之於
周禮有保氏以諫其惡矣有師氏以詔其
媺矣而又有矇誦瞽箴士傳民語使之隨
事因時以致其規戒之益焉考之周書有
三公以論之於前矣有三孤以弼之於後
punctuated:
養本源之地者，無以達乎天德，又何以輔理成化，而致主於王道之隆也哉？嗚呼！知此，則知我皇上之經筵日講，必有以輔養聖德，而弼成盛治矣。請得而詳言之。夫天下之治，君爲之也；人君之治天下，心爲之也。人君以一心之微，當衆欲之攻，聲色貨利乘間而竊發，便嬖使令伺隙而暗投。使非輔導之以正人，講明之以正學，則本源一偏，末流滋甚。是心也，烏可不知所以養之也哉？
稽古創業之君，若堯舜禹之精一執中，湯文武之懋德建極，卓乎不可尚矣。至於守成令主，則莫如周成王，而當時所以涵育薰陶之者，實由於輔導之力。今考之於《周禮》，有保氏以諫其惡矣，有師氏以詔其媺矣，而又有矇誦、瞽箴、士傳、民語，使之隨事因時，以致其規戒之益焉。考之《周書》，有三公以論之於前矣，有三孤以弼之於後。
translation_en:
…those who nurture the root and source will have no means of attaining heavenly virtue. How, then, could they assist in government, accomplish moral transformation, and bring their sovereign to the full flourishing of the kingly Way? Ah! Understanding this, we know that our Emperor’s Classics Colloquium and daily lectures must help nourish his sagely virtue and assist in bringing about illustrious governance. Allow me to explain in detail. Order in the realm is brought about by the ruler; the ruler’s governance of the realm is brought about by his heart. With the subtle workings of a single heart, the ruler confronts the assaults of myriad desires. Music, sensual beauty, wealth, and profit seize opportunities to emerge stealthily; favorites and attendants watch for openings to insinuate themselves unseen. Unless upright men assist and guide him, and orthodox learning is expounded to enlighten him, any deviation at the source will become ever more serious downstream. How could one fail to understand the means of nourishing this heart?
When we examine the founding rulers of antiquity, such as Yao, Shun, and Yu, with their refinement and singleness of purpose in holding fast to the Mean, or Tang and Kings Wen and Wu, with their assiduous cultivation of virtue and establishment of the supreme standard, their eminence could not be surpassed. Among excellent rulers who preserved an inherited achievement, none equaled King Cheng of Zhou. The nurturing and formative influences upon him in his time truly owed their efficacy to the assistance and guidance he received. If we now examine the Rites of Zhou, there was a Protector to remonstrate against his faults and a Preceptor to instruct him in what was good. There were also blind men who recited and blind musicians who admonished, officers who transmitted instruction, and commoners who spoke, enabling him to benefit from counsel and warnings suited to each affair and occasion. Examining the Documents of Zhou, we find the Three Dukes discoursing before him and the Three Junior Counselors assisting him from behind…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣而又有綴衣虎賁趣馬小尹使之旦夕
侍御以致其承弼之助焉由是其德之成
也則詩人頌之曰成王不敢康夙夜基命
宥密又曰日就月將學有緝煕于光明此
在敬之與昊天之章者可攷也由是其治
之盛也則詩人歌之曰昭明有融高朗令
終又曰公尸燕飲福祿來成此在旣醉與
鳧鷖之章者可考也降是而漢風斯下矣
宣帝非不講論於石渠閣也而無補於甘
===
露之治章帝非不講論於白虎觀也而無
裨於元和之政唐太宗甞講於弘文館矣
而不免有慙德之羞宋哲宗甞講於崇政
殿矣而不能無虛拘之弊若此者君或志
於治而輔養之非其道臣或得其人而所
遇之非其主何恠乎治不古若而終不能
與成王以令主並稱於天下後世也哉洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝定鼎中夏混一區宇
punctuated:
矣，而又有綴衣、虎賁、趣馬、小尹，使之旦夕侍御，以致其承弼之助焉。由是其德之成也，則詩人頌之曰：「成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。」又曰：「日就月將，學有緝煕于光明。」此在《敬之》與《昊天》之章者可攷也。由是其治之盛也，則詩人歌之曰：「昭明有融，高朗令終。」又曰：「公尸燕飲，福祿來成。」此在《旣醉》與《鳧鷖》之章者可考也。降是而漢風斯下矣。宣帝非不講論於石渠閣也，而無補於甘露之治；章帝非不講論於白虎觀也，而無裨於元和之政。唐太宗甞講於弘文館矣，而不免有慙德之羞；宋哲宗甞講於崇政殿矣，而不能無虛拘之弊。若此者，君或志於治而輔養之非其道，臣或得其人而所遇之非其主，何恠乎治不古若，而終不能與成王以令主並稱於天下後世也哉！
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，定鼎中夏，混一區宇。
translation_en:
…and there were also Keepers of the Robes, Tiger Guards, Masters of the Horse, and minor administrators, who attended him morning and evening, thereby providing support and assistance. Thus, when his virtue reached perfection, the poets praised him: “King Cheng dared not rest at ease; morning and night he laid the foundations of the Mandate with magnanimity and quiet diligence.” They also said: “Advancing daily and progressing monthly, through learning attain continuous brightness.” These passages can be examined in the odes Admonition to Reverence (Jing zhi) and Vast Heaven (Hao tian). Likewise, when his government flourished, the poets sang: “Your radiant brightness spreads afar; lofty and brilliant, you bring matters to a good conclusion.” They also said: “The august personator of the ancestor feasts and drinks; blessings and emoluments come to fulfillment.” These passages can be examined in the odes Already Drunk (Ji zui) and Wild Ducks and Gulls (Fu yi).
After this, standards declined under the Han. It was not that Emperor Xuan failed to hold learned discussions at the Shiqu Pavilion, yet these brought no improvement to government during the Ganlu era. It was not that Emperor Zhang failed to hold learned discussions at the White Tiger Hall, yet these brought no benefit to government during the Yuanhe era. Emperor Taizong of the Tang held lectures at the Institute for the Advancement of Literature, yet could not escape the disgrace of moral failings. Emperor Zhezong of the Song held lectures in the Chongzheng Hall, yet could not avoid the defect of being constrained by empty formalities. In such cases, a ruler might aspire to good government, but the means used to assist and nurture him were improper; or suitable ministers might be found, but the sovereign they served was not the right one. Why wonder, then, that their government fell short of antiquity, and that they could never be acclaimed alongside King Cheng as worthy rulers throughout the realm and by later generations?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao established his dynasty in the Central Lands and united the realm…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖德神功已超越百王之上矣然尤於
萬幾之暇咨訪儒臣講究經史愚嘗莊誦
聖政日曆
皇明政要而有以仰窺其萬一矣自其論易於
華蓋殿而於頤卦得養民之職於家人悟誠
實威嚴之道焉自其論書於
武英殿而於無逸知兢業之方於洪範得天
人𩔖應之理焉自其論宋史於
左閤而於太宗則譏其治内藏於真宗則鄙
===
其為天書所惑焉是其隨
幸輒講初無間斷亦無常所也惟講讀
御於文華則正統元年始為禮儀定式其後
列聖相承率循無怠玆遇
皇上
聰明天啓
仁孝夙成嗣登
大寶勵精圖治嘗勤
視朝之典復
punctuated: 聖德神功已超越百王之上矣，然尤於萬幾之暇，咨訪儒臣，講究經史。愚嘗莊誦《聖政日曆》、《皇明政要》，而有以仰窺其萬一矣。自其論易於華蓋殿，而於頤卦得養民之職，於家人悟誠實威嚴之道焉；自其論書於武英殿，而於無逸知兢業之方，於洪範得天人𩔖應之理焉；自其論宋史於左閤，而於太宗則譏其治内藏，於真宗則鄙其為天書所惑焉。是其隨幸輒講，初無間斷，亦無常所也。惟講讀御於文華，則正統元年始為禮儀定式。其後列聖相承，率循無怠。玆遇皇上，聰明天啓，仁孝夙成，嗣登大寶，勵精圖治，嘗勤視朝之典，復
translation_en:
…his sagely virtue and divine achievements had already surpassed those of all former kings. Yet even amid his myriad affairs, he used his leisure to consult Confucian officials and investigate the classics and histories. I have reverently read the Daily Record of Sagely Governance and the Essentials of Governance of the August Ming, and thereby gained a glimpse of one ten-thousandth of his greatness. When he discussed the Book of Changes in Huagai Hall, he learned from the hexagram Nourishment the duty of nourishing the people, and from the hexagram The Family the way of sincerity, integrity, dignity, and sternness. When he discussed the Book of Documents in Wuying Hall, he learned from “Against Idleness” how to remain vigilant and diligent, and from “The Great Plan” the principle that Heaven and humanity respond to one another according to kind. When he discussed the History of the Song in the Left Pavilion, he criticized Emperor Taizong for managing his inner treasury and scorned Emperor Zhenzong for being deluded by the celestial writings. Thus, wherever he went, lectures were held; they were never interrupted, nor confined to a fixed location.

It was only in the first year of the Zhengtong reign (1436) that imperial attendance at lectures and readings in Wenhua Hall became a formally established ritual practice. Thereafter, successive sage emperors followed it without neglect. Now we have encountered Your Majesty, whose intelligence is Heaven-bestowed and whose benevolence and filial piety matured early. Having succeeded to the imperial throne, you have devoted your energies to good governance, diligently observed the rites of holding court, and restored…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
面奏之規而於
經筵日講又惓惓不敢後焉此與我
皇祖聖不自聖之心古帝王兢兢業業之念蓋
先後一揆者今日侍從
經筵之臣所以精白承休者當何如耶抑甞
觀宋諸儒之在經筵者矣有畫書無逸爲
圖以進者孫奭也有遇講日必焚香靜坐
欲以所言感悟人主者范祖禹也有反覆
開導覬有所啓悟者蘇軾也有講色莊嚴
===
每繼以諷諫者程頤也夫此四臣者陳善
閉邪豈非一代之良哉又甞觀我
朝儒臣之在
經筵者矣有學貫天人若宋濂者有節秉堅
貞若楊士奇者有掌經綸而擁佑
三朝若楊榮者有任學士而望冠一時若朱
善者有陳列十事若劉定之者夫此數臣
者謨明弼諧又豈非四臣之儔哉在今侍
從諸臣所以
punctuated:
面奏之規，而於經筵日講又惓惓不敢後焉。此與我皇祖聖不自聖之心、古帝王兢兢業業之念，蓋先後一揆者。今日侍從經筵之臣，所以精白承休者，當何如耶？

抑甞觀宋諸儒之在經筵者矣。有畫書無逸爲圖以進者，孫奭也；有遇講日必焚香靜坐，欲以所言感悟人主者，范祖禹也；有反覆開導，覬有所啓悟者，蘇軾也；有講色莊嚴，每繼以諷諫者，程頤也。夫此四臣者，陳善閉邪，豈非一代之良哉？

又甞觀我朝儒臣之在經筵者矣。有學貫天人若宋濂者，有節秉堅貞若楊士奇者，有掌經綸而擁佑三朝若楊榮者，有任學士而望冠一時若朱善者，有陳列十事若劉定之者。夫此數臣者，謨明弼諧，又豈非四臣之儔哉？在今侍從諸臣所以
translation_en:
…the practice of presenting matters orally to the throne; and he is likewise unremitting in his concern for the Classics Colloquium and daily lectures, never daring to give them lesser priority. This accords with the spirit of our imperial ancestor, who possessed sagely wisdom yet did not regard himself as a sage, and with the vigilant, conscientious disposition of the ancient emperors and kings: earlier and later rulers alike follow the same standard. How, then, should the officials attending upon the Classics Colloquium today purify their intentions and receive this beneficence?

I have also considered the Confucian scholars who served at the Classics Colloquium under the Song. Sun Shi made illustrations of “Against Luxurious Ease,” a chapter of the Book of Documents, and presented them to the throne. Fan Zuyu invariably burned incense and sat quietly on lecture days, hoping that his words would move and awaken the ruler. Su Shi explained and guided repeatedly, hoping to bring the ruler to understanding. Cheng Yi maintained a solemn demeanor when lecturing and regularly followed his lectures with indirect remonstrance. These four ministers set forth what was good and barred what was pernicious. Were they not outstanding men of their age?

I have also considered the Confucian ministers of our own dynasty who served at the Classics Colloquium. There was Song Lian, whose learning encompassed Heaven and humanity; Yang Shiqi, whose integrity was firm and steadfast; Yang Rong, who directed affairs of state and supported three reigns; Zhu Shan, who served as Academician and whose reputation surpassed all others of his time; and Liu Dingzhi, who set forth ten matters for consideration. These ministers offered enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance. Were they not peers of those four ministers? As for the means by which the attendant ministers of today…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
匡賛匹休者又何如耶夫上之承休乎
聖君下之匹休乎賢佐其道豈有他哉亦曰以
講學爲功以正心爲要耳盖性之所主原
切於理而難於存養是卽所謂道心情之
所向多溺於欲而易於縱逸是卽所謂人
心然於道心而不時爲之培植則微者愈
微於人心而不嚴爲之克制則危者愈危
故當進講之時必析理欲之分嚴敬肆之
辨指其方動之初决其流弊之極約其幾
===
於獨知之地舉其要於克己之功自不覩
不聞之中以至於應事應物之際務使道
心爲主而人心聽命焉則萬化之本原已
端矣由是於講書之後凡遇五府軍政六
部要務一遵
大明會典條陳而悉數之軍伍如何以實之吏
治如何以飭之財賦如何以足之禮樂如
何以敷之兵威如何以張之刑辟如何以
明之興作如何以省之善則都之否則吁
punctuated:
匡賛匹休者，又何如耶？夫上之承休乎聖君，下之匹休乎賢佐，其道豈有他哉？亦曰以講學爲功，以正心爲要耳。盖性之所主，原切於理，而難於存養，是卽所謂道心；情之所向，多溺於欲，而易於縱逸，是卽所謂人心。然於道心而不時爲之培植，則微者愈微；於人心而不嚴爲之克制，則危者愈危。故當進講之時，必析理欲之分，嚴敬肆之辨，指其方動之初，决其流弊之極，約其幾於獨知之地，舉其要於克己之功。自不覩不聞之中，以至於應事應物之際，務使道心爲主，而人心聽命焉，則萬化之本原已端矣。
由是於講書之後，凡遇五府軍政、六部要務，一遵《大明會典》，條陳而悉數之：軍伍如何以實之？吏治如何以飭之？財賦如何以足之？禮樂如何以敷之？兵威如何以張之？刑辟如何以明之？興作如何以省之？善則都之，否則吁
translation_en:
…how, then, do they provide corrective assistance and match such excellence? To receive the blessings of the sage ruler above and match the excellence of worthy assistants below—could there be any other way? It consists simply in making the exposition of learning their work and the rectification of the mind their essential concern. What our nature governs is inherently close to principle, yet difficult to preserve and nurture: this is what is called the moral mind. What our feelings incline toward is often submerged in desire and readily lapses into indulgence: this is what is called the human mind. If the moral mind is not continually cultivated, what is subtle becomes ever subtler; if the human mind is not strictly restrained, what is precarious becomes ever more precarious. Thus, when delivering lectures before the throne, they must distinguish principle from desire, draw a strict distinction between reverence and laxity, identify impulses at their very inception, and determine the ultimate harmful consequences to which they lead. They must attend to these incipient movements where only the self is aware of them, and grasp the essentials through the work of overcoming the self. From the realm of what is neither seen nor heard to occasions of responding to affairs and things, they must ensure that the moral mind governs and the human mind obeys. Then the source of all transformation will have been set right.
Accordingly, after lecturing on the books, whenever military administration under the Five Chief Military Commissions or important business of the Six Ministries arises, they should follow the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming throughout, presenting matters item by item and enumerating them fully. How can military ranks be filled? How can the administration of officials be put in order? How can fiscal revenues be made sufficient? How can rites and music be widely extended? How can military might be strengthened? How can penal laws be clarified? How can construction projects be reduced? If something is good, acclaim it; if it is not, voice disapproval…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
之是則俞之非則咈之知之者無不言言
之者無不盡如此則知行竝進內外交脩
聖學緝熈純一不已虛靈澄徹義理昭明
聖德日躋于大成
盛治日臻于熈皡矣其於我
聖祖也則爲善繼善述於堯舜禹湯文武也則
爲同治同道雖成王且駕軼其上矣而況
漢唐宋之諸君也哉愚何幸躬逢其盛
第三問
同考試官教諭宋 批 發明仁義異同之故有根
據有體驗其獨得孔孟之宗旨者歟
同考試官教授唐 批 論仁義一一本之心匪析理
者不能爲此說宜錄以式
同考試官教授劉 批 剖析仁義精深詳盡是知
性者也錄之以示來學豈惟以其文哉
考試官教諭鎦 批 根極理要灼見指歸
考試官教授熊 批 議論純正
punctuated:
之，是則俞之，非則咈之。知之者無不言，言之者無不盡。如此，則知行竝進，內外交脩，聖學緝熈，純一不已，虛靈澄徹，義理昭明，聖德日躋于大成，盛治日臻于熈皡矣。其於我聖祖也，則爲善繼善述；於堯舜禹湯文武也，則爲同治同道。雖成王，且駕軼其上矣，而況漢唐宋之諸君也哉！愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第三問

同考試官教諭宋批：發明仁義異同之故，有根據，有體驗，其獨得孔孟之宗旨者歟！

同考試官教授唐批：論仁義，一一本之心，匪析理者不能爲此說，宜錄以式。

同考試官教授劉批：剖析仁義，精深詳盡，是知性者也。錄之以示來學，豈惟以其文哉！

考試官教諭鎦批：根極理要，灼見指歸。

考試官教授熊批：議論純正。
translation_en:
…reject it; approve what is right and oppose what is wrong. Let those who know speak without withholding anything, and let those who speak express all they have to say. Thus knowledge and action will advance together, and inner and outer cultivation will proceed in concert. Your Majesty’s sagely learning will grow ever more luminous, remaining pure and undivided without cease; the mind will be open, responsive, clear, and penetrating, and moral principles brilliantly manifest. Your sagely virtue will daily advance toward its fullest perfection, and your flourishing rule will daily approach radiant harmony. In relation to our sagely progenitor, this will constitute skillful succession to his work and fulfillment of his purposes; in relation to Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, it will constitute shared governance and a shared Way. You will surpass even King Cheng—how much more, then, the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song! How fortunate I, in my humble ignorance, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

Third Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Instructor: The elucidation of why benevolence and righteousness are alike and different has both a firm basis and grounding in personal experience. Has he not uniquely grasped the essential teachings of Confucius and Mencius?

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Professor: In discussing benevolence and righteousness, he roots each in the mind. Only someone who analyzes principle could offer such an account. It should be selected as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu 劉, Professor: His analysis of benevolence and righteousness is profound, detailed, and exhaustive. Here is someone who understands human nature. We select this to instruct future students—surely not merely for its literary merits!

Comment by Examiner Liu 鎦, Instructor: He traces the essentials of principle to their very roots and clearly perceives their ultimate purport.

Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: The argument is pure and correct.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
夫性之在吾心也一而已矣諸儒之論性
也亦一而已矣何也理有異名而性無殊
貫也夫惟其有異名也則其立言自不能
以强而同夫惟其無殊貫也則其論性也
亦不容以岐而二是故仁義者性之德也
而異同者理之辨也必有盡性之功者而
後可以達所性之蘊必有析理之精者而
後可以辨同異之旨儒者以盡性之學倡
天下而不免於立論之殊豈故立異說以
===
惑人哉要之其言之殊者時之異也而未
始不同者心之一也達性德於異論之中
迪妙旨於微詞之內非盡性之極析理之
精者其孰能之吁此之謂性學也而愚生
烏足以語此雖然仁義吾性也盡性吾分
也請因明問而分析其同異之故可乎今
夫天下之理其始則一太極也太極分而
有動靜則爲陰爲陽爲剛爲柔皆太極之
分見也故天得之以立命則曰陰與陽地
punctuated: 夫性之在吾心也，一而已矣；諸儒之論性也，亦一而已矣。何也？理有異名，而性無殊貫也。夫惟其有異名也，則其立言自不能以强而同；夫惟其無殊貫也，則其論性也亦不容以岐而二。是故仁義者，性之德也；而異同者，理之辨也。必有盡性之功者，而後可以達所性之蘊；必有析理之精者，而後可以辨同異之旨。儒者以盡性之學倡天下，而不免於立論之殊，豈故立異說以惑人哉？要之，其言之殊者，時之異也；而未始不同者，心之一也。達性德於異論之中，迪妙旨於微詞之內，非盡性之極、析理之精者，其孰能之？吁！此之謂性學也，而愚生烏足以語此？雖然，仁義吾性也，盡性吾分也。請因明問而分析其同異之故，可乎？今夫天下之理，其始則一太極也。太極分而有動靜，則爲陰爲陽，爲剛爲柔，皆太極之分見也。故天得之以立命，則曰陰與陽；地
translation_en: Human nature as it resides in my mind is simply one; the various Confucian scholars’ discussions of human nature likewise concern this one unity. Why is this? Principle has different names, but human nature has no divergent underlying thread. Precisely because the names differ, their formulations cannot forcibly be made identical; precisely because the underlying thread does not diverge, their accounts of human nature cannot be allowed to branch into two. Thus benevolence and righteousness are virtues of human nature, while their similarities and differences involve distinctions within principle. Only those who have worked to realize their nature fully can penetrate the depths of their inherent nature; only those who analyze principle precisely can discern the significance of these similarities and differences. Confucian scholars advocate throughout the world the learning that fully realizes human nature, yet their formulations inevitably differ. Could they deliberately devise divergent doctrines to confuse people? In essence, their statements differ because their times differ; what has never ceased to be the same is the unity of the mind. Who could comprehend the virtues of human nature amid divergent arguments and discern profound meanings within subtle expressions, unless they had attained the utmost realization of their nature and precision in analyzing principle? Ah! This is what is called the learning of human nature. How could an ignorant student such as I be qualified to discuss it? Nevertheless, benevolence and righteousness are my nature, and fully realizing that nature is my duty. May I therefore take your illuminating question as the occasion to analyze the reasons for their similarities and differences? Now, the principles of all things under Heaven originate in the single Supreme Ultimate (taiji). As the Supreme Ultimate differentiates, movement and stillness arise, becoming yin and yang, firmness and yielding: all are differentiated manifestations of the Supreme Ultimate. Thus, when Heaven receives it to establish its ordained order, these are called yin and yang; Earth…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
得之以奠形則曰柔與剛惟其分見於天
地也故名不得不殊惟其同出於太極也
則理未始不一仰觀天文則晝夜一氣也
上下一化也俯察地理則南北異勢而同
運也高深異齊而同機也時乎陰時乎陽
時乎柔時乎剛而實非判而爲二者也嗚
呼觀天地則知吾人觀陰陽剛柔則知仁
義之性矣彼立人之道曰仁與義則仁義
之理本乎天道之陰陽地道之剛柔而合
===
之以成性者也其分則有先有後其質則
有偏有全其具則有體有用其機則有內
有外其實一也非二物也是故自其渾然
合一者而言之曰仁人心也義人路也初
未名言其體用爲何物也此孟子之說也
自其融會貫通者言之曰仁者心之德愛
之理義者心之制事之宜則始該體用而
形容之此朱子之說也孟子論性之本故
此二言者形容最爲切要朱子論性之用
punctuated:
得之以奠形，則曰柔與剛。惟其分見於天地也，故名不得不殊；惟其同出於太極也，則理未始不一。仰觀天文，則晝夜一氣也，上下一化也；俯察地理，則南北異勢而同運也，高深異齊而同機也。時乎陰，時乎陽，時乎柔，時乎剛，而實非判而爲二者也。嗚呼！觀天地則知吾人，觀陰陽剛柔則知仁義之性矣。彼「立人之道曰仁與義」，則仁義之理，本乎天道之陰陽、地道之剛柔，而合之以成性者也。其分則有先有後，其質則有偏有全，其具則有體有用，其機則有內有外，其實一也，非二物也。
是故，自其渾然合一者而言之，曰「仁，人心也；義，人路也」，初未名言其體用爲何物也。此孟子之說也。自其融會貫通者言之，曰「仁者，心之德、愛之理；義者，心之制、事之宜」，則始該體用而形容之。此朱子之說也。孟子論性之本，故此二言者形容最爲切要；朱子論性之用
translation_en:
…when Earth receives it to establish its form, these are called the yielding and the firm. Precisely because it manifests separately in Heaven and Earth, its names must differ; precisely because these manifestations issue alike from the Supreme Ultimate, their principle has never been other than one. Looking upward at the patterns of Heaven, we see that day and night share a single vital energy, and above and below share a single process of transformation. Looking downward at the configurations of Earth, we see that north and south differ in their disposition yet participate in the same movement; heights and depths differ in level yet share the same animating impulse. At one time yin, at another yang; at one time yielding, at another firm: in reality, these are not divided into two. Ah! By contemplating Heaven and Earth, we understand ourselves; by contemplating yin and yang, firmness and yielding, we understand our nature of benevolence and righteousness. The saying, “Establishing the Way of humanity, one calls it benevolence and righteousness,” means that the principles of benevolence and righteousness are rooted in the yin and yang of Heaven’s Way and the firmness and yielding of Earth’s Way, united to constitute human nature. In their differentiation there is precedence and succession; in their constitution, partiality and completeness; in their endowment, substance and function; in their operation, the internal and the external. In reality they are one, not two things.
Thus, speaking of their undivided unity, one says, “Benevolence is the human heart; righteousness is the human path,” without yet explicitly identifying what their substance and function are. This is Mengzi’s account. Speaking of their integration and thorough interconnection, one says, “Benevolence is the virtue of the heart and the principle of love; righteousness is the heart’s regulation and what is fitting in affairs.” Only then are substance and function comprehensively described. This is Zhuzi’s account. Mengzi discusses the foundation of human nature, and so these two statements describe it with the utmost precision and relevance; Zhuzi discusses the functioning of human nature…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
故此六字者乃先儒之所未發而文公始
發之故有功於學者孟子也朱子也其言
各有攸當耳究而言之則孟子未發之旨
卽涵乎朱子之已發而朱子已發之旨卽
擴充孟子之未發也七篇之中無非此理
觀其論惻隱而以爲仁之端論辭讓而以
爲義之端非體用之謂乎自其專言之則
仁包四德此孔門之言也自其竝言之則
義對仁者而言此孟子之言也夫仁爲統
===
體專言之固可以包夫四德仁義同體而
異用偏言之則一事而義可以對仁是則
仁之所以包夫四者固未甞離夫偏言之
一事亦未有不識夫偏言之一事而可以
驟語專言之統體也故曰仁義之道常相
須而孟子之言淵源於孔子者也况戰國
之時性學不明於天下以仁義爲性中之
所無者有之以仁義分內外而不復以集
義爲事者有之杞柳湍水之喻無善無不
punctuated:
故此六字者，乃先儒之所未發，而文公始發之，故有功於學者。孟子也，朱子也，其言各有攸當耳。究而言之，則孟子未發之旨，卽涵乎朱子之已發；而朱子已發之旨，卽擴充孟子之未發也。七篇之中，無非此理。觀其論惻隱而以爲仁之端，論辭讓而以爲義之端，非體用之謂乎？自其專言之，則仁包四德，此孔門之言也；自其竝言之，則義對仁者而言，此孟子之言也。夫仁爲統體，專言之固可以包夫四德；仁義同體而異用，偏言之則一事，而義可以對仁。是則仁之所以包夫四者，固未甞離夫偏言之一事；亦未有不識夫偏言之一事，而可以驟語專言之統體也。故曰仁義之道常相須，而孟子之言淵源於孔子者也。
况戰國之時，性學不明於天下，以仁義爲性中之所無者有之；以仁義分內外，而不復以集義爲事者有之。杞柳湍水之喻，無善無不
translation_en:
… Thus these six characters express what earlier Confucian scholars had not articulated and what Zhu Xi, Duke Wen, first brought to light; hence his contribution to learners. The statements of Mengzi and Zhu Xi each have their proper application. Examined fully, the meaning that Mengzi left unexpressed is contained in what Zhu Xi expressed, while what Zhu Xi expressed expands upon what Mengzi left unexpressed. Throughout the seven books of the Mengzi, there is nothing that does not embody this principle. Consider how he discusses compassion as the beginning of benevolence, and deference as the beginning of righteousness [?]: is this not a matter of substance and function? When benevolence is spoken of alone, it encompasses the four virtues: this is the teaching of the school of Kongzi. When the virtues are spoken of alongside one another, righteousness is discussed in relation to benevolence: this is Mengzi’s teaching. Benevolence constitutes the comprehensive whole, so when spoken of alone it can indeed encompass the four virtues. Benevolence and righteousness share the same substance but differ in function; when spoken of in its particular aspect, benevolence is one matter, and righteousness can be set alongside it. Thus benevolence’s encompassing all four virtues has never been separate from the particular matter denoted when it is spoken of in its limited sense. Nor can anyone who fails to understand that particular matter abruptly proceed to discuss the comprehensive whole denoted when benevolence is spoken of alone. Hence it is said that the ways of benevolence and righteousness always require one another, and that Mengzi’s teaching has its source in Kongzi.
Moreover, during the Warring States period, the study of human nature was not clearly understood throughout the realm. Some held that benevolence and righteousness were absent from human nature; others divided benevolence and righteousness into the internal and the external, and no longer made the accumulation of righteous deeds their concern. The analogies of willow wood and swirling water, the claim that human nature is neither good nor …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
善之說紛紛籍籍著赤幟於天下此孟子
別而言之正以指其迷途而引之於正大
高明之域先儒謂其開關啓鑰而有功於
聖人之門詎不信夫至若韓子原道之篇
以博愛言仁以行而宜之言義乃反以小
吾仁義者也程子非之是矣而周子德愛
曰仁宜曰義之語則亦指仁義一事之用
言之耳况原道之作愈爲闢佛老而發也
通書之作周子指五行而言也要之言有
===
純疵而理無加損也孟子說仁義禮智義
在第二太極圖以義配利則義在第三禮
是陽故曰亨智是陰故曰貞仁義禮智猶
言東西南北孟子指其相對言之也元亨
利貞猶言東南西北周子指其一邊言之
也其言雖異其理則一安得有先後之間
哉仁是柔底物合屬陰義是剛底物合屬
陽而不知舒暢發達便是剛底意思此仁
之所以屬陽也收斂藏縮便是柔底意思
punctuated:
善之說，紛紛籍籍，著赤幟於天下。此孟子別而言之，正以指其迷途，而引之於正大高明之域。先儒謂其開關啓鑰而有功於聖人之門，詎不信夫！至若韓子《原道》之篇，以博愛言仁，以行而宜之言義，乃反以小吾仁義者也。程子非之，是矣。而周子「德愛曰仁，宜曰義」之語，則亦指仁義一事之用言之耳。况《原道》之作，愈爲闢佛老而發也；《通書》之作，周子指五行而言也。要之，言有純疵，而理無加損也。
孟子說仁義禮智，義在第二；《太極圖》以義配利，則義在第三。禮是陽，故曰亨；智是陰，故曰貞。仁義禮智，猶言東西南北，孟子指其相對言之也；元亨利貞，猶言東南西北，周子指其一邊言之也。其言雖異，其理則一，安得有先後之間哉？仁是柔底物，合屬陰；義是剛底物，合屬陽。而不知舒暢發達，便是剛底意思，此仁之所以屬陽也；收斂藏縮，便是柔底意思。
translation_en:
…good”—such doctrines proliferated in noisy profusion, raising their red banners throughout the realm. Mengzi spoke of benevolence and righteousness separately precisely to point out these mistaken paths and lead people into a realm of rectitude, greatness, loftiness, and illumination. Earlier Confucian scholars said that he opened the barrier and unlocked the gate, rendering service to the gateway of the sages. Is this not indeed true? As for Master Han’s essay “An Inquiry into the Way” (Yuan dao), it explains benevolence as universal love and righteousness as acting appropriately, thereby actually diminishing our benevolence and righteousness. Master Cheng was right to criticize it. Yet Master Zhou’s words, “Virtuous love is called benevolence [?]; appropriateness is called righteousness,” likewise refer only to the operation of benevolence and righteousness in particular affairs. Moreover, Han Yu wrote “An Inquiry into the Way” to refute Buddhism and Daoism, whereas Master Zhou wrote the Book of Penetration (Tong shu) with reference to the Five Phases. In essence, formulations may be sound or flawed, but principle itself undergoes neither increase nor diminution.
When Mengzi speaks of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, righteousness comes second; in the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu), righteousness is paired with benefit, and thus comes third. Ritual propriety is yang, and hence is called “success”; wisdom is yin, and hence is called “constancy.” Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are like saying east, west, south, and north: Mengzi speaks of them in opposing pairs. Origination, success, benefit, and constancy are like saying east, south, west, and north: Master Zhou speaks of them in sequence around the sides. Though their formulations differ, their principle is one. How could there be any distinction of priority or posteriority? Benevolence is something yielding and should belong to yin; righteousness is something firm and should belong to yang. But this overlooks the fact that free expansion and flourishing growth express precisely the meaning of firmness: this is why benevolence belongs to yang. Gathering inward, storing away, and contracting express precisely the meaning of yielding…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
此義之所以屬陰也禮配夫亨於時爲夏
夏則春之長也造化之顯諸仁也智配夫
貞於時爲冬冬則秋之收也造化之藏諸
用也孔子也孟子也周子也韓子程子也
言之或詳或略或離或合或深或淺而其
道理則未始不相值也是故諸儒之論隨
時以明道而未嘗有叛於道觀諸儒之論
者要皆得意以通言而不可泥言以滯道
也理之在人心一而已矣諸儒豈有異言
===
哉雖然非盡仁義之性者不足以語此亦
非盡仁義之功者不足以及此蓋仁義之
存於吾心顯於事爲有定理無常形最不
可以易識也君子由窮理之功以造於力
行之地由體驗之學以至於神而明之之
境則內外交孚體用互發仁義之變化在
我矣又何有於同異也哉故曰衆言淆亂
折諸聖愚則曰衆言淆亂折諸心
第四問
punctuated:
此義之所以屬陰也。禮配夫亨，於時爲夏；夏則春之長也，造化之顯諸仁也。智配夫貞，於時爲冬；冬則秋之收也，造化之藏諸用也。孔子也，孟子也，周子也，韓子、程子也，言之或詳或略，或離或合，或深或淺，而其道理則未始不相值也。是故諸儒之論，隨時以明道，而未嘗有叛於道。觀諸儒之論者，要皆得意以通言，而不可泥言以滯道也。理之在人心，一而已矣，諸儒豈有異言哉？雖然，非盡仁義之性者，不足以語此；亦非盡仁義之功者，不足以及此。蓋仁義之存於吾心、顯於事爲，有定理，無常形，最不可以易識也。君子由窮理之功，以造於力行之地；由體驗之學，以至於神而明之之境，則內外交孚，體用互發，仁義之變化在我矣，又何有於同異也哉？故曰：「衆言淆亂，折諸聖。」愚則曰：「衆言淆亂，折諸心。」

第四問
translation_en:
…This is why righteousness belongs to yin. Ritual propriety corresponds to heng, flourishing, and among the seasons to summer. Summer is the further growth of spring: the creative transformations of Heaven and Earth manifest themselves in benevolence. Wisdom corresponds to zhen, constancy, and among the seasons to winter. Winter is the gathering in of autumn: those creative transformations conceal themselves within their operation. Confucius, Mencius, Master Zhou, Master Han, and Master Cheng spoke sometimes in detail and sometimes briefly, sometimes separately and sometimes collectively, sometimes profoundly and sometimes simply; yet the principles they expressed invariably accorded with one another. Thus the discussions of the various Confucian scholars elucidated the Way according to their times, without ever departing from it. Those who study their discussions must grasp their meaning in order to comprehend their words; they must not cling to the words and thereby obstruct their understanding of the Way. Principle within the human heart is one and nothing more. How could these scholars have spoken at variance with one another?

Nevertheless, only those who fully realize the nature of benevolence and righteousness can discuss this, and only those who fully accomplish the work of benevolence and righteousness can attain it. For benevolence and righteousness, residing in our hearts and manifesting themselves in our actions, have fixed principles but no constant form; they are especially difficult to discern readily. Through the work of investigating principle to the utmost, the gentleman reaches the realm of earnest practice; through learning grounded in personal experience, he reaches the state of spiritually penetrating understanding. Then inner and outer mutually accord, and substance and function bring each other into expression. The transformations of benevolence and righteousness lie within oneself: what further concern can there be over agreement or difference? Thus it is said: “When the many statements are confused and disorderly, adjudicate them by reference to the sages.” I, in my humble view, would say: “When the many statements are confused and disorderly, adjudicate them by reference to the heart.”

Fourth Question

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭梅批條析久任超陞利弊精確
詳明是必留心民牧者
考試官教諭錙批條答無遺且有經畫
考試官教授熊批是有知人安民之略者
人君之用人也固不可無鼓舞之方而尤
貴乎有甄別之智鼓舞之方激勸之而已
矣甄別之智綜核之而已矣蓋激勸之典
不昭則賢者無所勉而不肖者無所懲綜
===
核之法不明則不肖者得詭迹以取譽而
賢者反不得以自見其何以振厲才賢而
奔走豪傑也哉今夫生民之休戚天下之
治亂關焉守令之賢否生民之休戚係焉
蓋守令者於民最親其惠易流而其虐亦
易及故吏民之本守令為急而其選不可
不慎在上之人所以風勵而化導之者不
可無其具耳執事下問慨然思古循良之
吏欲得其人以弘化理顧非承學所敢知
punctuated:
同考試官教諭梅批：條析久任、超陞利弊，精確詳明，是必留心民牧者。
考試官教諭錙批：條答無遺，且有經畫。
考試官教授熊批：是有知人安民之略者。
人君之用人也，固不可無鼓舞之方，而尤貴乎有甄別之智。鼓舞之方，激勸之而已矣；甄別之智，綜核之而已矣。蓋激勸之典不昭，則賢者無所勉，而不肖者無所懲；綜核之法不明，則不肖者得詭迹以取譽，而賢者反不得以自見，其何以振厲才賢而奔走豪傑也哉？今夫生民之休戚，天下之治亂關焉；守令之賢否，生民之休戚係焉。蓋守令者於民最親，其惠易流，而其虐亦易及。故吏民之本，守令為急，而其選不可不慎。在上之人所以風勵而化導之者，不可無其具耳。執事下問，慨然思古循良之吏，欲得其人以弘化理，顧非承學所敢知
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Mei, Instructor, comments: “The benefits and drawbacks of long tenure and accelerated promotion are analyzed point by point, precisely and clearly. This must be someone who takes an interest in those who shepherd the people.”
Examiner Zi [?], Instructor, comments: “The response addresses every point without omission and also offers considered plans.”
Examiner Xiong, Professor, comments: “Here is someone with a grasp of how to discern men’s abilities and bring peace to the people.”
When a ruler employs men, he certainly cannot dispense with methods of encouragement, but still more valuable is the discernment to distinguish among them. Methods of encouragement amount simply to stimulating and exhorting them; discernment in distinguishing among them amounts simply to comprehensive scrutiny. If the established measures for encouragement are not clearly displayed, the worthy have nothing to spur them on, and the unworthy have nothing to restrain them. If the methods of scrutiny are unclear, the unworthy can disguise their conduct to win praise, while the worthy, conversely, cannot make themselves known. How, then, can one rouse the talented and worthy and bring outstanding men into active service?
Now, the order or disorder of the realm depends upon the well-being or suffering of the people; the well-being or suffering of the people depends upon whether prefects and magistrates are worthy. Prefects and magistrates are closest to the people: their beneficence readily spreads, and their cruelty likewise readily reaches them. Thus, in the foundations of administration and the people’s welfare, prefects and magistrates are the urgent concern, and their selection must be undertaken with care. Those above them must possess the means to inspire, encourage, transform, and guide them.
You, sir, have condescended to put this question, earnestly recalling the conscientious and benevolent officials of antiquity and wishing to obtain such men to extend moral transformation and good government. Yet this is hardly something that I, a student, dare claim to understand…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
也然嘗考其世論其人矣請因明問而敬
陳之自封建之法廢而郡縣之制興秦罷
侯置守裂天下而爲郡縣漢因其故設刺
史二千石長吏以分治天下當是時天子
數召見問治效下璽書褒美增秩賜金公
卿缺則選諸所表以用之故三代而下稱
漢之吏治烝烝近古是以一時得人之選
如吳公之於河南廣漢之於京兆信臣之
於南陽延壽之於潁川龔遂之於渤海皆
===
彰彰表著者也由漢而唐尤重其任不歷
刺史不得任侍郎不歷郡縣不得任臺省
故一時循良之吏若賈敦頤之於冀州鄭
德本之於瀛州薛大鼎之於滄州又有令
武陽而孜孜惠愛令昌邑而以俸代輸者
皆籍籍可稱者也不可謂不盛矣然以漢
之宣帝而有王成之奸以偽增戶口而受
賞豈非採名之過而巧於飾名者遂得以
售其欺耶以唐之德宗而有陽城之賢以
punctuated:
也。然嘗考其世，論其人矣。請因明問而敬陳之。自封建之法廢，而郡縣之制興，秦罷侯置守，裂天下而爲郡縣。漢因其故，設刺史、二千石、長吏，以分治天下。當是時，天子數召見，問治效，下璽書褒美，增秩賜金；公卿缺，則選諸所表以用之。故三代而下，稱漢之吏治烝烝近古。是以一時得人之選，如吳公之於河南、廣漢之於京兆、信臣之於南陽、延壽之於潁川、龔遂之於渤海，皆彰彰表著者也。
由漢而唐，尤重其任。不歷刺史，不得任侍郎；不歷郡縣，不得任臺省。故一時循良之吏，若賈敦頤之於冀州、鄭德本之於瀛州、薛大鼎之於滄州，又有令武陽而孜孜惠愛、令昌邑而以俸代輸者，皆籍籍可稱者也，不可謂不盛矣。然以漢之宣帝，而有王成之奸，以偽增戶口而受賞，豈非採名之過，而巧於飾名者遂得以售其欺耶？以唐之德宗，而有陽城之賢，以
translation_en:
… Yet I have studied their times and considered the men themselves. Allow me respectfully to set forth my views in response to your discerning question. Once the system of enfeoffment was abolished and the system of commanderies and counties arose, the Qin abolished the feudal lords and appointed commandery governors, dividing the realm into commanderies and counties. The Han followed this precedent, establishing regional inspectors, officials ranked at two thousand bushels, and senior local officials to share in governing the realm. At that time, the Son of Heaven frequently summoned them to audience and asked about the results of their administration. He issued sealed letters of praise, increased their official emoluments, and bestowed gold. When vacancies arose among the highest ministers, he selected appointees from those who had been commended. Thus, among the ages following the Three Dynasties, Han administration is praised for its flourishing excellence, approaching that of antiquity. Among the successful selections of men in that age, Lord Wu in Henan, Guanghan in Jingzhao, Xinchen in Nanyang, Yanshou in Yingchuan, and Gong Sui in Bohai were all conspicuously distinguished.
From the Han to the Tang, still greater importance was attached to these responsibilities. Anyone who had not served as a prefect could not become a vice minister; anyone who had not served in commandery or county administration could not hold office in the central administrative agencies. Thus, among the benevolent officials of that age were Jia Dunyi in Jizhou, Zheng Deben in Yingzhou, and Xue Dading in Cangzhou. There were also one who, as magistrate of Wuyang, worked tirelessly to show kindness and care, and another who, as magistrate of Changyi, used his own salary to pay the people's taxes. All enjoyed reputations worthy of praise. This must indeed be called an age rich in such men. Yet even under Emperor Xuan of the Han, there was the deceitful Wang Cheng, who received rewards by falsely inflating the registered numbers of households and people. Was this not the fault of judging by reputation, which allowed those skilled at embellishing their reputations to make their deception succeed? Under Emperor Dezong of the Tang, there was the worthy Yang Cheng, who, on account of…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
催科政拙而被抑豈非求治之過而勞心
撫字者反不得以聞於上耶若此者激勸
之典雖行而綜核之法未盡無恠乎賢不
肖之混淆也已我
國家倣古為治設官分職而於守令之選為
尤重
今天子臨御之初勤恤民隱嘉惠元元
登極一詔首飭吏治一時郡縣之吏爭自濯
磨喁喁嚮風矣中間如召父杜母循良卓
===
異者固多而竭澤而漁飾實眩名以盜隆
虛譽者未敢謂盡無也玆欲求吏治如吳
公輩以稱
皇上重本之意豈無其道乎夫吳公治行載籍
無所見然史稱治平第一帝召以為廷尉
夫文帝好文之主專務以德化民躬行節
儉庶幾成康不知其臣其君可知也蓋守
令者牧民者也牧民者勿擾之而已吾民
茍安閭閻之政民之福也又何必有赫赫
punctuated:
催科政拙而被抑，豈非求治之過，而勞心撫字者反不得以聞於上耶？若此者，激勸之典雖行，而綜核之法未盡，無恠乎賢不肖之混淆也已。
我國家倣古為治，設官分職，而於守令之選為尤重。今天子臨御之初，勤恤民隱，嘉惠元元，登極一詔，首飭吏治，一時郡縣之吏爭自濯磨，喁喁嚮風矣。中間如召父杜母、循良卓異者固多，而竭澤而漁、飾實眩名以盜隆虛譽者，未敢謂盡無也。
玆欲求吏治如吳公輩，以稱皇上重本之意，豈無其道乎？夫吳公治行，載籍無所見，然史稱治平第一，帝召以為廷尉。夫文帝，好文之主，專務以德化民，躬行節儉，庶幾成康。不知其臣，其君可知也。蓋守令者，牧民者也；牧民者，勿擾之而已。吾民茍安，閭閻之政，民之福也，又何必有赫赫
translation_en:
…was held back for being inept at pressing for tax payments. Was this not an excess of zeal in seeking effective government, such that one who devoted his energies to nurturing the people instead could not gain recognition from above? In such cases, although measures to encourage and reward officials were implemented, methods of comprehensive scrutiny were not fully applied. Little wonder that the worthy and the unworthy became confused with one another.
Our dynasty models its government on antiquity, establishing offices and dividing responsibilities, and places particular weight on selecting prefects and magistrates. At the beginning of his reign, the present Son of Heaven diligently attended to the people's hidden sufferings and generously bestowed benefits on the common people. His accession edict made the rectification of local administration its first concern. Officials throughout the prefectures and counties at once competed to cleanse and improve themselves, eagerly looking toward his example. Among them there are certainly many outstanding, conscientious administrators like “Father Shao” and “Mother Du.” Yet we dare not say that there are none who drain the pond to catch its fish, embellish their actual achievements, and dazzle others with their names so as to steal an exalted but empty reputation [?].
Now, if we wish to obtain administrators like Lord Wu, in keeping with His Majesty's intention to give weight to the foundations of government, can there be no way to do so? The details of Lord Wu's administrative conduct are not to be found in the records, yet the histories call his peaceful governance the finest of all, and the emperor summoned him to serve as Chamberlain for Law Enforcement. Emperor Wen was a ruler who cherished civil culture, devoted himself to transforming the people through virtue, and personally practiced frugality, approaching the example of Kings Cheng and Kang. Though we do not know his minister, we can know his ruler. Prefects and magistrates are, after all, shepherds of the people; shepherding the people means simply refraining from disturbing them. If our people are at peace, government in their neighborhoods is a blessing to them. Why, then, must there be a dazzling…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
之聲事督責之法哉夫廷尉天下之平也
召以郡吏而豈徒哉吳公之政其務以德
化民而不欲以能自見者耶其爲天下第
一信文帝有以成之也故曰上有好者下
必有甚焉者矣其所以風勵化導之機謂
不有所在乎今之建議者必曰久任以責
其成矣夫計日而遷視如傳舍雖有黃魯
亦無由以竟其施久任之說是矣然不責
之以安養拊循之實政而徒繩之以簿書
期會之煩文吾恐卓異無以自見而賢者
亦將解體矣又曰超陟以異其寵矣夫循
資而擢以待中才豪傑之士非優異無以
表其賢超陟之說是矣然不考古課功核
實之法而徒採聽於聲譽風聞之間吾恐
君子未必見知而巧宦者反得以受其賞
矣夫淑慝無所分則相率而爲矯飾之歸
孰肯有長厚之行如是而欲守令之賢如
吳公輩者得乎誠能倣古考成之意如果
punctuated:
之聲，事督責之法哉？夫廷尉，天下之平也，召以郡吏而豈徒哉？吳公之政，其務以德化民而不欲以能自見者耶？其爲天下第一，信文帝有以成之也。故曰：「上有好者，下必有甚焉者矣。」其所以風勵化導之機，謂不有所在乎？

今之建議者必曰：「久任以責其成矣。」夫計日而遷，視如傳舍，雖有黃魯，亦無由以竟其施。久任之說是矣，然不責之以安養拊循之實政，而徒繩之以簿書期會之煩文，吾恐卓異無以自見，而賢者亦將解體矣。又曰：「超陟以異其寵矣。」夫循資而擢，以待中才；豪傑之士，非優異無以表其賢。超陟之說是矣，然不考古課功核實之法，而徒採聽於聲譽風聞之間，吾恐君子未必見知，而巧宦者反得以受其賞矣。夫淑慝無所分，則相率而爲矯飾之歸，孰肯有長厚之行？如是而欲守令之賢如吳公輩者，得乎？誠能倣古考成之意，如果
translation_en:
…a resounding reputation, or resort to methods of stringent supervision and demands for results? The Chamberlain for Law Enforcement is the arbiter of justice for all under Heaven. Could the summons appointing a commandery official to this office have been without good reason? Did Lord Wu’s administration concentrate on transforming the people through virtue, without seeking to display his own ability? That he ranked first in the empire was surely an achievement Emperor Wen helped bring about. Thus it is said: “Whatever those above favor, those below will pursue still more ardently.” Can one deny that the means of encouraging and guiding transformation have their source here?

Those who offer proposals today invariably say: “Keep officials in office for long terms and hold them accountable for results.” If officials count the days until their transfer and regard their posts as travelers’ lodgings, even men like Huang and Lu would have no way to carry their measures through. The argument for long tenure is sound. Yet if officials are not held accountable for substantive policies that nurture, comfort, and care for the people, but are merely constrained by the onerous formalities of registers, documents, and deadlines, I fear that exceptional officials will have no means to distinguish themselves, and worthy men too will lose heart. Others say: “Promote them beyond the ordinary ranks to show them special favor.” Promotion according to seniority is suitable for men of middling ability; outstanding men require special treatment if their worth is to be recognized. The argument for exceptional promotion is sound. Yet if we do not examine the ancient methods of assessing achievement and verifying actual performance, but merely gather reports of reputations and hearsay, I fear that gentlemen will not necessarily gain recognition, while those adept at maneuvering in office will instead receive the rewards. If good and bad are not distinguished, officials will follow one another into pretense and embellishment. Who will then be willing to act with generosity and integrity? Under such conditions, can we hope for prefects and magistrates as worthy as Lord Wu and his like? If we can truly emulate the intent of the ancient practice of assessing accomplishments, and if indeed…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
德澤及人烹鮮著績者則嘉奬而優待之
不責以歲月之近功則必殫心竭慮益圖
爲久安之計矣此於責成之中而寓激勸
之典如是而久任也不亦可行乎又能遵
會典所載薦舉之法如果政績彰聞賢聲茂著
者則超擢而寵異之不同以疇人之常典
則必感恩思奮益篤其報主之忱矣此於
旌異之中以寓甄感之意如是而超陟也
不亦可行乎雖然猶有說焉超擢之典不
===
可以濫施而奸貪之罰不可以姑息也夫
惟其濫施也則矯僞者日益滋固有以終
南爲捷徑者矣夫惟其姑息也則貪墨者
無所忌固有以谿壑爲歸囊者矣是故奸
貪者必嚴追奪之令如王成之僞增户口
與夫竭澤而漁者不惟罷黜之而已必律
以詐僞之罪重以追没之贓則矯僞貪墨
者無所容其奸而敦廉之行成矣超擢者
必于久任之中如陽城之政拙催科與夫
punctuated:
德澤及人、烹鮮著績者，則嘉奬而優待之，不責以歲月之近功，則必殫心竭慮，益圖爲久安之計矣。此於責成之中而寓激勸之典，如是而久任也，不亦可行乎？又能遵《會典》所載薦舉之法，如果政績彰聞、賢聲茂著者，則超擢而寵異之，不同以疇人之常典，則必感恩思奮，益篤其報主之忱矣。此於旌異之中以寓甄感之意，如是而超陟也，不亦可行乎？

雖然，猶有說焉：超擢之典不可以濫施，而奸貪之罰不可以姑息也。夫惟其濫施也，則矯僞者日益滋，固有以終南爲捷徑者矣。夫惟其姑息也，則貪墨者無所忌，固有以谿壑爲歸囊者矣。是故奸貪者必嚴追奪之令，如王成之僞增户口與夫竭澤而漁者，不惟罷黜之而已，必律以詐僞之罪，重以追没之贓，則矯僞貪墨者無所容其奸，而敦廉之行成矣。超擢者必于久任之中，如陽城之政拙催科與夫
translation_en:
…those whose beneficent governance reaches the people and whose achievements in governing—as in cooking a small fish—are evident should be commended and treated generously. If immediate results within a short span of months or years are not demanded of them, they will surely devote all their minds and energies to devising further measures for lasting peace. This incorporates encouragement into the practice of holding officials responsible for results. Would not retaining them long in office on this basis be practicable? Furthermore, the procedures for recommendation recorded in the Collected Statutes should be followed. Those whose administrative achievements are truly renowned and whose reputation for worthiness is outstanding should receive exceptional promotion and special favor, rather than be treated by the ordinary rules applicable to common men. They will surely feel gratitude and strive to exert themselves, becoming still more sincere in their desire to repay their sovereign. This incorporates the intent to distinguish and inspire [?] into the honoring of exceptional merit. Would not exceptional advancement on this basis be practicable?

Nevertheless, there is more to be said. Exceptional promotion must not be bestowed indiscriminately, nor may wrongdoing and corruption be punished leniently. Indiscriminate promotion causes pretenders to multiply daily; there will certainly be those who take Zhongnan as a shortcut to office. Leniency leaves corrupt officials without restraint; there will certainly be those who make their purses into insatiable ravines. Thus, against the unscrupulous and corrupt, orders for recovery and deprivation must be strictly enforced. Such men as Wang Cheng, who falsely inflated household and population figures, and those who drain the marsh to catch its fish must not merely be dismissed. They must be sentenced for fraud, with the additional penalty of recovering and confiscating their illicit gains. Then the deceitful and corrupt will find no scope for their villainy, and conduct marked by integrity will take shape. Those exceptionally promoted must be selected from among officials who have served long in office, such as Yang Cheng, whose administration was inept at pressing for tax payments, and those who …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
召父杜母者不惟循資而已必簡之以公
卿之職待之以不次之寵則要之以歲月
之久者實政不可以襲取而循良之風著
矣今其人之賢也一人譽之固甞超擢之
矣政績未久安保其不變乎即變而察之
則名器已濫加矣是其超也不足以勸賢
而適足以遂奸也今其人之不賢也貪墨
之行固甞黜罷之矣即褫其職滿載而歸
無所顧惜人將效尤而無忌矣是其黜也
===
不足禁暴而適足以長惡也其何以鼓舞
天下而奔走豪傑也哉欲得循良之吏如
吳公輩布列有位以成熈皡之治不亦難
乎吾故曰上之人所以風勵化導之者不
可無其具也若曰一郡一邑不足以廑
當宁之憂則非愚生之所敢知矣草茅之見惟
執事者採焉
第五問
punctuated:
召父杜母者，不惟循資而已，必簡之以公卿之職，待之以不次之寵，則要之以歲月之久者，實政不可以襲取，而循良之風著矣。今其人之賢也，一人譽之，固甞超擢之矣。政績未久，安保其不變乎？即變而察之，則名器已濫加矣。是其超也，不足以勸賢，而適足以遂奸也。今其人之不賢也，貪墨之行，固甞黜罷之矣。即褫其職，滿載而歸，無所顧惜，人將效尤而無忌矣。是其黜也，不足禁暴，而適足以長惡也。其何以鼓舞天下而奔走豪傑也哉？欲得循良之吏，如吳公輩，布列有位，以成熈皡之治，不亦難乎？吾故曰：上之人所以風勵化導之者，不可無其具也。若曰一郡一邑不足以廑當宁之憂，則非愚生之所敢知矣。草茅之見，惟執事者採焉。

第五問
translation_en:
…and those like “Father Shao” and “Mother Du,” they should not merely be advanced according to seniority. They must be selected for the offices of dukes and ministers and accorded the exceptional favor of promotion outside the regular order. When they are assessed over many years, genuine achievements in government cannot be obtained by borrowing another’s accomplishments, and a tradition of conscientious and benevolent administration will become manifest.

Nowadays, when a man is considered worthy, a single person praises him, and he has indeed sometimes been promoted beyond the regular grades. Yet his administrative achievements have not stood the test of time: how can one be sure that he will not change? Even if his change is detected, official rank and its insignia have already been bestowed indiscriminately. Such promotion does not suffice to encourage the worthy; it serves only to help the unscrupulous attain their ends. Nowadays, when a man is unworthy and has engaged in corruption, he has indeed sometimes been dismissed from office. Yet even stripped of his post, he returns home fully laden with his gains, with nothing to regret losing. Others will imitate his wrongdoing without restraint. Such dismissal does not suffice to restrain oppression; it serves only to foster evil. How can this inspire all under Heaven and move outstanding men to exert themselves?

Would it not be difficult to obtain conscientious and benevolent officials like Wu Gong, place them throughout the offices of government, and thereby achieve a reign of radiant harmony? Thus I say: those above cannot dispense with the means by which they encourage, reform, and guide officials. If it is said that a single prefecture or county does not warrant troubling the sovereign with concern, that is something this foolish student would not presume to understand. These are the views of a humble man outside official life; I ask only that you who preside consider adopting them.

Fifth Question

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批相時勢以治水方今急務
也子能條析明白可謂知要矣錄之
考試官教諭鎦批區畫詳盡
考試官教授熊批精切
善治河者固貴於相古今之時以通天下
之變尤貴於審輕重之勢以成天下之功
蓋時一也而有古今之不同其勢之趨者
爲之也不有以相之則膠於□定之迹而
天下之變於是乎不可通矣勢一也而有
===
輕重之不齊其時之會者起之也不有以
審之則惑於淆亂之言而天下之功於是
乎不可成矣故善治河者相時以施通變
之方而不泥時以病夫勢審勢以協趨時
之宜而不拂勢以執夫時如是則黃河之
變會通於一心而疏濬之役自可以成天
下之功矣執事以治河之道策諸生誠當
時之急務也顧識在俊傑愚生何足以知
之雖然黃河之源流與今日之時勢亦嘗
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：相時勢以治水，方今急務也。子能條析明白，可謂知要矣。錄之。
考試官教諭鎦批：區畫詳盡。
考試官教授熊批：精切。
善治河者，固貴於相古今之時，以通天下之變；尤貴於審輕重之勢，以成天下之功。蓋時一也，而有古今之不同，其勢之趨者爲之也。不有以相之，則膠於□定之迹，而天下之變於是乎不可通矣。勢一也，而有輕重之不齊，其時之會者起之也。不有以審之，則惑於淆亂之言，而天下之功於是乎不可成矣。故善治河者，相時以施通變之方，而不泥時以病夫勢；審勢以協趨時之宜，而不拂勢以執夫時。如是，則黃河之變會通於一心，而疏濬之役，自可以成天下之功矣。執事以治河之道策諸生，誠當時之急務也。顧識在俊傑，愚生何足以知之？雖然，黃河之源流與今日之時勢，亦嘗
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Assessing the times and circumstances in order to control the waters is an urgent task today. You have analyzed the issues clearly, point by point, and may be said to understand what is essential. Accept this essay.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The planning is detailed and comprehensive.
Comment by Examiner Xiong, Professor: Precise and pertinent.
Those skilled in managing the river certainly value assessing conditions in ancient and modern times so as to respond flexibly to changes throughout the realm. Still more, they value examining the relative importance of circumstances so as to accomplish works that benefit the realm. Time is one, yet conditions differ between antiquity and the present: the tendencies of circumstances bring this about. Without a means of assessing them, one becomes bound to established precedents [?], and can no longer respond flexibly to changes throughout the realm. Circumstances are one, yet differ in their relative importance: the conjunction of conditions at a given time gives rise to this. Without a means of examining them, one becomes bewildered by confused assertions, and can no longer accomplish works that benefit the realm. Thus, those skilled in managing the river assess the times to devise ways of adapting to change, without adhering so rigidly to the times that they impair the situation; they examine circumstances to determine the appropriate response to the times, without defying circumstances in rigid adherence to the times. In this way, the changes of the Yellow River can be comprehensively understood within a single mind, and dredging works can naturally achieve benefits for the realm. You, honored examiners, have put a policy question on river management to us students; this is indeed an urgent task of the present day. Yet such understanding belongs to men of outstanding talent. How could an ignorant student such as I know enough about it? Even so, concerning the source and course of the Yellow River and the times and circumstances of today, I have also previously…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
聞之矣請掇拾以復明問可乎粵考黃河
之源出自星宿踰崑崙九曲而入於中國
此河之所自來也禹之治河自積石鑿龍
門歷華陰下砥柱抵孟津洛汭至於大伾
廝為二渠過洚水至於大陸播為九河蓋
方大伾以下河始出峻而就平地則析之
而為二自大陸以下地平土疏水益善潰
則播之而為九故歷三代之久免衝决之
患者禹之功也此所謂相時審勢得治水
===
之道者也自周定王時河始南徙已非禹
之故道迨漢元光以後或徙東郡或决瓠
子或决館陶或分而為二或合而為一遷
徙不常而河之患於是乎日益甚是非禹
績之替也時勢之變為之也自漢以來明
智之君每廣詢而博訪宣力之臣恒竭思
以効勞是雖倡議疏治者代不乏人然河
無常處治無定策卒皆托諸空言而已若
夫賈讓當哀平之世陳上中下三策丘濬
punctuated:
聞之矣。請掇拾以復明問，可乎？粵考黃河之源，出自星宿，踰崑崙，九曲而入於中國，此河之所自來也。禹之治河，自積石，鑿龍門，歷華陰，下砥柱，抵孟津、洛汭，至於大伾，廝為二渠，過洚水，至於大陸，播為九河。蓋方大伾以下，河始出峻而就平地，則析之而為二；自大陸以下，地平土疏，水益善潰，則播之而為九。故歷三代之久，免衝决之患者，禹之功也。此所謂相時審勢，得治水之道者也。
自周定王時，河始南徙，已非禹之故道。迨漢元光以後，或徙東郡，或决瓠子，或决館陶，或分而為二，或合而為一，遷徙不常，而河之患於是乎日益甚。是非禹績之替也，時勢之變為之也。自漢以來，明智之君每廣詢而博訪，宣力之臣恒竭思以効勞。是雖倡議疏治者代不乏人，然河無常處，治無定策，卒皆托諸空言而已。若夫賈讓，當哀平之世，陳上中下三策，丘濬
translation_en:
…heard of these matters. May I gather together what I know to answer your discerning question? Examining the Yellow River’s source, we find that it rises at Xingxiu, crosses Kunlun, and enters the Central Lands through nine bends. Such is the river’s origin. In regulating the river, Yu began at Jishi, cut through Longmen, passed Huayin, descended past Dizhu, reached Mengjin and Luorui, and continued to Dapi. There he divided it into two channels, passed Jiangshui, reached Dalu, and distributed it into nine rivers. Below Dapi, the river first leaves the steep terrain and reaches level ground; he therefore divided it into two. Below Dalu, the ground is level and the soil loose, making the waters still more liable to breach their banks; he therefore distributed them into nine channels. That the people escaped the scourge of breaches throughout the long duration of the Three Dynasties was Yu’s achievement. This is what is meant by assessing the times and examining the circumstances, thereby grasping the way to regulate water.
From the time of King Ding of Zhou, the river began shifting southward and no longer followed Yu’s old course. From the Yuanguang reign period of the Han onward, it sometimes shifted into Dong Commandery, sometimes breached its banks at Huzi or Guantao, sometimes divided into two streams, and sometimes joined into one. Its course shifted unpredictably, and the disasters it caused consequently grew worse by the day. This was not a failure of Yu’s achievement: changing times and circumstances brought it about. Since the Han, wise rulers have repeatedly sought advice far and wide, while ministers exerting themselves in service have constantly devoted all their thought to the task. Thus, although no age lacked men proposing dredging and regulation, the river had no constant course and its management no settled policy; in the end, all amounted merely to empty words. As for Jia Rang, during the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping he presented three plans, ranked upper, middle, and lower. Qiu Jun…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
嘗稱其治河之法莫備於此矣夫謂增築
隄防約攔水勢使不氾濫者其法固無容
議也至於上策放河使北入海是即禹之
故智今妨運道已不可行中策據堅地作
石堤開水門分殺水勢然自漢至今千數
百年中州大名之境泥沙填委無復堅地
而河流與水門每不相值讓之策蓋就漢
之時勢論爾而今豈可以盡行乎賈魯任
河防之職言疏濬塞三法丘濬嘗稱其治
===
河之法莫要於此矣然殺河之流因而導
之之謂疏去河之淤因而深之之謂濬抑
河之暴因而扼之之謂塞是三者疏爲上
濬次之塞之法又不得已而用之爾而豈
可以一槩行乎故濬又以爲賈讓諸人皆
隨時制宜之策今日亦未必便者蓋有見
於時勢之不同耳我
國家建都上游漕會通之河輸東南之賦以
給
punctuated:
嘗稱其治河之法莫備於此矣。夫謂增築隄防，約攔水勢，使不氾濫者，其法固無容議也。至於上策放河使北入海，是即禹之故智，今妨運道，已不可行。中策據堅地作石堤，開水門，分殺水勢；然自漢至今千數百年，中州大名之境，泥沙填委，無復堅地，而河流與水門每不相值。讓之策蓋就漢之時勢論爾，而今豈可以盡行乎？賈魯任河防之職，言疏、濬、塞三法，丘濬嘗稱其治河之法莫要於此矣。然殺河之流，因而導之之謂疏；去河之淤，因而深之之謂濬；抑河之暴，因而扼之之謂塞。是三者，疏爲上，濬次之，塞之法又不得已而用之爾，而豈可以一槩行乎？故濬又以爲賈讓諸人皆隨時制宜之策，今日亦未必便者，蓋有見於時勢之不同耳。

我國家建都上游，漕會通之河，輸東南之賦，以給
translation_en:
…once declared that no methods for controlling the Yellow River were more comprehensive than these. As for the proposal to enlarge and build up embankments to contain the force of the water and prevent flooding, the method certainly admits of no objection. His highest policy, allowing the river to flow north into the sea, was precisely Yu’s ancient wisdom; today, however, it would obstruct the grain transport route and can no longer be implemented.
