His middle policy was to build stone embankments on firm ground and open sluice gates to divide and diminish the force of the water. Yet in the more than a thousand years from the Han to the present, mud and sand have accumulated throughout the territory of Daming in the Central Plain, leaving no firm ground, while the river’s course frequently fails to align with the sluice gates. Jia Rang’s policies were formulated with reference to the circumstances of the Han period. How could they all be implemented today?

When Jia Lu held responsibility for river defenses, he proposed three methods: channeling, dredging, and blocking. Qiu Jun once declared that no methods for controlling the river were more essential than these. To diminish the river’s flow and accordingly guide it is called channeling; to remove its silt and accordingly deepen it is called dredging; to restrain its violence and accordingly check it is called blocking. Of these three, channeling is best and dredging comes next; blocking is employed only when no alternative remains. How could they be applied indiscriminately? Thus Qiu Jun also held that the policies of Jia Rang and the others were all expedients adapted to their times and might not necessarily be suitable today. This was because he recognized that circumstances differ from one age to another.

Our dynasty established its capital upstream and uses the Huitong Canal for grain transport, conveying the tax grain of the southeast to supply…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
京師邇因二洪梗澁取濟黃流合於汶上諸
泉滔滔乎舟浮水面不煩牽挽之勞以濟
我
國家漕運之利誠天啓之會也比歲大雨水
溢河决於徐之飛雲浦逆流而上橫衝運
河沙淤百里中外驚惶莫知所措
先帝特勅總督大臣畢集羣策鳩工分理懼水
之東奔也而挑新河以讓其地懼水之北
徙也而築長隄以遏其衝所以相時權勢
===
而為目前濟運便民之計者誠善矣然或
者猶以為河從西北極高之地建瓴而下
以萬里轉折之勢而乗之以雨水交發百
川灌集之威而出之以秦溝一股不溢而
北徙則溢而東奔況芝蔴莊崔家壩等處
倒灣崩岸是北徙之勢方殷曹單之隄一
失則南陽魯橋一帶運河淤塞之患不免
議欲於上流別開支河以殺其勢是亦永
圖久大之謨以濟邦民之患者也執事又
punctuated:
京師。邇因二洪梗澁，取濟黃流，合於汶上諸泉，滔滔乎舟浮水面，不煩牽挽之勞，以濟我國家漕運之利，誠天啓之會也。比歲大雨水溢，河决於徐之飛雲浦，逆流而上，橫衝運河，沙淤百里，中外驚惶，莫知所措。先帝特勅總督大臣，畢集羣策，鳩工分理。懼水之東奔也，而挑新河以讓其地；懼水之北徙也，而築長隄以遏其衝。所以相時權勢，而為目前濟運便民之計者，誠善矣。
然或者猶以為，河從西北極高之地建瓴而下，以萬里轉折之勢，而乗之以雨水交發、百川灌集之威，而出之以秦溝一股，不溢而北徙，則溢而東奔。況芝蔴莊、崔家壩等處，倒灣崩岸，是北徙之勢方殷；曹單之隄一失，則南陽、魯橋一帶運河淤塞之患不免。議欲於上流別開支河，以殺其勢，是亦永圖久大之謨，以濟邦民之患者也。執事又
translation_en:
…the capital. Recently, because the two rapids had become obstructed, water from the Yellow River was drawn upon to aid navigation and joined with the waters of the various springs at Wenshang. On this abundant flow, boats floated freely without the labor of towing, thereby benefiting our dynasty’s grain transport. This was truly an opportunity opened by Heaven. In recent years, heavy rains caused the waters to overflow, and the Yellow River breached its banks at Feiyunpu in Xu. The water surged upstream and struck across the Grand Canal, silting up a hundred li. Officials at court and in the provinces were alarmed and did not know what to do. The late emperor specially commanded the grand minister serving as Supreme Commander to gather all proposals, muster workers, and divide responsibility for the works. Fearing that the water would rush eastward, they excavated a new channel to give it room; fearing that it would shift northward, they built a long embankment to check its onrush. These measures, devised by assessing the circumstances and weighing the conditions to facilitate transport and benefit the people for the present, were indeed sound.
Yet some still hold that the Yellow River plunges from the extremely high terrain of the northwest like water poured from a raised vessel. It carries the force accumulated through ten thousand li of twists and turns, augmented by the power of simultaneous rainfall and the converging waters of a hundred streams; yet it is discharged through the single channel at Qingou. Unless it overflows and shifts northward, it will overflow and rush eastward. Moreover, at Zhimazhuang, Cuijiaba, and other places, bends are giving way and banks collapsing [?], showing that the tendency to shift northward is now strong. Once the embankments at Cao and Shan fail, the Grand Canal around Nanyang and Luqiao will inevitably suffer from silting and obstruction. The proposal to open a separate branch channel upstream to diminish the river’s force is also a far-reaching plan for lasting benefit, intended to relieve the troubles of the state and its people. You, sir, further…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
謂使有濟漕之利而無衝决之患執畫一
之策而不惑於紛紛之議然事關大計非
愚生之所敢議也考之宋儒任伯雨曰河
流混濁淤沙相半久而必决者勢也安可
以人力制哉惟宜寬立隄防約攔水勢使
不至大叚漫流耳朱熹氏曰禹之治水只
是從低處下手下面之水旣殺則上面之
水必洩是故通乎任朱二君子之言而可
以知支河之不必開矣歐陽脩曰黃河已
===
棄之故道自古難復蓋河流旣久底岸皆
高水行漸壅自不能行乃棄而他徙非若
人力堵塞之河渠道猶存也呂祖謙曰禹
不惜數百里之地疏爲九河以分其勢善
治水者不與水爭地也是故通乎歐呂二
君子之言而可以知舊河之不必復矣蓋
黃河之流其東趨固一也而時不能無古
今之異其利害相對也而勢不能無輕重
之殊以今日之時言之河自孟津而下經
punctuated: 謂：「使有濟漕之利，而無衝决之患，執畫一之策，而不惑於紛紛之議。」然事關大計，非愚生之所敢議也。考之宋儒任伯雨曰：「河流混濁，淤沙相半，久而必决者，勢也。安可以人力制哉？惟宜寬立隄防，約攔水勢，使不至大叚漫流耳。」朱熹氏曰：「禹之治水，只是從低處下手，下面之水旣殺，則上面之水必洩。」是故通乎任、朱二君子之言，而可以知支河之不必開矣。歐陽脩曰：「黃河已棄之故道，自古難復。蓋河流旣久，底岸皆高，水行漸壅，自不能行，乃棄而他徙，非若人力堵塞之河，渠道猶存也。」呂祖謙曰：「禹不惜數百里之地，疏爲九河，以分其勢。善治水者，不與水爭地也。」是故通乎歐、呂二君子之言，而可以知舊河之不必復矣。蓋黃河之流，其東趨固一也，而時不能無古今之異；其利害相對也，而勢不能無輕重之殊。以今日之時言之，河自孟津而下，經
translation_en: …say: “Ensure that the river benefits grain transport without causing breaches; adhere to a consistent policy without being bewildered by conflicting proposals.” Yet this concerns a matter of great consequence, on which I, an unworthy student, dare not pronounce. Examining the words of the Song Confucian scholar Ren Boyu, we find: “The river runs turbid, with silt and sand making up half its flow. That it must eventually breach its banks follows from its inherent tendency. How could human effort control it? One should merely set the embankments far apart to contain the force of the water within broad limits, so that it does not spread unchecked over vast areas.” Zhu Xi said: “In controlling the waters, Yu simply began with the low-lying places. Once the water below has been reduced, the water above will necessarily drain away.” Thus, by grasping the words of these two gentlemen, Ren and Zhu, we can understand that there is no need to open a branch channel. Ouyang Xiu said: “Courses already abandoned by the Yellow River have, since antiquity, been difficult to restore. After the river has flowed for a long time, its bed and banks both rise, and its flow gradually becomes obstructed. Unable to proceed, it abandons its course and shifts elsewhere. This is unlike a river blocked by human effort, whose channel still remains.” Lü Zuqian said: “Yu did not begrudge several hundred li of land: he dredged nine channels to divide the force of the waters. Those skilled in controlling water do not contend with it for land.” Thus, by grasping the words of these two gentlemen, Ouyang and Lü, we can understand that there is no need to restore the old river course. For although the Yellow River’s eastward tendency remains constant, circumstances necessarily differ between ancient times and the present. Its benefits and harms stand in opposition, but their relative weight necessarily varies with conditions. Speaking of present circumstances, the river flows down from Mengjin, passing through…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
中州平坦之地迤邐而東洩於徐沛之間
大河南北悉皆故道土雜泥沙善崩易决
非若禹引水自大伾兩山極高之地而下
矣此其時之有不同也而欲效疏九河之
法將見河流細分則益緩而易淤矣而古
今可以並論耶以今日之勢言之取河水
以濟徐吕之洪而又阻其東奔以免
祖陵之害制其北决以防運道之淤况徐沛之
間復多阻山治之倍難非若禹播九河棄
===
數百里之地爲受水之區矣此其勢之有
不同也而欲圖萬全之策吾恐利之所在
害之所伏也而輕重可以弗審耶噫此當
事諸臣雖有謀國之忠長顧之慮而卒紛
紛莫之定也雖然知時勢之難而不有以
處其難不可也知治河之無上策而卒諉
之無策不可也今惟相古今之時權輕重
之勢師禹之意而不泥禹之迹如秦溝一
股果可以納大河之流也則倣禹行所無
punctuated: 中州平坦之地，迤邐而東，洩於徐沛之間。大河南北，悉皆故道，土雜泥沙，善崩易决，非若禹引水自大伾兩山極高之地而下矣。此其時之有不同也，而欲效疏九河之法，將見河流細分，則益緩而易淤矣，而古今可以並論耶？以今日之勢言之，取河水以濟徐吕之洪，而又阻其東奔，以免祖陵之害，制其北决，以防運道之淤。况徐沛之間，復多阻山，治之倍難，非若禹播九河，棄數百里之地爲受水之區矣。此其勢之有不同也，而欲圖萬全之策，吾恐利之所在，害之所伏也，而輕重可以弗審耶？噫！此當事諸臣，雖有謀國之忠、長顧之慮，而卒紛紛莫之定也。雖然，知時勢之難，而不有以處其難，不可也；知治河之無上策，而卒諉之無策，不可也。今惟相古今之時，權輕重之勢，師禹之意，而不泥禹之迹。如秦溝一股，果可以納大河之流也，則倣禹行所無
translation_en:
…through the level lands of Zhongzhou, winding eastward and discharging between Xu and Pei. North and south of the Yellow River lie its former channels; the soil is mixed with mud and sand, readily collapsing and giving way to breaches. This is unlike the time when Yu led the waters down from the extremely high terrain of the two mountains at Dapi [?]. Such is the difference between the circumstances of the two periods. If we nevertheless seek to imitate his method of dredging the Nine Rivers, we shall find that dividing the river into small streams makes its flow still slower and more liable to silting. Can ancient and present conditions be discussed as though they were alike?
Considering the configuration of the river today, we draw upon its waters to supply the rapids at Xu and Lü, yet must also check its eastward rush to spare the imperial ancestral mausoleum from harm, and restrain its northward breaches to prevent the grain-transport route from silting up. Moreover, between Xu and Pei, mountains repeatedly obstruct its course, making its management doubly difficult. This is unlike Yu’s dispersal of the waters into the Nine Rivers, when he relinquished several hundred li of land as an area to receive the waters. Such is the difference in their configurations. If we seek a plan that ensures success in every respect, I fear that wherever benefit lies, harm also lurks. Can we fail to weigh their relative importance carefully?
Alas! Although the officials charged with this matter are loyal in planning for the state and thoughtful about the distant future, their deliberations have ultimately remained divided, with nothing settled. Nevertheless, it is unacceptable to recognize the difficulties of the times and circumstances without finding a way to address them; it is unacceptable to recognize that there is no ideal plan for controlling the river and finally evade responsibility by claiming that there is no plan at all. We must now examine the circumstances of past and present, weigh the relative importance of the conditions, and take Yu’s intent as our guide without clinging to the precise course of his actions. If the single branch at Qingou can indeed accommodate the flow of the Yellow River, then we should emulate Yu’s practice of proceeding where there was no…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
事之智焉疏其下流以導其自然之歸固
其長隄以防其衝决之害而又以芝蔴莊
崔家壩等處下樁捲埽以抑其北徙之勢
各於沿河南岸去淤撈沙以疏其壅塞之
患使水由地中行而不至於氾濫斯已矣
支河固不必開也如秦溝一股不能容全
河之水也則倣禹决排之法焉淺者濬之
使遂其就下之性隘者疏之使緩其湍迅
之威務使上無所激而接河濟洪之道如
===
===
故下有所納而由清達淮由淮入海之道
如故斯已矣支河亦不必開也如此則不
惟運河疏通獲轉漕之利乆役疲民獲蘇
息之休而東奔之流既阻則
陵寢無衝决之虞北徙之勢既防則曹單免墊
溺之患庶乎永賴之績可復見於
今日而三策三法之說亦會通於異世之下
矣否則徒知用古人之法而不能相古今
之宜泥一定之迹而不能權輕重之勢則
punctuated: 事之智焉，疏其下流，以導其自然之歸；固其長隄，以防其衝决之害；而又以芝蔴莊、崔家壩等處下樁捲埽，以抑其北徙之勢。各於沿河南岸去淤撈沙，以疏其壅塞之患，使水由地中行，而不至於氾濫，斯已矣。支河固不必開也。如秦溝一股不能容全河之水也，則倣禹决排之法焉：淺者濬之，使遂其就下之性；隘者疏之，使緩其湍迅之威。務使上無所激，而接河濟洪之道如故；下有所納，而由清達淮、由淮入海之道如故，斯已矣。支河亦不必開也。如此，則不惟運河疏通，獲轉漕之利，乆役疲民獲蘇息之休，而東奔之流既阻，則陵寢無衝决之虞；北徙之勢既防，則曹單免墊溺之患。庶乎永賴之績可復見於今日，而三策三法之說亦會通於異世之下矣。否則，徒知用古人之法，而不能相古今之宜；泥一定之迹，而不能權輕重之勢，則
translation_en:
…the wisdom of accomplishing his work without forcing matters. Dredge the lower reaches to guide the water toward its natural destination; strengthen the long embankment to prevent damage from surging water and breaches; and drive piles and lay rolled brushwood fascines at Zhimazhuang, Cuijiaba, and other places to restrain its tendency to shift northward. Remove silt and dredge sand at the various points along the river’s southern bank to relieve obstructions, so that the water flows within its channel without overflowing. That is all that is required; there is certainly no need to open a branch channel. If the single channel at Qingou cannot accommodate the whole river’s waters, then follow Yu’s method of opening passages and draining the water: dredge shallow places so that the water can follow its natural tendency to flow downward, and widen narrow places to moderate the force of its rushing torrents. Ensure that upstream the flow meets no obstruction that makes it surge, and that the route connecting with the river and supplying the rapids [?] remains as before; downstream, ensure that there is an outlet to receive the water, and that the route through the Qing River to the Huai River, and through the Huai to the sea, remains as before. That is all that is required; here too there is no need to open a branch channel.
If this is done, the Grand Canal will be cleared, securing the benefits of grain transport, and the people exhausted by prolonged labor service will gain respite and recovery. Moreover, once the eastward-rushing flow has been checked, the imperial mausoleums will face no danger from surging water and breaches; once the tendency to shift northward has been restrained, Cao and Shan will escape the calamity of inundation. We may then hope to see once again, in our own day, achievements upon which people can depend enduringly, while the doctrines of the three policies and the three methods may likewise be reconciled and applied in a different age. Otherwise, if one knows only how to employ the methods of the ancients but cannot assess what suits ancient and present circumstances, and clings to a fixed precedent but cannot weigh the relative importance of the conditions, then…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
膠柱鼓瑟徒勞而罔功也烏足以語通天
下之變而成天下之功耶語曰以馬爲御
者不盡馬之情以古制今者不盡事之變
其此之謂歟書生之見如此而已惟執事
進而敎之幸甚
punctuated: 膠柱鼓瑟，徒勞而罔功也，烏足以語通天下之變而成天下之功耶？語曰：「以馬爲御者，不盡馬之情；以古制今者，不盡事之變。」其此之謂歟？書生之見如此而已，惟執事進而敎之，幸甚。
translation_en: …it would be like playing a zither with its bridges glued fast: labor expended to no avail. How could this qualify as comprehending the changes of all under Heaven and accomplishing the work of all under Heaven? As the saying goes, “Those who drive horses by taking the horse alone as their guide do not fully grasp the horse’s nature; those who govern the present by antiquity do not fully grasp how circumstances change.” Is this not precisely what it means? Such, and no more, are this scholar’s views. I would count it a great favor if you, honored officials, would offer further instruction.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
隆慶丁卯河南鄉試監臨御
史督諸執事業有成勞矣行
將進多士歌鹿鳴而賓興之
也濂不佞濫佐校文之選當
敘諸末簡廼申之曰濂聞徵
物於聚徵士於儔物聚則良
===
士儔則應古今之大較也余
觀於洛而嘆河嶽孕靈厥稱
區奧宏朗彪炳湛泓渟淵其
襃然淺之人者固以類聚而
漸漬於俗久矣即質行純駁
間以世殊總厥誕畀孰非明
智之期而天民之秀哉余所
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

隆慶丁卯，河南鄉試監臨御史督諸執事，業有成勞矣，行將進多士，歌《鹿鳴》而賓興之也。濂不佞，濫佐校文之選，當敘諸末簡，廼申之曰：濂聞，徵物於聚，徵士於儔；物聚則良，士儔則應，古今之大較也。余觀於洛而嘆：河嶽孕靈，厥稱區奧。宏朗彪炳，湛泓渟淵，其襃然淺之人者，固以類聚而漸漬於俗久矣。即質行純駁，間以世殊，總厥誕畀，孰非明智之期，而天民之秀哉？余所
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the dingmao year of Longqing [1567], the censor serving as Supervising Official for the Henan Provincial Examination directed the various officers and has already brought their labors to fruition. He is about to advance the assembled scholars, have “The Deer Call” sung, and honor them as guests as they are recommended for advancement. I, Lian, though unworthy, have undeservedly been chosen to assist in assessing their compositions. It falls to me to write an afterword on the concluding leaves, and I therefore offer these further remarks:

I have heard that things are appraised by their groupings, and scholars by their fellows. When things gather, their excellence becomes apparent; when scholars associate, they respond to one another. This is the general rule, past and present. Observing the Luo region, I marvel: the rivers and mountains engender spiritual potency, and the region is indeed a secluded treasury of it. Broad and luminous, splendid and brilliant, deep and still as a pool—those people described here as “expansive and shallow” [?] have long gathered with their own kind and been steeped in its customs. Even though the purity or admixture of their character and conduct sometimes differs with the age, considering the abundant endowments bestowed upon them, who among them does not hold the promise of intelligence and wisdom and rank among the finest of Heaven’s people? Those whom I…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
覩記如摯甫翊祚殷周秦冉
曹卹原憲司馬牛顓孫師漆
雕開之稱聖門高弟尚已及
周道闕而横議興學術流爲
老聃莊周列禦寇韓公子非
之倫各以其說爲百氏宗而
降自漢魏潤飾以文辭則招
===
客梁園論才鄴下競雕龍而
工藻績者學士且靡然騖焉
蓋至有宋理學大明諸儒輩
出倡自二程夫子而謝上蔡
吕侍講尹處士羣起和之又
何其斌斌也因斯以言洛豈
儉士哉夫挹水於河鑽火於
punctuated: 覩記，如摯甫翊祚殷周，秦冉、曹卹、原憲、司馬牛、顓孫師、漆雕開之稱聖門高弟，尚已。及周道闕而横議興，學術流爲老聃、莊周、列禦寇、韓公子非之倫，各以其說爲百氏宗。而降自漢魏，潤飾以文辭，則招客梁園，論才鄴下，競雕龍而工藻績者，學士且靡然騖焉。蓋至有宋，理學大明，諸儒輩出，倡自二程夫子，而謝上蔡、吕侍講、尹處士羣起和之，又何其斌斌也！因斯以言，洛豈儉士哉？夫挹水於河，鑽火於
translation_en:
…those I have seen recorded include Zhi and Fu, who assisted the royal houses of Yin and Zhou, and Qin Ran, Cao Xu, Yuan Xian, Sima Niu, Zhuansun Shi, and Qidiao Kai, who were renowned as eminent disciples in the Sage’s school. These belong to the distant past. When the Way of Zhou declined and contentious doctrines arose, learning branched into the teachings of such men as Lao Dan, Zhuang Zhou, Lie Yukou, and Fei, a prince of Han. Each made his doctrine a guiding authority for the hundred schools. Later, from the Han and Wei onward, learning was embellished with literary expression: guests were summoned to the Liang Garden, and literary talent was discussed at Ye. Scholars eagerly followed those who vied in “carving dragons” and excelled in weaving ornate compositions.

By the Song, the Learning of Principle shone brightly, and Confucian scholars appeared in succession. The two Masters Cheng initiated its teaching, and Xie of Shangcai, Expositor Lü, and the retired scholar Yin arose together to respond. How richly cultivated they were! Judging from this, could Luo possibly be deficient in scholars? Now, to draw water from the Yellow River and kindle fire by drilling into…

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
燧求楩柟桐梓於豫章鄧林
之野誠貴其聚也洛其士之
豫章鄧林耶何產之良也
國家稽令甲申
典制張賢羅蓋已跡至韓魏陳
衞之墟亦惟士是急今所羣
而校之者且得眝眡燭照磨
===
瑕吹疵衡計錙銖量程票繺
計所入彀十不一讎可謂精
矣匪徵於聚其誰應之爾多
士起屈蠖而附
飛龍昭明盛之上瑞颸至雲蒸旁
午殷湊皆是其選也倘亦有
如摯甫之儔出而名世者乎
punctuated:
燧，求楩柟桐梓於豫章鄧林之野，誠貴其聚也。洛其士之豫章鄧林耶？何產之良也！

國家稽令甲，申典制，張賢羅，蓋已跡至韓魏陳衞之墟，亦惟士是急。今所羣而校之者，且得眝眡燭照，磨瑕吹疵，衡計錙銖，量程票繺。計所入彀，十不一讎，可謂精矣。匪徵於聚，其誰應之？爾多士起屈蠖而附飛龍，昭明盛之上瑞，颸至雲蒸，旁午殷湊，皆是其選也。倘亦有如摯甫之儔，出而名世者乎？
translation_en:
…a fire drill, or seeking pian, nan, tong, and zi timber trees in the wilds of Yuzhang and Denglin: what truly matters is their concentration there. Is Luo the Yuzhang and Denglin of scholars? How excellent are those it produces!

The state consults its statutes, reaffirms its established institutions, and spreads its net for worthy men. Its search has already reached the former territories of Han, Wei, Chen, and Wei 衞, with securing scholars its urgent concern. Those now assembled for comparative examination can be closely scrutinized and brightly illuminated, their flaws polished away and their blemishes sought out, their worth weighed down to the smallest fractions, and their measure assessed [?]. Reckoning those who enter the target range of selection, not one in ten qualifies: the selection may indeed be called exacting. Unless candidates were summoned from a place where talent gathers, who could answer the call? You many scholars emerge like inchworms from your contracted state and attach yourselves to the flying dragon—the sovereign—manifesting an auspicious sign of the highest order for this enlightened and flourishing age. Arriving like a cool wind and gathering like rising clouds, converging from every direction in great numbers, you are all its chosen men. Might there also be among you someone like Zhi Fu, who will emerge and win renown in his age?

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
余甚欲觀之夫海內學術純
一號章縫者類能褒刺王霸
摽剝儒墨以明趨舍吾知其
必爲聖人之徒而不惑於百
家之指章矣所懼者有司方
程士以藝而士匪藝亦莫由
介紹而謁之有司此其趨容
===
不無摭華病實寖以文敝而
與梁園鄴下之風罔裨世敎
者同轍乎
國家得士將翼爲亮采是資俇
施名實如以藝而已矣辟石
田安所用之且以有宋諸賢
陸沈獻納之司研覈異同之
punctuated:
余甚欲觀之。夫海內學術純一，號章縫者類能褒刺王霸，摽剝儒墨，以明趨舍。吾知其必爲聖人之徒，而不惑於百家之指章矣。所懼者，有司方程士以藝，而士匪藝亦莫由介紹而謁之有司。此其趨容，不無摭華病實，寖以文敝，而與梁園鄴下之風罔裨世敎者同轍乎？
國家得士，將翼爲亮采，是資俇施名實。如以藝而已矣，辟石田，安所用之？且以有宋諸賢，陸沈獻納之司，研覈異同之
translation_en:
I very much wish to see such men. Throughout the realm, learning is uniform and undivided. Those who style themselves wearers of the scholar’s cap can generally praise and censure the ways of true kings and hegemons, distinguish Confucian from Mohist teachings [?], and thereby make clear what to pursue and what to reject. I know that they must be followers of the sages, unconfused by the purport of the hundred schools. What concerns me is that the authorities now assess scholars by their literary accomplishments, while scholars, without such accomplishments, have no means of securing an introduction and presenting themselves to the authorities. In their conduct, might they not pluck the flowers while harming the fruit, gradually becoming corrupted by literary ornament, and following the same course as the literary fashions of Liangyuan and Yexia, which contributed nothing to the moral instruction of the age?
When the state obtains scholars, it expects them to assist in carrying out its affairs; it relies upon them to put their abilities into practice, with reputation matched by substance [?]. If literary accomplishment alone were enough, they would be like a stony field: what use could be made of them? Moreover, consider the worthy men of the Song, who languished in obscurity in offices charged with presenting counsel, investigating and scrutinizing points of agreement and difference …

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
辨於力勤矣猶或詆之議論
滋多而寡成事然自今觀之
直諸賢之不遇時也爾多士
於時遇矣其何以志古之道
而自鏡乎夫物有同聚而殊
品士有同類而殊能者在審
處之一决也爾多士勗哉其
===
無負於洛產之良矣
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教
諭鎦鐮謹序
punctuated:
辨，於力勤矣，猶或詆之議論滋多而寡成事。然自今觀之，直諸賢之不遇時也。爾多士於時遇矣，其何以志古之道而自鏡乎？夫物有同聚而殊品，士有同類而殊能者，在審處之一决也。爾多士勗哉，其無負於洛產之良矣！
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教諭鎦鐮謹序。
translation_en:
…in distinguishing among them, they labored diligently; yet some still disparaged them for multiplying discussions while accomplishing little. Viewed from today, however, it was simply that those worthies had not encountered a favorable age. You scholars have encountered such an age. How, then, will you set your minds on the Way of antiquity and take it as a mirror for yourselves? Things may be gathered together yet differ in quality; scholars may belong to the same category yet differ in ability. It rests upon a single judicious determination of how to place them. Exert yourselves, you scholars! Do not fall short of the excellence of the men produced by Luo!
Preface respectfully written by Liu Lian 鎦鐮, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wuyi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 隆慶元年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣光祖於其錄之成也特舉
以申告云
直隸揚州府江都縣儒學教
諭蔡光祖謹序
punctuated:
矣。光祖於其錄之成也，特舉以申告云。
直隸揚州府江都縣儒學教諭蔡光祖謹序。
translation_en:
… Upon completion of this record, I, Guangzu, have specially raised these matters to reiterate my admonition.
This preface is respectfully composed by Cai Guangzu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered territory.
